title: Phase-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the Vela pulsar with NICER observations
abstract: PSR J0835-4510 (the Vela pulsar) is the best studied pulsar in the southern hemisphere given its high radio brightness and large glitch activity. However, its X-ray brightness is lower, making the study of its X-ray profile difficult. We aim to investigate the X-ray emission of the Vela pulsar coming from the surface of the neutron star to infer the properties of its hotspots and assess whether they share a common spectral shape. We also aim to prove whether the 2021 glitch affected the hotspots. We used an ephemeris obtained from high-cadence radio observations with the radio telescopes of the Argentine Institute of Radio Astronomy to combine all the observations of the Vela pulsar after its 2019 glitch and before its 2024 glitch. We obtained a folded pulse profile for three different energy ranges and subsequently studied their phase-resolved energy spectra. We additionally analyzed a observation to quantify the pulsar's contribution to the total soft X-ray emission detected by , which cannot spatially resolve the pulsar from the surrounding pulsar wind nebula (PWN). NICER Chandra NICER The pulsar contribution to the total observed emission represents less than 40–45% of the flux below 0.9 keV, dropping to 3–4% in the 0.9--2.0 keV range and further down to ∼2% above 2 keV, where the PWN fully dominates. We find that the X-ray folded profile of the Vela pulsar was not measurably perturbed by the 2021 glitch. We studied seven regions of the pulse profile separately. We found that all of them are well modeled by one or two blackbodies. title: Neutron star-companion interaction in core-collapse supernovae. Population synthesis based on detailed binary evolution models
abstract: Most massive stars live in binary systems. When the first supernova in a binary occurs, the ejecta hit the companion, which may inflate as a consequence, and then interact with the newly formed compact object. The recent Type Ic supernova shows a periodic modulation in its emission, which is interpreted as evidence of such interaction. 2022jli We derive predictions for the occurrence rate and observables of supernovae exhibiting these compact object--companion interactions (CCIs). We analyzed a comprehensive state-of-the-art grid of detailed binary stellar evolution models and implemented analytic prescriptions for the expansion of the companion star following its interaction with the supernova ejecta. We then employed the newly developed population synthesis code to derive the distribution functions of the properties of the supernovae affected by CCI and their companions, where we used different explodability and neutron star birth-kick distributions. SN-ORACLE We find that periodic CCI is expected to occur in more than half of the binary systems that produce a hydrogen-poor core-collapse supernova and are not disrupted, while the occurrence rate in systems producing hydrogen-rich supernovae is small. We found broad period ranges, peaking around 20-50 with the interaction lasting for 0.5-10 , , and . The inflation of the companion also increases their luminosity and brightness, increasing their detectability with current instruments. For , our best-fitting models predict a J-band magnitude of 21-23 for up to sim10 We identified specific binary evolution models that reproduce the observed period of the light curve undulations of 2022jli 2015ap 2022esa 2022jli We find that up to sim27% of H-poor supernovae could show periodicity in their light curves, while only a few such events have been identified so far. Our results may help identify periodic CCI features in future and archival supernova observations.

title: Contributions of massive stars and classical novae to Galactic Al 26
abstract: The radioactive isotope is believed to be mainly produced by massive stars and ejected into the interstellar medium through their winds and supernovae. Due to its lifetime of 1.04,Myr, it traces recent nucleosynthesis and star formation. The isotope Al 26 Fe 60 is similarly long-lived, with a lifetime of 3.8,Myr, and originates only in core-collapse supernovae (ccSNe). Stellar evolution models in combination with Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) models tend to over-predict the nuc Fe 60 / ratio. Population synthesis models that attempt to explain both the mass in the entire Milky Way and its spatial distribution through comparisons with the 1.8,MeV decay γ-ray line match the observational constraints only with an enhanced star formation rate (SFR) of ≳ 5, . Classical novae may contribute significantly to the production, potentially lowering the SFR inferred from massive stars, although previous studies suggest that their contribution is negligible or łeq,10%. However, a large nova contribution would also alleviate some tension in the Al 26 Al 26 -1 Al 26 Fe 60 / ratio. Al 26 In this work we aim to determine the mass distribution of as a function of the Galactocentric radius and estimate the contribution of (very) massive stars and classical novae to the 1.8 ,MeV signal. Al 26 We used 20,yr of INTEGRAL/SPI observations of the γ-ray line at 1.8, and compare the resulting mass distribution with different GCE models. to test different assumptions about the radial structure of Al 26 In our baseline analysis, all tested source models favour substantial nova contributions, with best-fit fractions of 77--84%. Because the nova and massive-star amplitudes are anti-correlated, the full two-parameter 2σ confidence regions permit substantially smaller nova fractions. The preferred large nova contribution alleviates tension in the / ratio and lowers the SFR from γ-ray measurements to 1--2, .
