title: Search for Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background in the Full KamLAND Dataset with Neural-network-based Event Classification
abstract: Abstract We report a search for the diffuse supernova neutrino background (DSNB) with the KamLAND detector, targeting electron antineutrinos ( ν ¯ e ) via inverse beta decay in the neutrino energy range of 8.3–30.8 MeV. Using an exposure of 9.02 kton-yr (8.3–9.3 MeV) and 9.42 kton-yr (9.3–30.8 MeV) with a liquid scintillator, we observe seven candidate events after applying a new deep-neural-network-based event classification technique. This is consistent with the background-only expectation of 16.2 ± 9.4 events, which includes systematic uncertainties associated with the neural-network selection. A spectral analysis of the energy and radial distributions finds no significant excess attributable to the DSNB. We therefore set 90% confidence-level upper limits on the DSNB flux of 38–43 cm −2 s −1 , depending on the assumed DSNB model. We also derive model-independent 90% confidence-level upper limits on the ν ¯ e flux, which are among the most stringent constraints below 13.3 MeV. Beyond the DSNB search itself, this work establishes neural-network-based event classification as a promising approach for suppressing neutron-associated backgrounds in liquid-scintillator neutrino detectors. The improved sensitivity also enables an astrophysical interpretation of the average neutrino emission from core-collapse supernovae and highlights the complementary role of low-threshold liquid-scintillator detectors in future DSNB searches.

title: Bag Parameters for Heavy Meson Lifetimes from a Lattice QCD Calculation at the SU ( 3 ) F -symmetric Point
abstract: We calculate the dimension-six Δ Q = 0 four-quark matrix elements describing heavy-meson lifetime ratios using the gradient flow with its short flow-time expansion (SFTX) as a renormalization procedure. On six RBC/UKQCD 2 + 1 -flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we determine flowed bag parameters for physical charm and strange quarks and match to the MS ¯ scheme with perturbative SFTX coefficients through next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). A multiscale matching procedure using renormalization-group running improves the extrapolation to zero flow time. For the operators relevant to τ ( D s ) / τ ( D 0 ) at the SU ( 3 ) F symmetric point, we obtain B 1 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = 1.0524 ( 97 ) , B 2 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = 0.9621 ( 70 ) , ε 1 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = − 0.2275 ( 76 ) , and ε 2 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = − 0.0005 ( 8 ) using a specific choice of evanescent operators. This is the first lattice-QCD determination of Δ Q = 0 four-quark operators with a full error budget. It opens the path toward higher-precision predictions of heavy-meson lifetimes and similar quantities exhibiting operator mixing under renormalization.

title: Theoretical Study of i -process Contribution to the Post-AGB Star IRAS 14325-6428
abstract: Abstract The post-asymptotic giant branch (post-AGB) star IRAS 14325-6428 exhibits a peculiar heavy-element abundance pattern, characterized by a high [Ba/La] ratio and an anomalous odd-isotope Ba ratio ( f odd,Ba = 0.25 ± 0.08), which is difficult to explain via the classical slow neutron-capture process ( s -process). We theoretically investigate this abundance pattern by considering the intermediate neutron-capture process ( i -process) nucleosynthesis. The i -process nucleosynthesis calculations are performed with a one-zone network (NucNet Tools) at constant temperature and density, using intershell abundances obtained from a stellar model (1.5 M ⊙ , Z = 0.003) evolved with MESA to the thermally pulsing AGB phase. The observed heavy-element abundances are best reproduced by a model with neutron density N n = 5 × 10 13 cm −3 and neutron exposure τ = 1.4 mbarn −1 , followed by dilution with a scaled-solar composition. This model reproduces the high [Ba/La] and [Ba/Ce] ratios and yields a postdilution odd-isotope fraction f odd,Ba ≈ 0.51, which is supported by the observed value being substantially above the expectations of the pure s -process. The abundance pattern arises from the i -process path approaching the neutron magic number N = 82, where the flow slows, and the material accumulates at 135 I, which subsequently β − decays to 135 Ba, enhancing Ba production and reducing the synthesis of heavier species. Combined with its multielement i -process classification, our results provide quantitative support for a dominant i -process origin of the heavy elements in IRAS 14325−6428, likely triggered by a relatively short-lived proton-ingestion episode in its AGB progenitor.

title: Ab initio calculations of Th 229 band-to-band internal conversion rate in ThO 2 229
abstract: We present an ab initio calculation of the band-to-band internal-conversion rate of the $\hbar\omega_{\rm nuc} \approx 8.35$ eV isomeric transition in $^{229}$ThO$_2$. Because the nuclear transition energy exceeds the electronic band gap of ThO$_2$, the isomer can decay nonradiatively by resonantly promoting a valence electron into the conduction band. We formulate this process as a Brillouin-zone sum over vertical interband transitions weighted by local Th-centered hyperfine matrix elements, which are evaluated directly from all-electron full-potential linearized augmented-plane-wave Bloch spinors. A finite nuclear magnetization model is included to regularize the short-range hyperfine interaction and to account for the Bohr-Weisskopf effect. After applying scissor shifts to span the experimentally reported ThO$_2$ band gaps, we find calculated internal-conversion lifetimes in the range of $1-16~\mu{\rm s}$. The lifetime increases strongly as the band gap approaches $\omega_{\rm nuc}$ because the resonant interband phase space at the nuclear transition energy is reduced. For the larger reported ThO$_2$ gaps, the calculated lifetime is comparable to the measured conversion-electron M\"ossbauer lifetime [Nature 648, 300 (2025)]. Our analysis implies that choosing solid-state hosts with band-gap values slightly lower than $\omega_{\rm nuc}$ can optimize solid-state nuclear clock performance with internal-conversion electron readout.

title: Strong-gain water-window X-ray laser driven by plasma photocathode wakefield acceleration
abstract: Abstract X-ray free-electron lasers are large and complex machines, limited by electron beam brightness. Here we show through start-to-end simulations how to realise compact, robust and tunable X-ray lasers in the water window, based on ultra-bright electron beams from plasma wakefield accelerators. First, an ultra-low-emittance electron beam is released by a plasma photocathode in a metre-scale plasma wakefield accelerator. By tuning the beam charge, space-charge forces create a balance between beam fields and wakefields that reduces beam energy spread and improves energy stability – both critical for beam extraction, transport, and focusing into a metre-scale undulator. Here, the resulting ultra-bright beams produce wavelength-tunable, coherent, femtosecond-scale photon pulses at strong gain. This regime enables reliable generation of multi-gigawatt-class X-ray laser pulses across the water window, offering tunability via the witness beam charge and robustness against variations in plasma wakefield strength and plasma photocathode laser jitter. Our findings help democratise access to coherent, high-power, soft X-ray radiation.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Adapting the barrier distribution and synthesizing superheavy nuclei through 50 Ti- and 54 Cr-induced fusion reactions
Heavy Quark Transport Is Non-Gaussian beyond Leading Logarithm
abstract: We find that heavy quark transport beyond leading logarithm at weak coupling is intrinsically non-Gaussian: the longitudinal momentum transfer distribution has that are crucial for equilibration dynamics. We show this by computing the leading-order momentum transfer kernel for relativistic heavy quarks in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas, matching perturbative momentum transfer on the thermal scale to hard-thermal-loop-resummed soft physics. This is the same structure previously found in strongly coupled holographic plasmas, showing that it is not peculiar to weak or strong coupling, conformality, or supersymmetry. We therefore expect that this is a robust feature that physical quark-gluon plasma should also exhibit.

title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades—or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Study of the shape coexistence in the 96 Zr, 96 Mo, 96 Ru isobars
abstract: Abstract Three stable isobars, 96 40 Zr 56 , 96 42 Mo 54 and 96 44 Ru 52 , which are in the vicinity of the harmonic oscillator proton shell closure Z = 40 and the spin-orbit neutron shell closure N = 50, are investigated for the presence of the shape coexistence and mixing phenomena. The ground state deformation of these isobars is extracted from the potential energy surface determined with the covariant density functional theory using a density-dependent point-coupling interaction, while the excited states are described involving the Bohr-Mottelson Hamiltonian with octic potential for both axially symmetric and γ-unstable quadrupole deformations. Within the broader view of the two approaches, the obtained results clearly highlight the significant contribution of these phenomena to the structure of the states of these nuclei.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
abstract: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg \Lambda_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/\alpha_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $\alpha_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $\omega\leq \alpha_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
abstract: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.

title: Efficiency measurements of GEM GE1/1 chambers in the upgraded CMS Endcap Muon System using 2023 collision data at √( s ) = 13.6 TeV
abstract: Abstract The CMS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider employs Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) detectors, a technology based on gaseous ionization, as one of the muon detectors. The muon spectrometer is being upgraded to handle the increased muon flux in the forward region. This study analyzes muon detection efficiency in the GE1/1 triple-GEM detector, using 2023 proton-proton collision data at √( s ) = 13.6 TeV. A dataset enriched with muons from Z boson decay, with a total recorded luminosity of 17.8 fb -1 has been used for this study. The detection efficiency of 137 GEM detectors are measured using muon trajectories established using other detectors in the tracking and muon systems, without use of the GEM detectors. The average efficiency of 137 GEM detectors is ∼ 93.3%. A subset of 108 detectors that had no shorts were operated at the nominal HV working point with average efficiency of ∼ 96%. Efficiency is found to be unaffected by the number of p-p interactions per bunch crossing (pile-up).

title: Effects of in-medium $NN$ inelastic cross sections and the high-momentum tail of nucleon momentum distributions on pion production in heavy-ion collisions
abstract: Pion production in intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions (HICs) provides a sensitive probe of the nuclear equation of state and of the isospin dependence of reaction dynamics. In particular, pion production near threshold is strongly affected by the nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) inelastic cross sections and by the high-momentum components of the nucleon momentum distribution. To explore the influence of these two ingredients on pion production and charged-pion ratios, the in-medium $NN$ inelastic cross sections calculated within the relativistic Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck transport theory and the short-range correlation induced high-momentum tail (HMT) are introduced into the Ultra-relativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics model. By simulating Au+Au collisions at intermediate energies, we find that the in-medium modification of the $NN$ inelastic cross sections suppresses the pion multiplicity by reducing the probability of $N\Delta$ production in dense matter. The HMT, on the other hand, enhances the high-momentum components of nucleons and modifies the available energy in individual $NN$ collisions, thereby affecting $NN\rightarrow N\Delta$ reactions and the subsequent pion production. With the simultaneous inclusion of these two effects, the pion yields and the $\pi^-/\pi^+$ ratio data can be better reproduced. These results highlight the importance of both the in-medium reaction cross sections and short-range correlation induced high-momentum components in pion production in intermediate energy HICs.

title: Search for the 229Pa Parity Doublet via Internal-Conversion Spectroscopy at FRIB
abstract: The radioisotope $^{229}$Pa is predicted to possess a nearly degenerate ground-state parity doublet. Previous $\gamma$-ray and conversion-electron spectroscopy suggests a splitting of $\Delta E = (60\pm 50)~\mathrm{eV}$, although the doublet's existence remains unconfirmed. Such a small splitting would give $^{229}$Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of $^{229}$Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of $^{229}$Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of $^{229}$U$^{+}$ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). This measurement would provide the key nuclear-structure input needed to establish $^{229}$Pa as a leading candidate for next-generation atomic and molecular electric-dipole-moment (EDM) experiments.

title: Quasisteady flavor configuration of multienergy neutrino ensembles
abstract: Neutrino flavor conversion profoundly impacts the explosion mechanism and multi-messenger emission of core-collapse supernovae. Yet, state-of-the-art hydrodynamic simulations of neutrino-dense astrophysical environments cannot account for neutrino quantum kinetics, necessitating subgrid schemes to model the impact of neutrino self-interaction on the quasi-steady flavor configuration. We present semi-analytic approximations for the outcomes of both slow and fast flavor conversions in quasi-homogeneous systems with periodic boundary conditions. Independent of the mass ordering, our ansatz demonstrates excellent agreement with multi-angle and multi-energy solutions of the neutrino kinetic equations across a wide range of representative (anti)neutrino distributions.

title: Experimental Characterization of Bulk Micromegas for Development of Active Target Time Projection Chamber for Nuclear Astrophysics Studies
abstract: A Micromegas-based active target Time Projection Chamber, namely Saha Active Target TPC (SAT-TPC), is under development at Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics for its application in nuclear astrophysics experiment to measure the branching ratio of the direct and sequential decay of the Hoyle state of $^{12}$C. A bulk Micromegas was characterized to optimize its operating parameters and its performance for $\alpha$-particle tracking was investigated using gas mixtures Ar + CO$_{2}$ (90:10) and Ar + i-C$_4$H$_{10}$ (95:5) at atmospheric pressure using 5.9~keV X-ray and 5.48~MeV $\alpha$-particles from radioactive sources. A hydrodynamic transport model was used to simulate the charge-deposit profile of the $\alpha$-particle track on the Micromegas readout and compared to the experimental data to complement the experimental measurement as well as validate the numerical model. A good agreement was observed that confirmed the suitability of the choice of the bulk Micromegas in the development of the SAT-TPC prototype and the hydrodynamic modelling of the detector dynamics

title: Test and irradiation results of the NKF7 10.24 Gbps serializer prototype chip for ALICE ITS3
abstract: Abstract The coming ALICE Inner Tracking System (ITS) upgrade uses MAPS (Monolithic Active Pixel Sensors) with multiple integrated 10.24-Gbps transmitters. The NKF7 chip is a proto transmitter serializing a 16-bit input into a 10.24-Gbps output. Connecting NKF7 16-data inputs to an FPGA allows for the generation of arbitrary patterns. A PRBS7 pattern results (at the end of the ITS3 FPC cable) into open eyes at 5.12 Gbps (Bit Error Ratio < 10 -15 ) but closes at 10.24 Gbps (BER > 10 -9 @ V DD = 1.45 V). Reducing V DD further degrades BER and increases jitter which is also seen in chip simulations after adding GND and V DD bond wire inductance. This inductance gives on-die supply noise which will be mitigated in future chips by integrating on-die regulators. Irradiation with 32-MeV protons gives σ SEU ≈ 10 -12 cm 2 and NKF7 withstands a TID > 10 Mrad.

title: Characterizing $\pT$-differential Radial-Flow Fluctuations in Au+Au Collisions at FAIR with a Multi-Phase Transport Model
abstract: We report the first predictions of the transverse-momentum ($\pT$)-differential radial-flow fluctuation observable, $\vzpT$, in Au+Au collisions at the top SIS100 energy, $\snn=4.9$~GeV, which will be available at the FAIR accelerator complex. Radial flow and its fluctuations are studied for different centrality intervals and reference-$\pT$ selections to investigate the properties and robustness of the calculated long-range correlation. $\vzpT$ displays a characteristic evolution from negative values at low $\pT$ to positive values at higher $\pT$. The integrated $v_0$, obtained with different reference-$\pT$ intervals, follows a common trend, with an approximately inverse-square-root dependence on the inclusive charged-particle multiplicity ($\nch$). The $\vzpT$ signal changes little when the pseudorapidity gap is varied between 0.2 and 0.8, or when the edges of the reference-$\pT$ interval are varied, in the bulk region. For identified particles, the pion and proton $\vzpT$ are ordered at low $\pT$, qualitatively similar to the mass ordering seen at higher energies. However, unlike at higher collision energies, $\vzpT$ does not exhibit constituent-quark number scaling, so the results do not support an interpretation in terms of partonic collectivity. The results are also in partial contradiction with the behavior of hadronic elliptic flow in these low-energy collisions. These results provide constraints on the evolution of radial correlations toward lower collision energies and motivate comparisons with complementary observables to clarify their connection to collective dynamics.

title: New Neutron Polarizabilities from Deuterium Compton Scattering at HI$\gamma$S
abstract: Elastic and inelastic Compton-scattering cross sections of the deuteron were measured at HI$\gamma$S using a circularly polarized, quasi-monoenergetic $\gamma$-ray beam (61.0 MeV). Scattered $\gamma$ rays from a liquid deuterium target were detected at $55^\circ$, $115^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. High-resolution NaI(Tl) detectors at backward angles enabled separation of elastic and inelastic events. A $\chi$EFT analysis of the data yields new neutron scalar polarizabilities, $\alpha^n_{E1} = 12.25 \pm 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \pm 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \pm 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ and $\beta^n_{M1} = 2.95 \mp 1.1\mathrm{(stat)} \mp 0.3\mathrm{(BSR)} \mp 0.8\mathrm{(th)}$ (in units of $10^{-4} \mathrm{fm}^3$) reducing statistical uncertainties by 12 %.

title: Toward a Quantum Information Foundation for Neutron Scattering
abstract: Neutron scattering is a central probe of quantum materials, yet what quantum information can, in principle, be extracted from a scattering experiment remains unclear. Here we formulate neutron scattering as a quantum measurement, with the scattering amplitudes acting as Kraus operators on the material state. This provides a unified description of conventional intensity, coherent scattering, interferometric measurements, and entanglement witnesses, including those based on quantum Fisher information. We then ask how far this connection can be extended to nonlinear properties of a quantum state. For two independently prepared samples, we derive the general structure of probe-mediated measurement probabilities and show that, for spin-projection-conserving dynamics, low-order scattering cannot resolve certain many-body coherences required to determine purity. Conversely, an idealized single-spin protocol shows how probe-mediated exchange can access purity when the appropriate two-copy operation is realized. Our results establish a quantum-information description of neutron scattering and delineate the information accessible through conventional and interferometric measurements.

title: The compact gas-dynamic ion-beam extractor/buncher module for the cryogenic stopping cells at FAIR
abstract: Abstract The original compact gas-dynamic ion-beam extractor/buncher module is proposed here as a new instrument for low-energy ion-beam manipulation. In order to enhance the quality of pulsed cold ion beams extracted from the two cryogenic stopping cells at FAIR (i.e., the one currently used in the FRS and the one under development for the Super-FRS at FAIR), it is hereby proposed that this module be utilised as a substitute for the extensively employed linear radiofrequency quadrupole (RFQ) technique. The proposed apparatus facilitates the extraction and fast bunching of approximately 100% ions into a vacuum by means of a short stack of thin cylindrical electrodes positioned on the axis behind the extraction RF carpet nozzle. The implementation of the proposal will enable the achievement of low emittance values for short-pulsed ion beams in a wide mass range, as demonstrated by detailed gas-dynamic and ion trajectory Monte Carlo simulations. The results of these simulations are presented and discussed.

title: Interacting Boson System at Finite Temperatures: The treatment of the lattice QCD results
abstract: We study an interacting relativistic system of charged bosons at finite temperature and fixed isospin density within a thermodynamically consistent mean-field approach. The interaction is represented by repulsive phi-4 and phi-6 self-interactions, which generate a density-dependent effective mass of the bosonic quasiparticles. We formulate the thermodynamics in the Extended Canonical Ensemble, obtained from the grand canonical description by a Legendre transformation from the isospin chemical potential to the conserved isospin density. In the condensed phase the chemical potential is constrained by the Bose-condensation condition and is therefore determined self-consistently through the effective mass. We apply the formalism to a pion-like system at finite isospin and clarify the relation between the isospin chemical-potential conventions used for pion and quark degrees of freedom. Using the convention adopted in lattice-QCD calculations, we compare the pressure, isospin density, energy density, and trace anomaly with lattice results at T=120 MeV. With one constant fitted to the lattice pressure, each model reproduces the lattice isospin density, energy density, and trace anomaly. Both the phi-4 and phi-6 models reproduce the main features of the lattice data, with the phi-6 interaction providing the better description. The Extended Canonical Ensemble provides a convenient framework for treating interacting particle-antiparticle systems across the transition to the Bose-condensed phase.

title: From lattice QCD thermodynamics to an effective quasiparticle description of gluonic matter at finite temperature
abstract: We develop a lattice-constrained quasiparticle description of pure SU(3) Yang--Mills matter at finite temperature. The temperature-dependent effective gluon quasiparticle mass is determined from the lattice entropy density over $0.70\leq T/T_c\leq5$. It is interpreted as an effective thermal parameter encoding medium modifications of gluonic excitations, rather than as a physical gluon mass. With this mass fixed, we reconstruct the background contribution required for thermodynamic consistency, using a single pressure-normalization condition. The resulting pressure, energy density, entropy density, interaction measure, and squared speed of sound are then compared with available lattice results. Near $T_c$, the rapid variation of the effective mass is accompanied by a pronounced maximum in the interaction measure at $T/T_c\simeq1.09$, a strong suppression of the squared speed of sound, and a maximum in the background contribution. These correlated features characterize the substantial departure from conformal behavior in the transition region. At higher temperatures, the interaction measure decreases and the squared speed of sound approaches the conformal limit. We also examine the energy-per-excitation ratio $E/n_g$, which has a minimum of approximately $964~\mathrm{MeV}$ at $T/T_c\simeq1.21$. This ratio provides a measure of the excitation scale within the quasiparticle description. Overall, our results show how lattice thermodynamics can be mapped onto an effective gluonic excitation spectrum while maintaining thermodynamic consistency.

title: Development of a positron imaging unit for advanced plant research
abstract: Abstract Positron-emitting tracer imaging systems (PETIS) apply the principles of positron emission tomography to plant research, enabling non-destructive, real-time visualization of substance distribution in living plants. However, the conventional PETIS instruments using bismuth germanate (BGO) scintillator arrays and position-sensitive photomultiplier tubes have limited spatial resolution 1.6–2.1 mm full width at half maximum (FWHM), and the relatively long decay time of BGO restricts the coincidence timing resolution (CTR) and count-rate performance. In addition, the thickness of the scintillator array can introduce parallax errors due to depth-of-interaction ambiguity. To enable submillimeter-scale imaging of fine structures like leaf veins, we developed a compact, high-resolution prototype PETIS unit tailored for thin plant organs. The prototype features two face-to-face detector modules separated by 2 cm. Each module consists of a finely segmented cerium-doped gadolinium aluminium gallium garnet scintillator array (1 × 1 × 1 and 1.5 × 1.5 × 1 mm 3 crystals), a 1-mm light guide, an 8 × 8 silicon photomultiplier array, and a TOFPET2 application-specific integrated circuit. The 1-mm-thick scintillator design drastically reduces depth-of-interaction parallax errors while optimizing count-rate capability. The performance was evaluated using a 22 Na point source. The system achieved 511 keV energy resolutions of 11–13 % FWHM. Reconstructed images demonstrated spatial resolutions of 1.1–1.2 mm FWHM, significantly outperforming the conventional PETIS instruments. The CTR reached 773 ± 16 ps with an effective coincidence detection efficiency of 6.54 × 10 -5 . These fundamental performance results demonstrate the strong potential of the compact unit for localized, high-resolution plant transport studies.

title: Development and characterization of a wingless ICPC HPGe detector with thin amorphous-Ge contacts
abstract: Abstract High-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors with thin amorphous-germanium (a-Ge) contacts can provide bipolar charge blocking and surface passivation while minimizing contact-related inactive thickness. We report the fabrication and characterization of a p-type inverted coaxial point-contact (ICPC) HPGe detector using thin a-Ge contacts in a wingless geometry that avoids the protective wing structure used in our previous prototype. The detector was fabricated from a USD-grown, zone-refined HPGe crystal and has a mass of 20.0 g. With the temperature controller set to 77 K, the detector exhibited picoampere-scale leakage current and an operational depletion voltage of approximately 440 V. A representative monitored temperature of approximately 76.3 K was recorded during detector characterization. Gamma-ray spectroscopy yielded energy resolutions of 1.8 keV FWHM at 59.5 keV and 3.2 keV FWHM at 662 keV. The calibrated charge-injection method gave a pulser-derived effective capacitance of 0.496 pF, compared with the simulated intrinsic detector capacitance of 0.488 pF obtained using SolidStateDetectors.jl . With a 241 Am source positioned inside the detector bore, the detector showed a source-correlated excess current and a broad degraded-alpha continuum centered near 3558 keV, demonstrating sensitivity to near-surface interactions. Because the source encapsulation, intervening materials, and near-surface charge-collection response were not independently characterized, the continuum is not used to infer a unique dead-layer thickness or energy-loss mechanism. The principal result is successful fabrication and stable sub-pF operation of a 20-g wingless thin-contact ICPC prototype.

title: Large Offsets of Double-neutron-star Mergers: Degeneracies and Implications for Host Associations
abstract: Abstract The projected offset of a gamma-ray burst (GRB) from its host galaxy is an important diagnostic of its physical origin, where the host associations are usually evaluated through chance-coincidence probabilities. However, as shown by observations, the host associations given by this approach may be ambiguous in some cases. In this work, we revisit the modelling of the offsets of double-neutron-star (DNS) mergers with controlled numerical experiments using Monte Carlo simulations. To isolate the dynamical effects of the second supernova (SN) from uncertainties in the upstream binary evolution, we parametrize the direct progenitor of DNSs and integrate the post-SN trajectories in galactic potentials using galpy . Complementary to previous population synthesis calculations, our Monte Carlo tool, GRB-offset , provides a lightweight framework to identify sensitivities and expose degeneracies in offset modelling. With GRB-offset , we have investigated the following physical ingredients: SN physics (ejected mass and kick velocity), galactic potential (potential shape, galaxy virial mass), DNS birth location, star formation history, and redshift. The offset distributions given by our reference Monte Carlo simulation peak at around 30 and 1000 kpc for the DNSs bound to and unbound from the host galaxy, which sensitively depends on the considered physical ingredients. A given offset can arise from various combinations of these ingredients, introducing substantial degeneracies when interpreting observed offsets. Therefore, an observed offset alone can hardly constrain the properties of the DNS progenitor and of the host galaxies.

title: Spurious center-of-mass mode as an $S$-matrix pole within the Jost-random-phase approximation
abstract: Within the Jost-random-phase approximation (Jost-RPA), the spurious center-of-mass mode is a zero of the Jost determinant and hence a pole of the $S$ matrix. A zero at zero excitation energy $E$, whether from self-consistency or from a calibration of the residual interaction, is a pole of exactly second order when it has a single independent solution, every unoccupied bound orbital lies above the holes, and each hole is paired with every allowed partial wave; the order follows from the position of the zero, not from self-consistency. The state of this double pole, given by the Autonne-Takagi factorization of its $E^{-2}$ coefficient, is the zero-energy solution normalized by its inertia. In a self-consistent model of one energy density of the neutron and proton densities, every physical $S$-matrix element continued to $E=0$ carries the $E^{-2}$ term, contrary to an earlier conclusion. Subtracting the mode's principal part from the response changes the strength at real $E\neq0$ only through the smoothing and, in such a model, coincides with the projection of the ideal spurious state. In uncalibrated Woods-Saxon models of $^{16}$O and $^{208}$Pb the mode is a pair of poles on the imaginary axis.

title: QCD phase structure at high baryon density
abstract: Heavy-ion collisions provide unique access to the properties of QCD matter over a broad range of temperatures and baryon densities. We review recent progress in constraining the high-density phase structure of QCD, with particular emphasis on the microscopic inputs required for reliable transport modeling. We discuss cluster production, strange-particle interactions, collision dynamics at few-GeV energies, and the isospin dependence of the nuclear interaction, together with their impact on the interpretation of flow, yields, fluctuations, and possible critical signatures.

title: Density-driven $\alpha$-particle clustering in neutron-rich oxygen isotopes
abstract: In this work, we study the effect of valence neutrons on density-driven localisation in the neutron-rich oxygen isotopes. Calculations are performed within the multidimensionally constrained relativistic Hartree--Bogoliubov model using the DD-ME2 covariant energy-density functional. By constraining the mass rms radius to larger values, we study the structural evolution of these nuclei under progressive dilution, from spatially delocalised configurations to localised clustered states. The total energy, pairing correlations, deformation, and proton and neutron density distributions are analysed to determine how valence neutrons influence the emergence of $\alpha$-like clustering. For all three isotopes, we find a transition from a spatially delocalised nucleonic configuration to a tetrahedral $4\alpha$-like structure. The onset of this transition occurs at similar values of the radius-derived relative dilution parameter, $\chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\rho_{\mathrm{PT}}/ \rho_{\mathrm{GS}}\simeq 0.28$--$0.31$, and shows only a weak dependence on neutron number. The excess neutrons modify the clustered density by increasing the density in the central regions and between clusters, while leaving the underlying tetrahedral core structure largely intact. Finally, we also use a phenomenological four-centre H\"uckel-type mapping of nuclei, which provides a molecular-orbital-like interpretation of cluster structures. We find that the effective coupling between the cluster centers decreases by progressively expanding the nucleus. The centroid-referenced energy shift $\Delta E_{\mathrm{val}}$ also becomes less negative and provides smaller net molecular-orbital-like energy lowering relative to its centroid with increasing neutron number.

title: Systematical examination of the B 4 / 2 anomaly as a signature of enhanced triaxiality at the border of shape-coexistence regions
Suppression of heavy-ion fusion by slow quasifission
Scalable quantum state preparation via large-language-model-driven discovery
Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution
abstract: Parton multiplicity entropy, proposed by Kharzeev and Levin as entanglement between the region probed in deep inelastic scattering and the proton's remainder, was compared with hadron multiplicity data. It is computed from parton densities, which do not fix the partons' quantum state. We show that a one-parton density matrix from Lipatov's wave functions determines two entropies for resolved modes with finite mean number and entropy. Its trace is the mean parton number, and normalization gives a sampled parton's entropy. A compatible thermal state, if it exists, maximizes entropy at fixed one-parton matrix. This maximum equals the actual entropy only for that thermal state and measures entanglement only for a specified subsystem of a pure state. The geometric multiplicity entropy follows if all emitted partons share one mode. An entropy computed from densities becomes such a maximum, an upper bound on the actual entropy, only for specified resolved modes. We also show that the state averaged over unrecorded emissions, assumed incoherent across scales, obeys probability-preserving Lindblad evolution on finitely many regulated modes with the resolution scale if emission and no-emission terms match. The occupations reproduce leading-order DGLAP, with virtual terms, at leading logarithmic accuracy as the cutoffs on momentum fractions are removed. The reduction holds for strongly ordered transverse momenta in light-cone gauge and dilute occupations, including those of newly resolved modes. Approximating momentum and helicity modes by independent thermal populations closes the occupation equation and gives this bound's evolution, with Bose and Pauli factors from the operator algebra. We propose testing this approximation at HERA or the LHC. The test compares the mode number inferred from normalized hadron factorial moments in a rapidity window with the window's transverse mode count.

title: Isospin-breaking effects on the threshold cusp structures in Λ N - Σ N scattering
Design study of a 325 MHz ion injector and cold tests of RFQ and IH-DTL aluminum prototypes
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Chromatic Calorimetry -- A Novel Approach to Validate Energy Resolution and Particle Discrimination
abstract: Chromatic calorimetry (CCAL) analyses particle detection by utilizing scintillators with distinct emission wavelengths to measure the longitudinal energy deposition of particle showers in high-energy physics, improving particle identification (PID) and energy resolution. By stacking scintillators in order of decreasing emission wavelength, CCAL enables layer-specific energy measurements, analyzed via amplitude fractions ($f_i = A_i / \sum_j A_j$) and center of gravity ($\langle z_{\text{cog}} \rangle = \sum_i z_i E_i / \sum_i E_i$). This thesis presents results from two CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) experiments conducted in 2023 and 2024, complemented by GEANT4 simulations of a quantum dot (QD)-based CCAL design, to validate its potential for future colliders such as the Future Circular Collider (FCC).

title: CMS ECAL Phase-2 upgrade: characterisation and stability analysis of a three-stage low-voltage power-conversion system
abstract: As part of the High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider, the front-end electronics of the Compact Muon Solenoid electromagnetic calorimeter barrel are being replaced. A three-stage low-voltage power-conversion system supplies the upgraded electronics. As the cascade dynamics require characterisation to ensure stable operation, interactions between the three converter stages are assessed at their two interfaces using the Nyquist criterion. A validated shunt-injection setup using a Bode 100 frequency-response analyser provides in-situ impedance measurements under load to assess the accuracy of the averaged converter models. Results show that both interfaces are stable over the evaluated configurations, with modelled minimum distances to the critical point of 0.76 and 0.79, respectively. A turn-on study identifies capacitor charging at Stage 3 as the main cause of inrush currents triggering Stage 2 overcurrent protection. Two Stage 3 board variants stagger converter enables within and between boards, keeping the measured two-tower current below 5 A, within the 8.0 A protection threshold.

title: Tritium breeding lifetime assessment of a ceramic-based blanket in a fusion tokamak device
abstract: Abstract Achieving tritium self-sufficiency is a critical requirement for the viability of future fusion power plants. Here, a comprehensive assessment of the operational lifetimes of ceramic breeder materials under neutron irradiation within a tokamak environment is resented, focusing on the evolution of the tritium breeding ratio (TBR) over reactor-relevant timescales. This is defined here as the operational timeframe at which the TBR is maintained above a critical threshold of ≈1.10. Using the depletion capabilities within the OpenMC neutronics code, both conventional ceramic breeders (Li2TiO3, Li4SiO4, and advanced ceramic breeder – ACB) and emerging hybrid breeder-multiplier ceramics (Li8PbO6, Li2Be2O3) are assessed for operational lifetime strategies. Initial optimisation identifies breeder-to-multiplier volumetric ratios that maximise TBR at time zero, followed by time-dependent simulations to quantify TBR degradation due to lithium depletion during service. It is shown that while higher initial multiplier fractions enhance TBR, they also accelerate lithium depletion, reducing blanket lifetime. Conversely, hybrid ceramics with intrinsic neutron multiplication show reduced sensitivity to additional multipliers. A novel layer-wise optimisation approach, varying breeder and multiplier distributions radially and poloidally, is shown to extend blanket lifetimes and maintain TBR above the critical threshold for longer periods demonstrating lifetime limitations may be elsewhere within the breeder blanket. Verification against FISPACT-II confirms the accuracy of the OpenMC depletion methodology utilised. The results highlight the importance of spatially optimised material distributions and lithium inventory management in maximising breeder blanket longevity. This work provides robust framework for the design of next-generation solid breeder blankets, offering practical strategies to minimise replacement frequency and support sustainable fusion energy.

title: Performance and damage mechanisms of dispersion-strengthened tungsten under H-mode plasma in DIII-D
abstract: Abstract Dispersion strengthened tungsten (DSW) alloys are promising materials for plasma facing components, displaying improved mechanical properties and microstructure stability compared to pure tungsten. In this work, the performance of DSW reinforced with 1 wt% transition-metal carbide (TaC, TiC, or ZrC) has been examined under H-mode plasma in the DIII-D tokamak. DSW samples were mounted both flush with the divertor floor and at a 10° angle towards the incoming plasma fluxes to further increase the heat and particle loading. To simulate the impact of prolonged tokamak operation, similar plasma exposures were repeated on two additional sets of DSW samples: one set pre-implanted with 10 22 m -2 helium, and another set heated in-situ to an additional 500°C. Flush mounted samples exhibited good surface stability, with no evidence of melting or cracking regardless of composition or treatment. Carbon redeposition was observed on most samples, likely due to the graphite environment of DIII-D. Under coupled thermal loading and helium implantation, surface nanostructuring developed in some DSW samples; however, DSW containing tantalum dispersion phases showed strong resistance to such surface modification. In contrast, obvious surface melting was observed on 10° angled samples containing TaC and ZrC dispersoids, likely associated with dispersoid oxidation during fabrication, which reduced thermal conductivity and promoted elevated surface temperatures during plasma exposure. The grain morphology of DSW containing TiC remained largely unchanged, although near-surface dispersoids on the angled TiC sample were missing after plasma exposure. The loss is associated with oxidation of the dispersoids during fabrication, followed by sublimation during plasma exposure. Through systematic comparison of DSW performance under H-mode plasma conditions, this study identifies key degradation mechanisms and highlights strategies to improve the performance of DSW as plasma facing materials.

title: Measurement, modeling, and correction of decapolar Hamiltonian terms in the LHC
abstract: Understanding and mitigating high-order nonlinearities is essential for ensuring long-term beam storage in high-energy colliders. The stability of particles at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is indeed strongly influenced by nonlinear effects, particularly at injection energy where the beam occupies a large fraction of the vacuum chamber. Among these effects, third-order chromaticity, primarily driven by decapolar fields, limits dynamic aperture and beam lifetime. Despite corrections based on magnetic measurements and model predictions, a discrepancy remains between the measured and expected third-order chromaticity, indicating the presence of residual decapolar components. In this study, the decapolar fields in the LHC at injection energy are investigated and their impact on beam dynamics assessed. Chromatic amplitude detuning and decapolar resonance driving terms are directly measured for the first time, using forced oscillations driven by an ac dipole. These measurements provide new insights into the source and impact of decapolar fields in the LHC and indicate that refined correction strategies could enhance beam lifetime, particularly for high-brightness operation in future runs.

title: Heavy quarkonium spin transport in a hot medium
abstract: We investigate the in-medium spin transport of heavy quarkonium using an open-quantum-system approach based on potential nonrelativistic QCD. We express the heavy quarkonium dilepton decay angular distribution in terms of late-time quarkonium spin-dependent distribution functions. Working in the quantum-optical regime, where the inverse quarkonium size is much larger than the binding energy and the binding energy is comparable to or larger than the medium temperature $T$, we derive a spin-dependent quantum master equation incorporating both dissociation and regeneration, followed by the corresponding projected semiclassical Boltzmann equations. At leading order in the coupling, we retain the recoil corrections of relative order $T/M$ that contribute to the leading spin-dependent collision kernel. Here $M$ denotes the heavy-quark mass. At zeroth order in fluid gradients, we show that the relative motion between quarkonium and the medium supplies the leading anisotropy, while spin-chromomagnetic and spin-orbit interactions both contribute to the leading nonzero spin-alignment kernel. As an exploratory phenomenological application, we also estimate the medium-induced polarization parameter $\lambda_{\theta}$ of bottomonium $\Upsilon(1\text{S})$ using a simplified rate equation with background density matrices obtained from the Lindblad equation using QTraj. Within this simplified treatment, the resulting medium-induced polarization is found to be very small while a naive rescaling for charmonium can qualitatively describe the polarization of charmonium.

title: Statistical mechanics and hierarchy of learnability in quantum codes: From generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders
abstract: Local weak measurements provide noisy information about observables encoded in a quantum code. We formulate the corresponding Bayesian inference problem for a broad class of topological stabilizer codes by mapping it to classical spin models with generalized symmetries. When the wavefunction deformation and Gaussian measurement strengths coincide, the replicated model acquires an enlarged symmetry. We use this symmetry to derive exact identities among correlators averaged over measurement records that quantify the learnability of nonlocal observables associated with fractionalized excitations. Together with correlation inequalities in the associated clean ferromagnetic models, these identities establish hierarchies of learnability: if two observables remain learnable at long distances, their product must also remain learnable. We demonstrate these relations in the rank-2 toric code and the X-cube model, whose classical descriptions exhibit modulated and subsystem symmetries, respectively. We further extend the analysis to finite group quantum double models, including non-Abelian ones. We derive exact relations between learnability and correlations in the corresponding classical models, and show that the representation structure and fusion rules of anyons impose further constraints under suitable positivity conditions. These results constrain which types of nonlocal information can be learned simultaneously, providing a guide to learning phase diagrams in quantum codes under local weak measurements.

title: Probing Heavier-Baryon Oscillations through Light-Baryon Mixing
abstract: Motivated by the existing direct limits on $\Xi_b^0$ and $\Xi_c^0$ oscillations, we investigate how Standard Model weak interactions connect baryon-number-violating mixing in heavy neutral baryons to the much more strongly constrained neutron-antineutron and $\Lambda-\bar\Lambda$ mixing. We focus on $\Xi_b^0$, $\Lambda_b^0$, $\Xi_c^0$, and $\Omega_c^0$ oscillations and derive indirect constraints on their mass-mixing parameters from existing limits on $n-\bar n$ oscillations and on $\Lambda-\bar\Lambda$ mixing, the latter inferred from dinucleon-decay searches. The weak baryon-to-baryon transition amplitudes are estimated by saturating the relevant hadronic correlators with low-lying intermediate baryons. The required weak vertices are modelled using semileptonic form factors from lattice QCD, quark models, and QCD sum rules. Since these form factors must be continued outside their physical semileptonic domains and the resulting loop integrals depend on a UV cutoff, our results are order-of-magnitude estimates subject to sizeable hadronic uncertainties. For a benchmark cutoff of $10~{\rm GeV}$, the indirect bounds on the $\Xi_b^0$ and $\Xi_c^0$ mixing parameters are roughly three and five orders of magnitude stronger than the direct LHCb and Belle limits, indicating that light-baryon $|\Delta B|=2$ searches can probe heavy-baryon oscillations far beyond present direct sensitivities.

title: Machine-learned particle flow as a foundation model for collider physics
abstract: The workflow from particle collision to physics analysis passes through a series of reconstruction steps that are traditionally modular and disconnected, with no shared representation linking low-level detector data to high-level analysis tasks. We show that casting event reconstruction as a machine learning problem naturally produces such a shared representation. We repurpose a machine learning model trained for particle-flow reconstruction (MLPF) to perform three distinct analysis tasks: jet flavor identification, jet energy regression, and missing momentum regression. By appending the per-particle latent representations learned during reconstruction as additional input features, we substantially improve over baselines that use conventional particle-level features alone. We further demonstrate that a single linear layer trained using only the latent representations achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art baseline architectures, and outperforms the baseline for missing momentum regression with approximately 35 times fewer parameters. These results demonstrate that the latent representations learned during reconstruction encode essential physics information needed for downstream analysis, establishing MLPF as a foundation model and offering a concrete step toward an end-to-end pipeline from detector data to physics analysis.

title: Heavy-meson bag parameters using gradient flow
abstract: We demonstrate the use of the gradient flow combined with the short flow-time expansion ( GF + SFTX ) as a renormalization procedure for four-quark operator matrix elements and associated bag parameters relevant to neutral heavy-meson mixing ( Δ Q = 2 ) and heavy-meson lifetimes ( Δ Q = 0 ). Using six RBC/UKQCD 2 + 1 -flavor domain-wall fermion ensembles, we calculate for a charm-strange system with physical quark masses flowed bag parameters and match them to the MS ¯ scheme using perturbative SFTX coefficients up to next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD. We employ a multiscale matching strategy and a renormalization-group improved flow-time evolution which allows for a reliable estimate of systematic uncertainties. For a fictitious neutral D s meson, we obtain the Δ Q = 2 MS ¯ bag parameter B 1 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = 0.7673 ( 123 ) , consistent with existing short-distance D 0 mixing determinations. For the Δ Q = 0 lifetime-ratio operator basis, we find the MS ¯ results B 1 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = 1.0524 ( 97 ) , B 2 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = 0.9621 ( 71 ) , ε 1 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = − 0.2275 ( 76 ) , and ε 2 MS ¯ ( 3 GeV ) = − 0.0005 ( 8 ) . We provide conversion formulae to reexpress these results for an arbitrary choice of evanescent operators. These results demonstrate that GF + SFTX can deliver precise determinations of dimension-six four-quark operators and establish a framework for future lattice computations including more complex operator bases, where the challenge of power-divergent mixing is shifted to the continuum and handled in the SFTX.

title: Core reduction for increasing neutron flux and radioisotope production in the IEA-R1 research reactor
abstract: This work aims to present and analyze a new reactor core configuration for the IEA-R1 reactor core with the objective of enhancing its neutron irradiation capabilities. The reactor was modeled using the KENO-VI module from the SCALE Code System, provided by ORNL. Results have shown that implementing a near-cylindrical configuration with 20 fuel elements in the IEA-R1 core could substantially increase neutron flux, particularly in the center irradiation positions such as the EIBe (Beryllium Irradiated Element). After comparing various configurations, we conducted a brief analysis of the proposed core configuration's potential to produce 177Lu, resulting in a 34% increase in the specific activity of 177Lu considering a fuel power cycle around 21 days.

title: CMS ECAL VFE Production Qualification
abstract: Upgrading the CMS ECAL barrel for the HL-LHC requires replacement of all on-detector electronics, including 12240 Very-Front-End (VFE) cards employing CATIA and LiTE-DTU ASICs for amplification and digitisation of signals from ECAL's 61200 lead-tungstate crystals. All production VFEs undergo the same qualification procedure: functional testing, environmental stress screening, and calibration. We have received and functionally tested 13596 unique VFEs; two never passed our test criteria. Results for other VFEs are uniform and within expectations, demonstrating the excellent quality of the cards. Key metrics, such as a gain ratio of $10.21 \pm 0.07$ and power consumption of $1.805 \pm 0.013~\mathrm{W}$, demonstrate high consistency across the batch.

title: Asymmetric dark matter from low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis
abstract: We investigate a novel type of asymmetric dark matter (ADM) model in which the dark matter asymmetry and the baryon asymmetry in our Universe (BAU) are produced simultaneously via low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis, where the mass scale of right-handed neutrino is much lower than the Davidson–Ibarra bound M 1 ≪ 10 9 GeV . In our scenario, both asymmetries are predominantly sourced by a dynamical C P phase, namely, the Majoron. Its kinetic misalignment provides a sufficiently large, time-dependent effective C P phase, allowing efficient asymmetry production even for low-scale right-handed neutrinos. In our framework, the sources of C P violation responsible for the BAU and ADM are correlated with each other, leading to a predictive relation for the dark matter mass. In particular, when the dark matter asymmetry reaches its equilibrium value before freeze-out, the dark matter mass is typically predicted to lie in the range O ( 0.1 ) GeV ≲ m χ ≲ O ( 100 ) GeV , which lies within the sensitivity of direct detection experiments. On the other hand, if the dark matter asymmetry does not reach its equilibrium value due to weak coupling, the allowed mass range extends over a broader interval, O ( 0.1 ) GeV ≲ m χ ≲ O ( 10 ) TeV .

title: Toward high-performance tracking simulation of long-range resistive-wall driven transverse coupled-bunch instabilities
abstract: The long-range transverse resistive-wall (RW) wakefield is a key driver of transverse coupled-bunch instabilities in high-current storage rings. Simulating these instabilities accurately is typically time-consuming, because conventional time-domain tracking codes such as store the turn-by-turn bunch-centroid history and perform discrete convolutions with the wakefield, which poses a bottleneck for long-term tracking. To overcome this limitation, this work reformulates the long-range RW wakefield calculation, converting the explicit history-dependent convolution into a recursive update by representing the wakefield as a sum-of-exponential functions. This approach avoids storing the bunch-centroid history and is well suited to parallel graphics-processing-unit architectures; it has been implemented in the tracking code . Benchmark tests, using parameters of the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF), show that with the proposed method maintains high accuracy in the growth rate while achieving a speedup of at least 2 orders of magnitude over . Leveraging this computational efficiency, we conduct a systematic study of RW instabilities for HALF, with particular focus on the interplay among filling pattern, chromaticity, and harmonic-cavity bunch lengthening.

title: Suppression of transient beam-loading effects in storage rings via main-cavity power source feedforward scheme
abstract: Dual-frequency radio-frequency systems are widely deployed in high-brightness synchrotron radiation light sources to achieve electron bunch lengthening. However, the transient beam-loading (TBL) effect induced by bunch gaps causes significant synchronous phase shifts and severely compromises bunch-lengthening performance. To address this, we propose an active compensation scheme that suppresses voltage fluctuations in both the main and harmonic cavities by modulating only the driving voltage of the main cavity via a feedforward approach. To elucidate the underlying physical mechanisms, we establish a gap-induced linear decomposition analytical model, which decomposes the TBL-induced beam voltage into steady-state and transient components. Based on this model, we derive an optimization method to minimize power requirements, enabling the main-cavity TBL compensation to achieve performance levels comparable to those of broadband-cavity TBL compensation. The efficacy of this framework is demonstrated through two case studies: for an steady-state microbunching storage ring with a 7.5-MHz hardware half-bandwidth, the required single-cavity peak power is maintained at 158 kW, with normalized average radiation power improved from 78% to 97%; for the KEK light source storage ring with a 6-MHz bandwidth, the single-cavity peak power is optimized to 148 kW, successfully restoring the average bunch length from 31.1 to 40.9 ps. The proposed scheme establishes a highly efficient and cost-effective paradigm for TBL suppression, providing a promising technical pathway for next-generation light sources.

title: Space charge modeling method in 2.5D for scaling fixed-field alternating-gradient accelerators
abstract: Scaling fixed-field alternating-gradient accelerators (scaling FFAs) are promising candidates for high-intensity proton drivers, for which space charge effects are a key limitation of beam performance. For long bunches in circular accelerators, 2.5D space charge methods provide an efficient alternative to full 3D PIC methods by exploiting the large longitudinal-to-transverse aspect ratio of the bunch. In scaling FFAs, however, the reference closed orbit varies with particle energy, and the transverse and longitudinal directions are not directly available in cylindrical coordinates. Therefore, the longitudinal slicing and transverse planes required by a 2.5D model must be reconstructed dynamically, rather than defined from a single fixed reference orbit, which poses a central challenge for efficient 2.5D modeling in high-intensity scaling FFAs. This paper presents a new 2.5D space charge modeling method for high-intensity scaling FFAs and its implementation in the PyFFA code. The central idea is to replace the fixed reference orbit used in conventional 2.5D models with a dynamically reconstructed local reference frame based on a precomputed family of energy-dependent closed orbits. During tracking, this frame is updated according to the instantaneous particle state, enabling transverse Poisson equations to be solved consistently in this dynamic local coordinate system. The resulting space charge field is then transformed back to global cylindrical coordinates and applied in the tracking equations. Benchmarks of space charge fields, tune shifts, rms envelope evolution, and longitudinal phase-space evolution show good agreement with analytical results, validating the field calculation and its coupling to beam dynamics for long, arc-shaped bunches in scaling FFAs. The implemented model enables efficient studies of space charge effects on beam dynamics in high-intensity scaling FFAs.

title: Design criteria for a beam-driven resonant passive transverse deflector for longitudinal beam diagnostics
abstract: Conventional radio-frequency (rf) transverse deflecting structures provide high-resolution longitudinal beam diagnostics, but require externally generated high-power rf, waveguide distribution, synchronization, and input coupling at the operating frequency. We propose design criteria for a beam-driven resonant passive transverse deflector that does not require an external rf source. A leading drive bunch excites long-range wakefields in an off-axis periodic copper structure and a delayed witness bunch experiences the transverse wake near a zero crossing. The concept is based on the large temporal slope available from high-frequency wake components. A structure designed for installation after the second bunch compressor in the three-bunch-compressor layout of the European XFEL is optimized to place the zero crossing of the drive-bunch-induced transverse wake potential approximately one rf-bucket spacing of the 1.3 GHz linac behind the drive bunch. The selected geometry produces a multimode transverse kick dominated by TM-like modes. We use time-domain wake simulations, frequency-domain decomposition, cell-number scaling, mechanical-tolerance scans, orbit-offset studies, and uniform thermal scaling to determine the operating point and its sensitivity. For this geometry, the zero crossing occurs at s 0 ≃ 230.6 mm , with a per-cell temporal slope of S cell = 1.186 mV / ( pC fs cell ) . For a compact 1 m structure operated with a 250 pC drive bunch and a 700 MeV witness beam, the estimated temporal resolution is about 33 fs .

title: Comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction methods on IXPE astrophysical data
abstract: A hybrid reconstruction algorithm combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with standard moment analysis to improve the reconstruction of photoelectron tracks in the gas pixel detectors (GPDs) on board the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE). The method has been validated on laboratory calibration data, but its performance on astrophysical sources with known polarimetric properties has not yet been systematically characterized. We present the first comparison of hybrid and standard reconstruction methods on IXPE data of astrophysical point sources, with the aim of quantifying the improvement in polarimetric sensitivity as a function of energy. We analyzed two IXPE observations selected to probe complementary regimes: Her X-1, a bright and highly polarized accreting X-ray pulsar used as a quantitative benchmark, and the transient neutron star low-mass X-ray binary XTE J1701-461 in its soft state, a bright source with no detectable polarization used to measure residual systematic effects. For each source, we compared the normalized Stokes parameters, the degree of polarization (PD) and angle (PA), and the detection significance derived from the level 2 event files produced by both pipelines. For Her X-1, the hybrid method yields a consistently higher detection significance at all energies, with a statistically significant improvement above ∼2.83 keV. The significance ratio, R = σ_ /σ_ , deviates from unity by up to 9.3σ in the 2.83-4.00 keV bin, rising to R = 1.18 ± 0.03 at 5.66-8.00 keV at 6.2σ. For XTE J1701-461, both methods yield polarization degrees consistent with zero and significance ratios consistent with unity. Through a Fourier analysis, we identify some modes (m = 3, m = 6, m = 12, and m = 15) with power excesses in the hybrid angle distributions at low energies, which are significant at $>7σ$ relative to the standard method, while at 5-8 keV all modes are consistent with the expected noise level for both methods: these modes are amplified by CNN but do not propagate to the Stokes parameters. hyb std The hybrid method provides a measurable and statistically significant improvement in the polarimetric sensitivity for bright point sources that is fully consistent with the predictions from laboratory calibrations and equivalent to a sim20% increase in effective area without the additional cost of observation time. The hexagonal-grid modes are a geometric artifact of the GPD pixel structure and have no effect on polarimetric results since the additional modes are orthogonal to the polarization modes. The improvement is robustly detected for the bright source examined here (σ_ std For the unpolarized source in our sample (σ_ std the central significance increase is consistent with the same trend, but is not individually resolved at the available statistics. These findings confirm the readiness of the hybrid method for systematic application to IXPE astrophysical data.

title: The two-flavor Schwinger model at 50: Solving Coleman's puzzles
abstract: In his 1976 paper "More about the massive Schwinger model," Coleman introduced $1+1$-dimensional Quantum Electrodynamics coupled to two charged massive fermions. By applying Abelian bosonization, he elucidated much of the physics of this two-flavor Schwinger model, but he listed three puzzles at the end of his paper. We present new analytical and numerical calculations to solve Coleman's three puzzles and thereby deepen our understanding of this model. These puzzles pertain to the theory with equal fermion masses at $\theta = 0$ and at $\theta = \pi$, as well as the size of isospin-breaking effects when the fermion masses are unequal. For the puzzle at $\theta = \pi$, the solution is related to the structure of the zero-temperature phase diagram arXiv:2305.04437: for equal fermion masses $m$, the model exhibits spontaneous breaking of charge conjugation symmetry and absence of confinement for any value of the gauge coupling $g$, so that there is a smooth interpolation from weak to strong coupling. Using two-loop Renormalization Group and integrability methods, we show that the mass gap behaves as $\sim m e^{-0.111 g^2/m^2}$ in the strong coupling regime $m\ll g$. Our numerical results using the lattice Hamiltonian are in good agreement with this behavior. For the puzzle at $\theta = 0$, the solution is related to a level crossing between two isosinglet particles with different discrete quantum numbers; we demonstrate the necessity of such a crossing by comparing integrability and weak coupling calculations, and we also exhibit the crossing numerically. Finally, we provide a new estimate for the size of isospin-breaking effects caused by different fermion masses at strong coupling.

title: Probing the G (3900) state in heavy-ion collisions
Multi-Threshold Sampling: Signal Space, Sampling Operators, and First Recorded Crossing-Time Distributions
abstract: Multi-threshold (MT) sampling records crossing times for parameter estimation and waveform reconstruction. We develop signal and observation spaces and stochastic crossing, timing, and selection operators with associated Markov kernels. Finite point measures accommodate variable crossing counts and preserve multiplicity after quantization. For nonhomogeneous Poisson photon arrivals with shared threshold noise, shared timing jitter before quantization, and identity selection, we derive exact first recorded crossing-time distributions. A Poisson series covers general admissible paths with a time-uniform truncation bound. For continuous paths, interval extrema give the exact cumulative distribution function (CDF) and a Fourier representation with contact corrections. A biexponential arrival-intensity and response model admits a two-dimensional first-crossing integral equation on arbitrary finite observation windows, with a unique bounded measurable solution and a Poisson-tail approximation bound. For continuous causal responses with finitely many analytic pieces and bounded first and second branch derivatives, we prove a conditional standard-deviation (SD) limit at first mean crossings with positive slope under relative threshold-noise and fine timing scales. For the biexponential model, its coefficient increases strictly on a parameter-uniform interval and, under a shape condition, up to the first mean peak. Scintillation experiments compare the calculated CDF and conditional SDs with independent waveform simulations on a window extending beyond the single-photon response peak.

title: Identifiability of g mode resonances in eccentric binary neutron stars with multidetector observations
High-precision numerical framework for the time-varying solar neutrino flux with full Earth matter oscillation corrections for global underground laboratories
Heavy quark collisional energy loss in a nonextensive quark-gluon plasma
abstract: Abstract In this study, we derive the longitudinal and transverse gluon self-energies and the corresponding dielectric functions for a nonextensive QGP, based on nonextensive statistical mechanics and a kinetic theory framework. The nonextensive parameter $q$ enters these quantities primarily through the modification of the Debye mass. Utilizing the derived dielectric functions, we then calculate the collisional energy loss for a heavy quark using two established formalisms: the plasma physics-based Thoma-Gyulassy formula and the thermal field theory-originated Kirzhnits-Thoma formula.Our results show that for both formalisms, the collisional energy loss increases with the nonextensive parameter$q$ with this enhancement being more significant at higher incident quark momenta and suppressed for a heavier quark mass. The energy loss predicted from the Kirzhnits-Thoma formula is substantially larger than that from the Thoma-Gyulassy formula, and the nonextensive effect on the energy loss is more pronounced in the former. Furthermore, the mass suppression of the nonextensive effect on the energy loss is weaker in the Kirzhnits-Thoma approach. These calculations demonstrate that nonextensive statistics can significantly alter the energy loss in the QGP. title: Ground-State Heavy-Baryon Mass Spectrum in the Relativistic Independent Quark Model
abstract: We extend our work to compute the ground-state baryon mass spectrum containing charm and bottom quarks in the relativistic independent quark (RIQ) model with an average flavor--independent confining potential in equally mixed scalar--vector harmonic form. Each quark moves as a Dirac particle inside the potential. The resulting core mass is then corrected perturbatively, accounting for the pion self-energy, pion exchange, and pairwise color--electric and color--magnetic one-gluon exchange. Six input parameters common to every baryon: the potential parameters (confinement strength, the potential offset) and the $u(=d)$, $s$, $c$, and $b$ constituent quark masses are optimized using a few experimentally measured baryon states. The model then uses these optimized parameters to predict the mass spectra of doubly heavy, mixed-$bc$, and triply heavy baryons. We compare our predictions with lattice QCD, relativistic quark model results, and available experimental measurements. Our results are consistent with these model predictions and experimental results.

title: A Duality Model in Which Dual QCD Becomes Hydrodynamics
abstract: Revisiting a duality model in which dual QCD becomes hydrodynamics, or the dual gluon is a fluid, allows us to understand some of the mysteries of QCD, such as the behavior of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) as a perfect fluid and gluon saturation in the structure function at high energies. This old-fashioned duality converts the gluon action into hydrodynamics described by the 2-form stream function $W^a_{\mu\nu}$ with eight colors. All interactions then become current--current interactions of the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio type. The resulting theory admits a strong-coupling expansion about the fluid. This can provide a third method to supplement perturbative QCD and lattice QCD.

title: $\bar{D}$-meson Nucleon Scattering from Lattice QCD at the Physical Point
abstract: We report the first lattice QCD study of the $s$-wave scattering of the $\bar{D}$-meson and the nucleon at the physical point, utilizing (2+1)-flavor configurations generated by the HAL QCD collaboration with a pion mass of $m_\pi\simeq 137$ MeV and a lattice spacing of $a\simeq0.084$ fm. By applying the HAL QCD method to the four-point correlation function of the $\bar{D}N$ system, we obtain a leading-order potential of the derivative expansion of the interaction kernel, which is then used to extract the $s$-wave phase shifts of low-energy $\bar{D}N$ scattering. Both the isospin $I=0$ and $I=1$ channels have a short-range repulsive core and a shallow attractive pocket in the intermediate to long-range region, though the $I=0$ channel is more attractive than the $I=1$ channel. We also observe that the $\bar{D}N$ potential exhibits more attraction than the $KN$ potential, which is its analog in the strange sector. In terms of the $s$-wave phase shifts, the $I=0$ channel shows a weak attractive behavior in the low-energy region with a positive scattering length of $0.425 \pm 0.163 (_{-0.105}^{+0.129})$ fm, whereas the $I=1$ channel shows repulsion with a negative scattering length of $-0.235 \pm 0.046 (_{-0.007}^{+0.040})$ fm. No bound states are found in both isospin channels, indicating the absence of a pentaquark state in the $s$-wave $\bar{D}N$ system.

title: Semileptonic Decay of $\Lambda_b \rightarrow N(1520)\ell^-\bar{\nu}_{\ell}$ from QCD Light-cone Sum Rules
abstract: Abstract We investigate the complete set of vector and axial-vector form factors for the charged-current transition $\Lambda_b^0\to N(1520)^+$ using QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSRs) based on the light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the $\Lambda_b$ baryon, with the hard-scattering kernels evaluated at tree level. In the hadronic representation of the correlation function, we include the pole contributions of both the negative-parity $N(1520)$, with $J^P=3/2^-$, and the positive-parity $N(1720)$, with $J^P=3/2^+$. By matching a selected set of Lorentz structures, we derive sum rules that separate the $N(1520)$ contribution from the $N(1720)$ contribution within the adopted two-pole hadronic ansatz. After extrapolating the large-recoil LCSR results over the physical$q^2$ region using a pole-improved $z$ expansion truncated at linearorder, we predict the differential branching fractions, the lepton forward-backward asymmetry, the charged-lepton polarization, and the $N(1520)$ polarization in $\Lambda_b^0\to N(1520)^+\ell^-\bar{\nu}_{\ell}$ ($\ell=e,\mu,\tau$). The corresponding total branching fractions are$\mathcal{B}_{e,\mu,\tau}=(12.4\pm10.5,\,12.4\pm10.5,\,5.0\pm4.3)\times10^{-5}$. Within the stated approximations, these results may serve as theoretical benchmarks for future experimental studies of this channel.
