AI-based plasma equilibrium parameter inference in KSTAR for DEMO-relevant reactors using only ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a deep neural network for high-fidelity equilibrium parameter inference, serving as a surrogate of the magnetic EFIT reconstruction and relying exclusively on ex-vessel magnetic signals. The objective is to circumvent the long-term integrity constraints of in-vessel magnetic diagnostics in the nuclear environment of the Demonstration Fusion Power Reactor (DEMO)-relevant devices. Using KSTAR data (2021–2024), a baseline model trained solely on measured ex-vessel magnetic diagnostics (the Measurement-only model) is compared with an Augmented model, which addresses informational sparsity via virtual-sensor signals computed from the GEQDSK. The Augmented model achieves predictive fidelity comparable to off-line EFIT, with a coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) above 0.99 and a range-normalized root-mean-squared error (NRMSE) of 0.332 % averaged over all parameters, against 2.385 % for the Measurement-only model. Because the virtual-sensor inputs derive from the EFIT solutions that define the targets, these figures quantify the surrogate fidelity with respect to the magnetic EFIT and constitute an upper bound on the accuracy attainable with physically installed ex-vessel probes, not that of an independent reconstruction. As the reference floor for the Measurement-only model, the magnetic fitting residuals of the parent EFIT reconstructions against the measured probe signals are quantified, yielding pooled range-normalized residuals of 1.55 % – 3.87 % per campaign with structured, campaign-persistent components that random noise perturbations do not emulate. Robust accuracy is maintained during neutral beam injection (NBI)-induced transients, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based attribution verifies that the Augmented model captures the underlying magnetohydrodynamic physics, specifically the Shafranov shift. With a median single forward pass inference latency of 3.47 ms (99th percentile: 3.53 ms), the framework is a viable surrogate for conventional numerical solvers. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that an idealized, EFIT-consistent realization of a densified ex-vessel sensor configuration retains sufficient information for high-precision equilibrium parameter inference, provided that magnetic probes are physically installed at the designated locations. This establishes the information-content prerequisite for ex-vessel-only inference in DEMO. The accuracy attainable from physically installed probes, subject to conductor-model, calibration and structured measurement-model errors, is not established and requires validation against measured ex-vessel signals.

title: Neutrino production at the extreme vicinity of the supermassive black hole in NGC 1068
abstract: The identification of NGC~1068 as an extragalactic high-energy neutrino source raises the question of the physical conditions required for neutrino production. Motivated by the newly updated IceCube data (down to $\sim 0.2 \,\rm TeV$) for NGC 1068, we present a statistical, model-independent inference primarily constrained by the multi-messenger observations. We calculate neutrino production from hadronic channels (including hadronuclear and photomeson processes) and the accompanying cascade gamma rays, and then employ the Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) method to explore the parameter space comprehensively, constrained by observational data. According to our results, the emission region is tightly limited: $R \gtrsim 10\,R_{\rm s}$ is excluded at $\sim 5\sigma$, and $R \gtrsim 6\,R_{\rm s}$ at $\sim 3\sigma$, where $R_{\rm s}$ is Schwarzschild radius of supermassive black hole (SMBH). Furthermore, reproducing $\gtrsim 80\%$ of the observed neutrino flux further restricts the emission to $R \lesssim 3R_{\rm s}$. Finally, we explore the possible particle acceleration mechanisms and find that stochastic acceleration naturally satisfies all constraints, whereas alternative mechanisms require extreme, fine-tuning parameters. We therefore identify stochastic acceleration as the most viable origin of the neutrino emission from NGC~1068.

title: Hybrid stars with hyperons: structure based on QCD sum rule coupling constants
abstract: We present a comprehensive study of hybrid stars composed of hadrons, leptons, and quarks within a relativistic mean-field framework. Using coupling constants derived from QCD sum rules (QCDSR), we first determine the bulk properties of nuclear matter and evaluate the single-particle potentials of nucleons and hyperons to constrain the hadronic sector. The equation of state (EOS) under beta equilibrium is then constructed employing the $\sigma-\omega-\rho$ model for the hadronic phase, while the quark phase is described using both the MIT bag model and the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. The hadron-quark phase transition is analyzed through both Gibbs and Maxwell constructions. Based on resulting EOSs, we obtain the mass-radius relations of hybrid stars, investigate particle fractions and their radial distributions, and calculate the tidal Love number ($\mathcal{K}_{2}$) and the dimensionless tidal deformability ($\varLambda$). Our results provide quantitative predictions relevant for comparison with current multimessenger astrophysical observations.

title: CLVisc Agent for autonomous relativistic hydrodynamics studies
abstract: Abstract We enable large language model (LLM) agents to autonomously perform end-to-end hydrodynamic simulations of the quark–gluon plasma evolution and calculation of final hadron spectra in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. We design a meta skill that allows an agent to explore a project’s source code, craft a specialized skill, and iteratively refine it. Applying this meta skill to the (3+1)D viscous hydrodynamic code CLVisc, the agent builds a CLVisc skill encoding its operational knowledge and then independently executes full scientific workflows: designing parameter scans, running simulations, comparing ensemble results, and producing publication-ready figures. Crucially, the agent draws on literature-informed heavy-ion physics to select physically meaningful observables and interpret outcomes without explicit instruction. We demonstrate the pipeline in two scenarios: temperature-dependent shear viscosity over entropy density $\eta/s$, and nuclear-structure effects in O+O collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$~TeV using four \textit{ab initio} descriptions of $^{16}$O. In both, the agent plans, executes, and analyzes autonomously, devising new initial-state observables to explain final observations and extract qualitative knowledge. The meta skill is agnostic to code versions and Monte Carlo generators, promising future multi-agent systems in high-energy nuclear physics.

title: n=1 ideal MHD stability of tokamak plasmas with low aspect ratio and negative triangularity
abstract: Abstract Spherical tokamaks (STs) exhibit excellent ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) stability owing to their low-aspect-ratio configuration, while negative triangularity (NT) configurations have attracted extensive attention in recent years for their superior confinement performance, despite relatively inferior MHD stability. This paper investigates the n=1 ideal MHD stability of NT configurations at low aspect ratios, to evaluate the potential compatibility of these two advantageous regimes. Using the MARS-F code, we perform beta-limit scans over various triangularity and aspect ratio values, with fixed safety factor $q$ profiles and normalized pressure gradient $p'$ profiles. The results show that the stability of positive triangularity (PT) configurations is enhanced at low aspect ratios, consistent with classical expectations; however, counterintuitively, the stability of NT configurations deteriorates with decreasing aspect ratio. We present a physical interpretation of this phenomenon, demonstrating that two intuitive concepts ( the ``most natural shape" and ``good/bad curvature") and magnetic well depth can fully explain this geometric effect and the observed stability trend. In addition, the stabilizing effect of the safety factor preserves at low aspect ratios for both PT and NT configurations, partially mitigating the aforementioned stability deterioration of NT plasmas.

title: Wave-energy partition governs weak collisional damping in cold plasmas
abstract: Abstract Weak dissipation can control wave propagation, mode competition, and instability thresholds in plasmas, yet the physical origin of large branch-to-branch differences in collisional damping is often obscured by dielectric-tensor calculations. We show that weak collisional damping in cold plasmas is governed by wave-energy partition. In the one-rate cold plasma model with independent-relaxation collisions, the damping rate of a positive-energy collisionless eigenmode equals, to leading order in weak collisions, the collision frequency multiplied by the fraction of the total wave energy stored in plasma motion. This result recasts the standard perturbative damping formula into a compact and physically transparent law, immediately explaining why field-dominated branches such as whistlers can be much less damped than the collision frequency, whereas quasi-electrostatic modes can exhibit damping of comparable magnitude. Analytic examples for Langmuir, transverse electromagnetic, whistler, and extraordinary waves show that the energy-partition form classifies weak collisional damping across distinct branches and provides a simple diagnostic for mode competition in multibranch plasma-wave systems.

title: Twist-three quark TMDs from back-to-back dijet production in next-to-eikonal DIS
abstract: We study back-to-back dijet production in deep inelastic scattering (DIS) at next-to-eikonal accuracy within the Color Glass Condensate framework, focusing on the quark-background contributions. We compute the quark-gluon and quark-antiquark production cross sections through next-to-leading power in the correlation limit for longitudinally and transversely polarized photons. In the quark-gluon channel, we derive both the kinematic corrections to the hard parts accompanying the twist-two quark distribution and the genuine twist-three contributions involving three-body quark-gluon-quark correlators. In the quark-antiquark channel, the interference of the eikonal amplitude with the double $t$-channel quark-exchange amplitudes probes three-body correlators with a different transverse arrangement of the fields. We express the results in terms of transverse momentum dependent (TMD) correlators and provide the corresponding hard coefficients. Our analysis extends the operator-level connection between the next-to-eikonal CGC framework and quark TMDs beyond leading power in the correlation limit.

title: Three-dimensional assessment of toroidal heat-load distribution on divertor targets in EAST
abstract: Abstract Although actively cooled W/Cu monoblock targets are designed for high steady-state heat exhaust, local overheating and damage have been observed on these targets in EAST. These observations suggest that, beyond the nominal heat-removal capability, the practical thermal margin may be compromised by engineering alignment, target geometry and plasma operating conditions—all of which can alter the local surface-normal heat flux via modifications in magnetic incidence and magnetic shadowing. In this work, the toroidal distribution of the heat loads on the EAST divertor is analyzed by integrating infrared thermography, finite element heat flux inversion, and three-dimensional field-line tracing using PFCFlux. This analysis focuses on the effects of toroidal-field ripple, cassette misalignment in the presence of ripple, and divertor geometry. It is shown that the 16-fold toroidal field ripple can produce a 2 π / 16 modulation of the peak heat flux on the current upper outer divertor target, with a peak fluctuation amplitude of approximately 17.75 % . Under a peak heat flux constraint of Q safe = 10 MW m − 2 , the allowable average heat flux on the upper outer target (OT) decreases from 4.28 MW m − 2 in the absence of ripple to 3.94 MW m − 2 in the presence of ripple. When ripple and relative cassette misalignments are considered simultaneously for the same target, the allowable average heat flux is further reduced to 3.11 MW m − 2 , 2.79 MW m − 2 , and 2.27 MW m − 2 for Δ = 0.6 mm , 1.0 mm , and 3.0 mm , respectively. Compared with the present upper OT, the toroidally curved lower outer vertical target (OVT) has higher allowable average heat fluxes under both ripple-free and ripple conditions without cassette misalignment, with values of 7.00 and 5.98 MW m − 2 , respectively, compared with 4.28 and 3.94 MW m − 2 for the upper OT. Undertoroidal-field ripple and a Δ = 1 mm misalignment, the new upper horizontal target achieves a higher allowable average heat flux than the lower outer horizontal target (OHT), with values of 4.70 and 4.01 MW m − 2 , respectively. These results show that magnetic ripple, assembly tolerances, and toroidal geometric continuity must be considered in the thermal design of divertor targets in fusion devices.

title: The multiscale nonlinear interactions between kinetic ballooning mode and drift wave turbulence critical for confinement improvement of hybrid fusion plasmas
abstract: Abstract Nonlinear suppression of short-wavelength drift wave turbulence by long-wavelength kinetic ballooning mode (KBM) in tokamak fusion plasma is proposed to be the main cause for confinement improvement in the core of hybrid fusion plasmas. Specifically, the ambient ion temperature gradient (ITG) turbulence, which can contribute considerable transport flux if not mitigated, is fully suppressed in the presence of KBM. KBM is demonstrated to be robustly unstable from fully electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations. While its flux is low under low magnetic shear, KBM can generate significant stabilizing zonal flow whose velocity well surpasses the normalized linear growth rate (linear growth rate divided by its wave number) of ITG. This multiscale physics phenomenon is convincingly verified on a representative ASDEX-Upgrade hybrid scenario plasma.

title: System identification simulations using the advanced fluid neutral model and wide grid formalism in SOLPS-ITER
abstract: Abstract This work presents a first step towards using the SOLPS-ITER code package (Wiesen 2015 J. Nucl. Mater. 463 480–4) for synthetic system identification (SysID) using multisine perturbations. Numerical modelling is used to replicate SysID experiments performed to establish exhaust control done on MAST-U (Kool 2025 Nat. Energy 10 1116–31), (Van Berkel 2025 DPP 2025 (APS)). These experiments involve perturbing the gas injection rate and observing the Scrape-Off-Layer (SOL) response in the frequency domain. The model used is the Advanced Fluid Neutral (AFN) model of SOLPS-ITER (Horsten 2022 Nucl. Mater. Energy 33 101247), implemented in the Wide Grids version of the code (Dekeyser 2021 Nucl. Mater. Energy 27 100999). The grid was generated with the Grid Optimization and Adaptation Toolbox (Van den kerkhof 2024 Contrib. Plasma Phys. 64 e202300134) and extends to the vessel wall, to enable calculating fluid neutral parameters across the entire domain. New boundary condition types were implemented in the code to allow for multisine gas injection perturbations, as well as reservoir models for remote vessel regions without plasma. In steady state, it is possible to simulate plasmas ranging from attached to deeply detached using different gas injection rates. This allows for comparison between simulation and experimental results at similar levels of detachment. Comparison between simulation and experimental data in the frequency domain shows that the AFN SOLPS-ITER simulations predict faster response times to divertor fuelling perturbations than the experiments, likely in part due to the fluid approximation used for the neutrals. When including the reservoir models for remote vessel regions the phase shifts increase, but are still too low compared to experiments.

title: Semiparametric Estimation of Physics Parameters and Parton Distribution Functions
abstract: The simultaneous determination of Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and fundamental physical parameters, e.g. the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s$, the mass of the top quark $m_t$, or Wilson coefficients of an Effective Field Theory operators, is essential for the high-precision physics programme of the Large Hadron Collider. Yet, simultaneous global fits face significant methodological and computational challenges, rooted in the fundamental tension between estimating a finite-dimensional parameter and an infinite-dimensional function. In this paper, we address this problem by introducing a semiparametric estimation framework. The key advantage of our approach is that it avoids the need to refit the PDFs in the presence of either modified SM parameters or BSM contributions. Starting from standard, decoupled estimates of the PDFs and physics parameters, the method computes a bias correction a posteriori via the efficient influence function, yielding a debiased one-step estimator of the finite-dimensional parameter along with uncertainties with valid frequentist coverage. This correction rigorously accounts for the interplay between PDF and physics parameters without requiring a computationally expensive joint fit. As a proof of concept, we apply the method to two toy scenarios preparatory to a realistic global fit: the extraction of a dimension-six SMEFT Wilson coefficient from Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) pseudo-data based on BCDMS measurements, isolating the non-singlet PDF combination $T_3$, and to the determination of the proton total valence $V$ from combined HERA measurements. Our results demonstrate that the one-step estimator successfully removes the bias inherent in a preliminary, decoupled estimate and achieves confidence intervals with correct nominal coverage, offering a statistically rigorous and computationally efficient alternative to full simultaneous PDF fits.

title: Electromagnetic gyrokinetic analysis in Tokamak Energy’s pre-concept design of the ST-E1 fusion power plant
abstract: Abstract ST-E1 is Tokamak Energy’s concept for a fusion power plant. As part of the pre-concept design, a series of reference flat-top plasma operating points have been developed and analysed in [McNamara et al (2026 Nucl. Fusion 66 086008)]. The present work focuses on the low-density baseline conceptual power plant (BCP) operating point of [McNamara et al (2026 Nucl. Fusion 66 086008)] selected as a representative operating point for the ST-E1 pilot plant and investigates its micro-stability, turbulent transport and transport-informed optimisation using first-principles spectral flux-tube electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations. Linear gyrokinetic calculations, involving electrons, thermal ions, impurities, and thermal and fast helium ions, complemented by dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) to identify subdominant and stable drift-wave eigenmodes, reveal two principal long-wavelength electromagnetic instability branches: hybrid h-ITG modes driven by thermal gradients and FI-KBMs, i.e. kinetic-ballooning-like modes strongly influenced by the plasma beta (a ratio of thermal to magnetic energy) and the fast-ion (FI) population. At shorter wavelengths, electron-temperature-gradient (ETG) modes become unstable towards the plasma edge while remaining stable in the core. A comprehensive sensitivity analysis identifies the principal equilibrium parameters governing these instabilities. Building on these linear predictions, nonlinear electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations are performed to quantify the resulting turbulent transport of the thermal plasma and fast helium ions. The reference operating point is found to exhibit saturated, rather than runaway, electromagnetic turbulence, establishing it as a physically meaningful baseline for further optimisation. The nonlinear simulations show that turbulent transport is governed primarily by the combined effects of the plasma beta, safety factor and fast-ion fraction, with intrinsic-rotation-driven E × B shear providing an additional, complementary reduction in transport. Although fast ions provide the free energy driving the FI-KBM branch, increasing the fast-ion fraction is found to reduce the saturated turbulent transport across all species through nonlinear self-organisation. To efficiently explore the resulting multidimensional parameter space, defined by the plasma beta, safety factor and fast-ion fraction, a physics-informed interpolation framework constrained and validated by nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations has been developed, enabling the identification of transport-favourable operating points without requiring exhaustive nonlinear parameter scans. The resulting framework yields a family of transport-favourable operating points for the ST-E1 low-density BCP equilibrium and provides quantitative targets for future self-consistent equilibrium optimisation.

title: Comparative investigation of temperature-dependent defect evolution and irradiation hardening in CVD and ITER-like tungsten
abstract: Abstract Chemical vapor deposited tungsten (CVD-W) is known for its high thermal stability of the microstructure and lower susceptibility to deuterium-induced blistering compared to ITER-like W (IL-W). However, it remains unclear whether these advantages extend to displacement damage tolerance. To address this, CVD-W and ITER-like tungsten (IL-W) were irradiated with 6 MeV copper ions up to 0.6 dpa at room temperature (RT), 773 K, and 973 K. Transmission electron microscopy, defect statistics, and nano-indentation revealed comparable damage accumulation and irradiation hardening in both materials across all investigated temperatures. At RT, both materials exhibited dense dislocation networks and loops, together with very sparsely distributed voids, resulting in comparable increases in hardness. At elevated temperatures, these networks disappeared, giving way to dislocation loop strings and dislocation lines, along with an increased density of voids, accompanied by further irradiation hardening. The dispersed barrier hardening model analysis indicates that the dominant contribution to irradiation hardening transitions from dislocation structures at RT to voids at elevated temperatures. In addition, differences in dislocation morphology and nature were observed between the two materials. Displacement damage defects in CVD-W exhibited higher mobility than in IL-W, as evidenced by an expanded damage layer, a higher degree of dislocation loop ordering into one-dimensional strings, a larger fraction of glissile 1/2<111> dislocation loops, and a greater proportion of loops exceeding 10 nm at ≥ 773 K, mainly owing to its lower impurity content. This further supports void-dominated hardening at elevated temperatures, as different dislocation morphologies observed at elevated temperatures had minimal impact on the overall hardening. These findings provide valuable insights into the irradiation response of CVD-W under fusion-relevant conditions.

title: AI-Newton: A concept-driven physical law discovery system without prior physical knowledge
abstract: While current artificial intelligence (AI)-driven methods excel at deriving empirical models from individual experiments, a significant challenge remains in uncovering the common fundamental physics that underlie these models—a task at which human physicists are adept. To bridge this gap, we introduce AI-Newton, a framework for concept-driven scientific discovery. Our system autonomously derives general physical laws directly from raw, multiexperiment data, operating without supervision or prior physical knowledge. Its core innovations are twofold: (1) proposing interpretable physical concepts to construct laws and (2) progressively generalizing these laws to broader domains. Applied to a large, noisy dataset of mechanics experiments, AI-Newton successfully rediscovers foundational and universal laws, such as Newton's second law, the conservation of energy, and the universal gravitation. This work represents a proof-of-concept step toward autonomous, humanlike scientific discovery.

title: A fully electromagnetic hybrid PIC-fluid model for predictive fusion neutron yield in dense plasma focus
abstract: Abstract A fully electromagnetic hybrid ion-PIC/electron-fluid framework is developed for the implosion-to-pinch phase of dense plasma focus (DPF) discharges. Ions are advanced kinetically, electrons form a charge-neutralizing fluid under the quasi-neutral approximation, and the full Maxwell equations are solved in both plasma and vacuum. The generalized Ohm law includes resistive, electron pressure-gradient, and Hall terms. Applied to a non-hollow 180 kA geometry initialized from a pre-ionized end-of-rundown state, the framework reproduces the axial rundown, radial compression, and pinch stages. The sheath front trajectory agrees with fully kinetic benchmarks within 10%, and a pinch-radius comparison captures the radial collapse. A beam-target neutron diagnostic applied to the simulated ion distribution gives a yield of 0.296e7, at the same scale as the fully kinetic reference. The ion spectrum develops a non-Maxwellian suprathermal tail to about 0.25 MeV. The yield remains sensitive to the electron-temperature closure and anode geometry. The framework captures relevant macroscopic observables and ion-kinetic diagnostics at a computational cost roughly 1e5-1e6 times lower than comparable fully kinetic electromagnetic PIC simulations.

title: Updated analysis of charmonium states in a relativized quark potential model
abstract: Motivated by recent experimental observations of charmonium(like) states, we investigate their interpretation as conventional charmonium states within the framework of relativized quark potential model. We find a consistent description of the updated masses of charmonium, bottomonium and some selected charmed mesons, then systematically compute open-charm strong decay widths and electromagnetic transition widths for radially excited charmonium states up to n = 5 . The numerical results show significantly improved agreement with experimental masses and widths. Notably, the newly observed χ c 1 ( 4010 ) and χ c 1 ( 4274 ) are tentatively associated with the χ c 1 ( 2 P ) and χ c 1 ( 3 P ) , respectively, while the χ c 0 ( 4500 ) and χ c 0 ( 4700 ) are interpreted as the χ c 0 ( 4 P ) and χ c 0 ( 5 P ) states. For the controversial χ c 1 ( 3872 ) state, we suggest its potential connection to χ c 1 ( 4010 ) , as a two-pole structure due to the χ c 1 ( 2 P ) coupling to D D ¯ * channels. Intriguingly, the predicted mass of χ c 0 ( 2 P ) is about 3851 MeV, diverging from the original estimate of 3916 MeV in the Godfrey and Isgur’s work but consistent with nonrelativistic potential model predictions. This calculation might provide more insight to the future experimental investigation of charmonium(like) states.

title: Tensor-polarized parton distribution functions of the deuteron by a convolution model
abstract: Tensor-polarized parton distribution functions (PDFs) are calculated for the deuteron by using a convolution formalism, where the tensor-polarized PDFs are given by the corresponding nucleon's unpolarized PDFs convoluted with the tensor-polarized nucleon momentum distribution in the deuteron. These distributions are obtained at $Q^2=2.5$ GeV$^2$ in order to compare with the tensor-polarized PDFs which were determined by HERMES $b_1$ data. The obtained distributions are very different from the ones determined from the HERMES data, which indicates further studies are needed to clarify the difference, possibly by considering a new mechanism beyond the simple bound system of a proton and a neutron. The obtained PDFs $\delta_T q $ and $\delta_T \bar q$ are converted to the PDFs of the Trento convention $f_{1LL}^{\, q}$ and $f_{1LL}^{\, \bar q}$, and they are used for estimating the twist-3 PDFs $f_{LT}^{\, q}$ and $f_{LT}^{\, \bar q}$ by using a Wandzura-Wilczek-like relation. Because deep-inelastic-scattering experiments are under preparation for structure functions with a tensor-polarized deuteron target at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility, and a Drell-Yan experiment will be possible at hadron accelerator facilities, such as the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, the obtained tensor-polarized PDFs will be tested experimentally.

title: Static quark-antiquark interactions in rotating SU(3) gluodynamics
abstract: We study static quark-antiquark interactions in rotating SU(3) gluodynamics using quenched lattice simulations at imaginary angular velocity. At zero temperature, we extract the static potential from Wilson loops for quark-antiquark pairs aligned with the rotation axis, for transverse pairs with one source on the rotation axis, and for symmetric transverse pairs across the rotation axis. Within the present accuracy, no significant rotation dependence or anisotropy is observed in the zero-temperature potential. At finite temperature, imaginary rotation suppresses the color-averaged free energies obtained from Polyakov-loop correlators in both longitudinal and transverse geometries. Axial-diagonal comparisons are used to identify a bulk region where open-boundary artifacts are reduced. In this region, the large-distance longitudinal free-energy shift is well described by Δ F z ( R x y ) = A R x y 2 + B . The transverse channels exhibit the same qualitative suppression, while their distance dependence additionally reflects the radial arrangement of the static sources and is compatible with a radial single-source free-energy shift in the bulk region. For the finite-temperature observables studied above T c , the response weakens as the temperature is increased. These results provide lattice evidence for a position- and geometry-dependent response of bare static-source free energies to imaginary rotation in a gluonic medium.

title: Quantum simulation of bottomonium dynamics in the quark–gluon plasma via the Lindblad equation
abstract: Abstract Quantum computing provides a powerful framework for simulating real-time dynamics in open quantum systems, offering key advantages for modeling heavy-quarkonium transport in high-energy nuclear collisions. In this work, we perform quantum simulations of the isotropic next-to-leading-order Lindblad equation for bottomonium in the quark-gluon plasma using a reduced spherical coordinate representation. We discretize operators and wavefunctions, map the physical state onto qubits, and execute time evolution via parameterized quantum gate operations. By extracting the Υ(1S) survival probability, we quantitatively isolate the color-octet contribution to the correlated regeneration of the bottomonium ground state, demonstrating that its overall impact is small in the final production of the bottomonium ground state Υ(1S) in the hot QCD medium at temperatures accessible at the Large Hadron Collider. Additionally, we have further optimized the quantum simulation algorithm for the Lindblad equation. The improved algorithm requires only a single ancillary qubit to realize the Lindblad evolution, thereby minimizing the circuit significantly.

title: Positron Emission Tomography with quantum-entangled Compton events: first imaging results at clinically relevant activities
abstract: In Positron Emission Tomography, a potential, yet unutilized enhancement, may come from exploiting the quantum entanglement of the annihilation quanta, inscribed in the correlation of their polarizations. To investigate this, we built a PET demonstrator capable of measuring polarization correlations of annihilation quanta by their Compton scattering, based on single-layer scintillator polarimeters. We present a detailed study of the imaging of two $^{68}$Ge line sources, 45 MBq each, to extract the spatial resolution and assess image quality. The results show that a spatial resolution of 2.5$\pm$0.1 mm is obtained using single-pixel events, while resolutions obtained with polarization-correlated Compton events range from 3.6$\pm$0.3 mm to 4.9$\pm$0.3 mm, depending on data selection criteria. We also found that the polarization-correlated Compton events exhibit up to 20% higher average signal to random background ratio compared to the single-pixel events. We also present the first imaging of the NEMA NU-4 phantom filled with a $^{68}$Ga solution of 378 MBq initial activity, successfully combining polarization-correlated events with conventional single-pixel event selection. Based on the extracted spatial resolution, signal-to-background, signal-to-noise, contrast, and contrast-to-noise ratio, we estimate that up to 10% sensitivity increase may be attained by exploiting the polarization-correlated events, while preserving a high image quality.

title: Bayesian inference of moments of inertia for wobbling motion in Pr 135
Search for active-sterile neutrino transitions using Pierre Auger Observatory data
Residual AM and PM Noise of Selected X-Band Amplifiers
abstract: In microwave systems design, amplitude modulation (AM) noise is often ignored relative to phase modulation (PM) noise. However, in high-performance applications requiring ultra-low PM noise, AM noise becomes a critical limiting factor due to AM-to-PM conversion mechanisms. Because AM noise specifications are rarely, if ever, provided for commercial microwave components, this study characterizes the residual AM and PM noise of several 10 GHz amplifiers. We present performance data for various Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) amplifier designs and demonstrate the noise reduction achieved through power-summed configurations. For example, a discrete-die GaAs HBT amplifier achieves residual PM noise below $-160$ dBrad$^2$/Hz and AM noise of approximately $-155$ dB/Hz at a 1 kHz offset in a quad power-summed configuration. A notable finding is that the majority of amplifier designs surveyed in this study exhibit higher AM noise relative to their PM noise, with only a few exceptions. The impact of bias supply quality on residual noise is also quantified, demonstrating that the choice of voltage regulator is a first-order design parameter below 1 kHz offset.

title: On the Electrodynamics of a Non-Contact Inductive Sensor for High-Accuracy Tip Deflection Measurements of Piezoceramic Bending Actuators and its Application for Energy Harvesting Purposes
abstract: Piezoelectric bending actuators provide deflections of several hundred micrometers and are used in electrical and mechanical engineering, acoustics, automation, automotive technology and healthcare. Highly efficient, low-cost piezoceramics offer a wide range of technical solutions. Their highpiezoelectric coefficients enable large strains at low electric field strengths. However, hysteresis, drift and creep impair positioning accuracy. Precise switching and positioning require compensation for these material-related effects, as well as varying mechanical loads and vibrations. A non-contact inductive proximity sensor is therefore combined with high-precision electronic circuit. Within a closed-loop control system, this sensor-actuator arrangement detects disturbances and enables their compensation, allowing highly efficient piezoceramics to be used for high-accuracy positioning. This paper investigates the electrodynamics of a specially developed eddy-current-based proximity sensor suitable for integration into confined spaces. A theoretical description explains its physical operating principle and enables analytical determination of the relative change in inductance as a function of actuator tip deflection. Experimental measurements validate the electrodynamic approach. The paper also considers energy harvesting applications. Measuring tip deflection allows the power dissipated in the piezoelectric transducer to be determined. The sensor system thus provides a basis for investigating and evaluating the performance of piezoelectric energy harvesters.

title: Nucleon effective mass in neutron stars cooling
In-situ azimuthal sample rotation within a horizontal-field cryomagnet for small-angle neutron scattering
abstract: We present an in-situ azimuthal rotation stage for small-angle neutron scattering measurements. The stage provides an azimuthal rotation range of $315^\circ$ about the stage normal. At the reference sample-stick orientation, the stage normal is parallel to the incident neutron beam, so that the sample rotates in the plane perpendicular to the beam. Combined with a sample stick rotation about a second, orthogonal axis, the stage provides control of the magnetic-field direction relative to the crystal axes, while the field remains fixed in the laboratory frame. For a 5 mm diameter incident beam, sample-stick rotations of approximately $\pm315^\circ$ are accessible with negligible additional attenuation from the holder. The commercial rotator is specified for operation between 1 and 373 K and in magnetic fields up to 35 T, making the stage nominally compatible with the full temperature (1.8 to 320 K) and field (0 to 6.8 T) ranges of the used cryomagnet. As a working example, we characterize its performance on a spherical single crystal of MnSi between 20 and 35 K and in fields up to 183 mT, observing local sample heating during operation of $\sim$20 mK per $5^\circ$ step. We illustrate the design considerations behind the holder construction, with specific notes for mounting spherical samples, and discuss the resulting performance and limitations.

title: Characterization of immersed SiPM arrays in liquid scintillator between room temperature and $-30\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$
abstract: Liquid scintillator detectors instrumented with distributed silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) arrays can be used in compact, topology-sensitive, and low-background experiments, but the temperature dependence of SiPMs immersed directly in the scintillation medium has not been widely characterized. We report the operation of a 125-liter linear-alkylbenzene-based liquid scintillator detector read out by 125 SiPM channels immersed in the active volume, over the range from room temperature to $-30\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The detector response was measured with cosmic-ray muons, including stopping muons followed by their Michel-electron decay. Cooling from $+15\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $-30\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ reduced the SiPM dark-count rate by a factor of 13.5, increased the single-photoelectron response by 49.1%, and increased the cosmic-ray muon light yield by 16.7%. The improved photoelectron separation and baseline stability at low temperature enabled a selection of stopping-muon events, from which the effective muon lifetime was measured to be $1959\pm132\,\mathrm{ns}$, consistent with the value expected for a hydrocarbon scintillator once $\mu^{-}$ capture on carbon is taken into account.

title: Structural quasi-universality in highly magnetized, differentially rotating neutron stars
abstract: Context. Universal relations among macroscopic properties of neutron stars provide a powerful framework to probe their internal structures while minimizing uncertainties associated with the equation of state (EoS). Although such relations have been extensively studied for uniformly rotating stars, their extension to differentially rotating and strongly magnetized configurations has been explored less. Aims. We aim to investigate whether it is possible to obtain a phenomenological, quasi-universal relation between moment of inertia and stellar compactness for differentially rotating, strongly magnetized neutron stars modeled with nuclear EoSs. Methods. We systematically investigated equilibrium configurations for a wide range of EoSs, rotation profiles, and magnetic-field strengths with the XNS numerical simulation code. For sequences with fixed angular momentum, we analyzed the dependence of the normalized moment of inertia on compactness. Results. We establish a generalized, quasi-universal relation between the moment of inertia and the compactness that remains remarkably insensitive to the underlying EoS across uniformly rotating, differentially rotating, and strongly magnetized toroidal configurations. For sequences with fixed angular momentum, the normalized moment of inertia exhibits a quasi-universal dependence on compactness, with deviations primarily due to the magnetic-field strength and degree of differential rotation. We derive analytic expressions for these dependencies, enabling a unified phenomenological model applicable over a wide range of stellar configurations. As astrophysical applications, we quantify the systematic bias in magnetar luminosity estimates and the rotational kinetic energy of post-merger remnant of GW170817. Conclusions. These results extend quasi-universal relations beyond the standard assumptions of uniform rotation and weak magnetization, providing a robust framework for interpreting observations of highly magnetized and differentially rotating neutron stars and enabling more reliable constraints on their astrophysical properties.

title: Nonlinear dynamics induced by strong radio-frequency fields in ReBCO high temperature superconductors
Low-$Q^{2}$ nucleon structure from an infrared-saturated evolution scheme
abstract: Abstract The low-$Q^2$ nucleon structure is given with a simple nonperturbative input of three valence quarks and an all-order infrared-saturated evolution scheme, showing some consistencies with the experimental data. The resonance peaks in the experimental data of $F_2$ structure function are found to be modulated by the valence quark distributions. With little sea quark distributions at low $Q^2$, the valence-quark bump is clearly shown in the structure function. The three valence quark distributions at the hadronic scale is found to be the dominant origin of the PDFs at the hard scales. The high-twist corrections are needed to explain the sizeable discrepancy between the theory and the experimental measurements at low $Q^2$. The infrared-saturated evolution scheme is a powerful tool for connecting the nucleon structures in the nonperturbative and perturbative regions.

title: Impact of electromagnetic showers on the Diamond-II permanent magnet dipoles
Image-catalog complementarity in quasar-galaxy ambiguous regimes of photometric source classification
abstract: Abstract The photometric separation of stars, galaxies, and quasars is important for large imaging surveys, but quasar–galaxy ambiguity remains challenging when colors and optical appearances overlap. We present a rule-guided image–catalog fusion analysis to identify regimes in which optical image cutouts provide complementary information to catalog features. The study uses a balanced medium-hard benchmark of 12 000 spectroscopically labeled sources combining SDSS labels, Legacy Survey measurements, WISE variability, Gaia features, and optical cutouts. We compare catalog ensemble models, a ConvNeXt image classifier, and probability-level image–catalog fusion in quasar–galaxy ambiguous regimes. These regimes are selected using local color-space overlap from training-set nearest-neighbor class probabilities and a label-free catalog-uncertainty score from a reference catalog classifier. In the rule-selected color-overlap and high-uncertainty regimes, fusion reaches macro-F1 scores of 0.643–0.696, improving catalog-only baselines by 2.6–3.1 percentage points. The quasar F1 score increases in all three fixed ambiguous subsets, and fusion corrects more catalog errors than it introduces without increasing quasar–galaxy confusion. With validation and test sets fixed, increasing the image-training set from 8 400 to 84 000 sources raises image-only macro-F1 from 0.7486 to 0.7856. Ablation tests, nearest-neighbor-scale tests, threshold sensitivity analyses, and bootstrap resampling associate these gains with the joint selection of local color mixing and catalog uncertainty. The results provide evidence for a modest positive trend, suggesting that optical cutouts may be particularly useful for sources that are both locally mixed in color space and uncertain under catalog-only prediction.

title: Holographic light-quark energy loss in a spinning plasma
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate light-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled plasma described by a spinning black-brane background obtained from the large-black-hole limit of the Myers--Perry geometry. The parameter $a$ characterizes the boost/rotation of the dual fluid in this holographic setup and is related to the angular velocity in the corresponding limit. We employ two complementary probes, the falling-string and shooting-string descriptions, to compute the stopping distance and the instantaneous energy loss of a light quark moving either transverse or parallel to the rotation axis. The results show that light quarks thermalize more readily in a hot environment. For parallel propagation, a counter-propagating configuration facilitates thermalization, whereas a co-propagating configuration suppresses it. For transverse propagation, increasing the magnitude of the rotational motion promotes thermalization. In addition, the instantaneous energy loss increases along the trajectory of the endpoint. title: Form-factor-constrained non-factorized transition-GPD tomography of N → Δ ( 1232 ) multipole structure
abstract: Abstract A form-factor-constrained non-factorized transition-GPD reconstruction is developed for the N → Δ ( 1232 ) electromagnetic transition. The production input consists of the published CLAS magnetic multipole amplitude and electric and scalar/Coulomb quadrupole ratios. Additional external low- Q 2 ratio data are retained only as a separate ratio-sector diagnostic. The electroproduction quantities are propagated replica by replica and converted to the dimensionless Jones–Scadron transition form factors G M ∗ , G E ∗ , and G C ∗ . AICc model selection yields a modified dipole for G M ∗ , a dipole for G E ∗ , and a cubic z expansion for G C ∗ . These fits define the imposed positive- x normalization F α ( t ) = 2 G α ∗ ( − t ) for factorized, correlated exponential, Regge-like, and double-distribution-inspired transition-GPD profiles. The upper boundary of the impact-parameter transform is fixed by the largest measured absolute-form-factor point, Q 2 = 6 GeV 2 , so that no high- Q 2 continuation beyond the measured range enters the production reconstruction. The primary transverse localization observable is therefore defined from the small- Q 2 slope of the modeled transition GPD, with finite-window radial moments retained only as secondary core-shape diagnostics. For the slope-defined width, the transition form factor contributes an x -independent channel-dependent offset, while the entire x dependence is fixed by the chosen longitudinal–transverse profile ansatz. The factorized profile is x -independent and the three non-factorized families generate distinct modeled x dependences. The resulting reconstruction separates measured transition-form-factor information from model-dependent longitudinal structure and provides a controlled framework for assessing structural and covariance sensitivity in N → Δ ( 1232 ) transition tomography.

title: Fast kicker development and test in ESRF-EBS and SLS 2.0
Detecting seven new glitches in PSR J1341−6220 using six-year timing observations from the Parkes 64 m radio telescope
abstract: Aims. This paper aims to report seven newly detected glitches in pulsar (PSR) J1341−6220 from six-year timing observations of the Parkes 64 m radio telescope, and to conduct a detailed analysis of the post-glitch recovery processes via Bayesian methods and the vortex creep model. Methods. We used six-year (MJD 58222–60589) timing observations obtained from the Parkes 64 m radio telescope to search for glitches and study the rotational evolution of PSR J1341−6220. We measured the key parameters of the detected glitches and examined their temporal distribution and recovery behaviours. Bayesian analysis and the vortex creep model were used to quantitatively study glitches with sufficient post-glitch data and interpret the delayed spin-down rate increase as the response of inward-moving vortices transported by crustquake-driven platelet motion. We further evaluated the relative decrease in moment of inertia assuming starquake-driven glitches, and compared the result with standard neutron star structure models. Results. We detected seven new glitches (G36–G42) for PSR J1341−6220. Reliable parameters are successfully measured for five of these glitches (G36 and G39–G42), with Δ ν / ν from 136.4 × 10 −9 to 953.4 × 10 −9 and Δ ν ˙/ ν ˙ from 0.36 × 10 −3 to 1.57 × 10 −3 . The intervals between successive glitches range from 149 to 579 days and show no significant periodicity. None of these glitches exhibits definite exponential or linear recovery behaviour, but instead show a pronounced non-linear recovery process. Unidentified small-amplitude glitches may exist between the two unconstrained glitches G37 and G38, and a possible overshoot is observed in the recovery of G41. We performed a Bayesian analysis of glitches G39–G42 with the vortex creep model. G36 was excluded from the vortex-creep modelling because of insufficient post-glitch data. The model reproduces the observations well and indicates that non-linear responses dominate the post-glitch recovery. For G40 and G41, inward vortex motion is invoked to explain the delayed spin-down rate increase after the glitches.

title: Coherent γ -ray generation by partially stripped ion beams
Clock–WEP tests of string-derived dilaton and modulus sectors
abstract: Abstract String compactifications and runaway-dilaton models can contain light scalar directions. Motion along these directions changes gauge couplings, the QCD scale, quark masses, and Yukawa parameters. A given string-derived sector then predicts low-energy slopes. Its gauge kinetic functions, matter-metric or Yukawa slopes, source charge, scalar trajectory, and scalar range determine a Damour–Donoghue weak-equivalence-principle (WEP) vector and a clock-drift vector. The analysis uses this map to compare such sectors with WEP and clock data. The numerical fit assumes one effective long-range scalar, or an aligned direction in a multi-field space. With that assumption, WEP tests and secular clock drifts probe related projections of the same scalar-slope vector. The minimal two-charge Damour–Donoghue fit uses Ti–Pt MICROSCOPE, Be–Ti torsion-balance, and 85 Rb– 87 Rb atom-interferometer data, then adds the Yb + 10 3 / 10 2 secular α -drift row. The WEP-only fit gives D m ^ = ( − 6.06 ± 34.91 ) × 10 − 12 and D e = ( 8.80 ± 46.46 ) × 10 − 12 , with correlation − 0.99958 . The clock input is α ˙ / α = 1.0 ( 1.1 ) × 10 − 18 yr − 1 . It matches the WEP marginal reach when | ζ | = 2.37 × 10 − 8 yr − 1 , with ζ = φ ˙ / α E . For the benchmark φ ˙ = ξ H 0 and α E = 10 − 3 α 0 , this gives ξ / α 0 ≃ 0.34 . This value marks equal information between the clock row and the WEP marginal constraint. A model becomes testable after it supplies r = D m ^ / D e , the scalar amplitude, and ζ . As an example, the Damour–Piazza–Veneziano runaway-dilaton estimate lies near η ∼ 10 − 12 for order-unity n = 2 parameters, well above the MICROSCOPE-level WEP scale. In the representative-isotope two-charge model, a MICROSCOPE-level Be–Ti-like row would reduce the long WEP axis by a factor 27.8 ; a repeated Ti–Pt-like row would barely change it. The calculation tests compactification-level predictions for string-derived dilaton or modulus sectors after the model supplies its low-energy data.

title: Analysis of beam loss induced by longitudinal parametric resonance in a heavy ion synchrotron
Can multi-level Monte-Carlo address the sign problem in a finite-density Bose gas?
abstract: Numerical simulation of field theories with complex actions is frustrated by the sign problem, which causes an exponential growth in statistical sampling noise. A key example of such a theory is QCD at finite baryon chemical potential, which has important applications to the structure of atomic nuclei and neutron stars. Until now, the sign problem has precluded the possibility of first-principles numerical calculations that could provide key insight into these important physical systems. In this work, we propose an approach to avoiding this limitation by applying a reweighting procedure coupled with a multi-level Monte-Carlo sampling algorithm that offers an exponential enhancement of statistics to counteract the sign problem. We test the approach on a simpler model that displays the same sign problem at finite chemical potential. Our results demonstrate the promise of the proposed approach, significantly increasing the range over which precise calculations are possible, and providing improvements all the way up to the phase transition.

title: Study of enhancing the signal-background separation for the Higgs boson production in association with a single top-quark in $pp$ collisions at the LHC
abstract: In this paper, a multivariate analysis based approach for enhancing the extraction of the rare Standard Model (SM) process being studied - Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH) - from the prevailing background processes is presented. The analysis was performed using a Monte Carlo generated dataset simulating the outcomes of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). A deep fully connected neural network was developed for signal-background discrimination, incorporating a masking mechanism designed to suppress the contribution of input variables associated with objects that were not reconstructed in a given event. The performance of the masked architecture was evaluated on independent Monte Carlo samples. The results of the proposed methodology are compared with a conventional cut-based approach in terms of the statistical significance of the tH production channel. The developed framework was tested using a simulated dataset corresponding approximately to the combined statistical samples of LHC Runs 1, 2, and 3.

title: The Late-time Afterglow of GW170817 and Implications for Jet Dynamics
abstract: GW170817 is the first binary neutron star merger detected with gravitational and electromagnetic waves, and its afterglow is still detectable 7 years post-merger. Some previous studies of the X-ray afterglow have claimed the onset of a new afterglow component or raised concerns about the data processing techniques. Motivated thus, we present here a reanalysis of X-ray afterglow data for GW170817 and find potential sources of discrepancies between the data reduction techniques employed by various research groups. We also analyze the updated panchromatic afterglow data to find that there is no significant evidence for any new afterglow component (e.g. due to the ejecta that gave rise to the kilonova) and that the jet must be still in a mildly relativistic phase. The decline in the afterglow light curve is significantly shallower compared to that expected from the standard synchrotron afterglow jet models with sideways spreading, indicating either an additional energy injection at late times or the velocity dependence on the microphysics parameters. In this context, we discuss the implications of the late time afterglow data on jet dynamics.

title: Optimization of ARC-like tokamak stationary operation via core plasma composition and boundary shaping
abstract: Abstract Impurity composition, plasma shape, and pedestal density all provide strong levers on fusion power. Here, we explore the ways in which their variation changes fusion power and seek to find the optimum of these parameters. The key impacts of these variables are through changes in the core turbulent transport, the density of the fuel species, the pedestal pressure, and the plasma volume. ITG stabilization due to increased amounts of impurities is observed. The dependence of all of these parameters on the pedestal pressure is especially complicated because of the separate impacts on the peeling and ballooning modes, which can each limit the pedestal. Optimization of this multidimensional operating space is enabled by the use of Bayesian optimization, resulting in an operating point similar to ARC V3A with ∼ 30% more fusion power and a higher fusion power density. Increased shaping parameters, including elongation, triangularity, and squareness are all beneficial, as is high Z eff . When elongation is also allowed to vary, a ∼ 65% increase in fusion power can be achieved. While not commonly considered, we find squareness is an important lever on fusion power. The workflow developed here and demonstrated with the example of ARC V3A can readily be applied to other tokamak designs.

title: First transport study of Li and Sn for COMPASS Upgrade tokamak
abstract: Abstract One of the principal research objectives of the COMPASS Upgrade (COMPASS-U) tokamak under construction in Prague is the investigation of reliable long-term plasma power exhaust solutions for future fusion reactors. Owing to its unique operational parameters, including magnetic field of 5 T, plasma current of 2 MA, divertor plasma densities exceeding 10 21 m -3 , and a tungsten first wall, COMPASS-U is expected to generate divertor surface-normal heat fluxes of several tens of MW/m 2 , relevant to future DEMO-class reactors, in 1–10 s discharges. Prototype liquid metal (LM) divertor tiles based on lithium (Li), tin (Sn), and their alloys will be experimentally tested. To support these experiments and enable extrapolation to larger devices, transport of sputtered and vaporized LMs was simulated using the ERO2.0 code. LM erosion was evaluated with HeatLMD, LM transport inside the separatrix with Aurora, and the stationary plasma background was obtained from narrow-grid SOLPS-ITER simulations complemented by METIS.For two COMPASS-U operational scenarios, the high-performance case #5400 and the ITER-like case #24300, the upper limits of acceptable confined-plasma contamination by LMs in the fully toroidal lower outer LM divertor case were assessed. The corresponding volume-averaged impurity concentrations were estimated as 14; 21 % (meaning 14 % and 21 % for scenarios #5400 and #24300, respectively) for Li, and 10 −5 ; 10 −4 % for Sn. The associated radiation losses from the confined plasma were estimated as 5; 9 % of the input power for Li, while remaining negligible for Sn. These estimates do not include the effects of edge-localized modes (ELMs), which will be investigated in future work. They also neglect Sn spitting, which may increase the risk of plasma disruptions unless Sn droplet transport is sufficiently suppressed by divertor design, and the possibility of runaway Li self-sputtering under conditions of thermally enhanced erosion yield exceeding unity combined with strong redeposition.

title: Design of a radio-frequency photoinjector for generating relativistic vortex electron beams
abstract: We present the design and an analysis of the classical and quantum beam dynamics for an S-band radio-frequency (RF) photoinjector dedicated to the generation of relativistic vortex electron beams carrying a quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). The field-map-based tracking simulations were performed in the ultra-low bunch charge regime ($Q = 0.63$ pC), where space-charge effects are strongly suppressed. We demonstrate that optimizing the injection phase and solenoidal focusing preserves the intrinsic thermal limit of the photoemission source, yielding a stable, emittance-compensated beam with a final kinetic energy of 4.9 MeV and a normalized transverse emittance of $56\,\pi\,\mu\mathrm{m}\cdot\mathrm{mrad}$. Furthermore, our quantum-mechanical analysis of single-electron Laguerre-Gaussian wave packets inside the designed accelerating fields reveals that rapid energy gain suppresses transverse quantum spreading by nearly three orders of magnitude compared to free-space propagation. This suppression protects the characteristic OAM-dependent spatial structure of the wave packet. These results establish the beam-dynamics operating regime and vacuum conditions required for subsequent experiments on the generation and transport of relativistic vortex electron beams.

title: Unitary $KK$ and $K\pi$ inputs for an amplitude analysis of the $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$ decay
abstract: Charge-Parity Violation (CPV) is expected in three-body charm decays. In particular, in the singly Cabibbo suppressed decay process $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$; in which an amplitude analysis is required to understand the dynamics of Final State Interactions (FSI) and the mechanism that can generate CPV. In this work, we show the prospects of analysing recent data from the Large Hadron Collider beauty (LHCb) experiment at CERN, with a precise theoretical model expected to reveal CPV mechanisms. Previous analyses of the $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$ decay were unable to satisfactorily describe the data using the Isobar Model. Currently, LHCb has a sample of charmed meson decays with around 100 million events for the $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$ decay, so a more robust phenomenological model is needed to describe such a large data set. The present model has allowed the inclusion of hadronic FSI and will, in prospect, introduce three-body effects, overcoming some limitations of the Isobar Model, and has all factors necessary to reveal the presence of CPV. To do so, it factorizes the weak vertex separated in leading topologies and relies on extensions of Resonant Chiral Perturbation Theory to describe FSI. As a proof-of-concept, a toy dataset of the S-wave of the most recent amplitude analysis of $D^+ \to K^-K^+\pi^+$, by the CLEO-c collaboration, was fitted with this model. From fits to model-independent parametrizations of scattering amplitudes, the parameters of the FSI amplitudes were fixed, and the production parameters of the weak vertex were then obtained from the fit to the toy dataset, yielding a good agreement between the data and our model.

title: Searching for Long-Lived Dark Scalars with MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 at the HL-LHC
abstract: Feebly interacting particles (FIPs) arise generically in dark-sector extensions of the Standard Model (SM). Among the simplest and most theoretically motivated such candidates is a dark scalar that mixes with the SM Higgs boson, acting as a mediator between the dark sector and the SM. For sufficiently small mixing, such a dark scalar manifests at collider experiments as a long-lived particle with a macroscopic decay length---a signature to which conventional general-purpose detectors have limited sensitivity. The MoEDAL-MAPP experiment is a dedicated search facility at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) targeting long-lived FIPs as avatars of physics beyond the SM. We present $95\%$ confidence-level background-free sensitivity projections for the MAPP-1 and MAPP-2 detectors at the High-Luminosity LHC to Higgs-portal dark scalars produced via rare $B$-meson decays and exotic Higgs boson decays. Our results establish the proposed MAPP-2 detector as a complementary probe of feebly-coupled dark scalars, with sensitivity to lifetimes beyond the reach of existing collider searches.

title: Search for anomalies in vector-boson fusion production of the Higgs boson in $H(\rightarrow \gamma\gamma) jj$ events using 164 fb$^{-1}$ of $pp$ collision data collected at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
abstract: This article details two studies of Higgs boson properties using the vector-boson fusion production mode and the $\gamma\gamma jj$ final state. Both efforts are based on a data sample corresponding to 164 fb$^{-1}$ of $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV proton--proton collisions recorded by the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. The first study employs matrix-element-based optimal observables to constrain CP-odd couplings beyond the Standard Model within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory framework, expressed in the Warsaw basis. The second study exploits angular distributions to probe the Higgs boson's couplings to longitudinally and transversely polarised $W$ and $Z$ bosons in the production of the Higgs boson. To maximise the sensitivity, the constraints of the CP-odd couplings are combined with those from a previous analysis performed in $\gamma\gamma jj$ events in a data sample of proton--proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$^{-1}$. A significant improvement with respect to the previous analysis is achieved through the implementation of a new neural-network-based classification algorithm. All measurements are in agreement with the Standard Model prediction of a CP-even Higgs boson with the expected relative coupling strengths to longitudinally and transversely polarised vector bosons.

title: Probing the Spatial Coherence of Chiral-Imbalance Fluctuations with Hyperon Spin Correlations
abstract: Topological fluctuations in the quark-gluon plasma can generate local chiral imbalances whose spatial coherence remains difficult to access with conventional charge-separation measurements. We propose differential hyperon-pair spin correlations as a probe of both the strength and spatial organization of these fluctuations. Fluctuations of the axial chemical potential $\mu_5$ can induce pair correlations even when the mean helicity polarization vanishes. Using the AMPT model, we find that the magnitude of the hyperon spin correlation probes the magnitude and spatial coherence scale of $\mu_5$, while the ratio of short- and long-range correlations varies strongly with the spatial coherence scale, but only weakly with $\mu_{5}$ over the range of explored parameters. These observables provide an experimentally testable strategy for constraining the spatial structure of chiral-imbalance fluctuations.

title: Light Mediators at the Neutrino-Dark Matter Frontier: Coherent Scattering, Precision Constraints, and Complementary Searches
abstract: Low-threshold neutrino and dark-matter experiments constrain light mediators through different momentum transfers, targets, and coupling combinations. We examine scalar and vector interactions in coherent neutrino--nucleus scattering, neutrino--electron scattering, and dark-matter direct detection. Three representative interaction models are used to compare recoil spectra and coupling degeneracies. For $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ and $^{131}\mathrm{Xe}$, the nuclear-charge response matrix has a condition number of approximately 115, so two different targets may still leave nearly parallel blind directions. An analytic profile-likelihood calculation shows how spectral overlap and uncertainties in neutrino interactions affect dark-matter discovery sensitivity in the neutrino fog. We discuss the implications of measurements from COHERENT, CONUS+, LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T and specify which theoretical inputs, detector responses, and statistical correlations are needed to combine their constraints. keyword : coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering; light mediators; neutrino--electron scattering; dark matter direct detection; non-standard interactions; solar neutrinos; complementarity

title: Theoretical studies of envelope oscillations and instabilities of mismatched intense charged-particle beams in periodic focusing channels
abstract: The behavior of mismatched intense charged-particle beams in periodic transport channels of the solenoid and quadrupole type is studied theoretically. The envelope-oscillation frequencies of the mismatched beam are obtained by the smooth-approximation method and by numerical evaluation of the linearly perturbed K-V envelope equations. Phase shifts of the envelope oscillations and growth factors per focusing period in the case of instability are calculated for a solenoid and a magnetic quadrupole (FODO) channel using the parameters of the Maryland and GSI beam transport experiments. For comparison and the purpose of illustration, the K-V equations are integrated numerically, and envelope curves as well as single-particle trajectories for mismatched beams are shown in graphical form. In addition, computer simulation studies with the PARMILA code were performed, and results are presented both for K-V and a Gaussian distribution in transverse phase space.\\~\\ Revised version of: Particle~Accelerators~{\bf 14}, 227--260 (1984)}

title: The problem of self-consistent particle phase space distributions for periodic focusing channels
abstract: Charged particle beams in equilibrium with their collective fields are represented by self-consistent phase space distributions. As the starting point, we assume the external focusing forces to act continuously on the beam. In the collisionless mean-field approximation, a broad class of stationary self-consistent particle phase space distributions can then be constructed. The method is reviewed how to determine the single-particle Hamiltonian of the focusing system for a given phase space density function. Subsequently, canonical transformations are used to relate this description to a beam passing through a non-continuous transport system. The correspondence is exact for the linear K-V model and provides an approximate matching prescription for distributions with nonlinear space-charge forces. The transverse Hamiltonian generally changes with the focusing strength, including in a rotationally symmetric periodic solenoid channel. Our computer simulations, presented in the second part of the paper, indicate very small rms-emittance changes for appropriately matched beams in the continuous and periodic solenoid channels investigated. The simulation for a periodic quadrupole channel yields a small persistent increase of the rms-emittance, whose physical interpretation requires control of numerical errors. Revised version of: Particle~Accelerators 39, 219--249 (1992)}

title: QCD Axion Conversion in Magnetospheres of Neutron Stars
abstract: The axion-converted-photons flux plays a key role in searches of QCD axions as a dark matter (DM) candidate. In addition to solving the strong CP problem, these may explain the properties of the mysterious DM. Neutron star (NS) cooling by neutrino/axion emissions rate constrains the astrophysical properties of superdense matter. We attempt to analyse the impact of strong magnetic fields on the emission properties of axions by employing the APR, FPS, and SLY equation of State (EoS). We modify the Tolman Oppenheimer Volkoff (TOV) equations by considering effects of strong fields' and generate profiles. We assume Cooper-pair-breaking formation (PBF) and the Bremsstrahlung process occurring in the core of NS. We use the radial distance-dependent magnetic field configuration within the permissible limit of the central magnetic field. Our work explores the variations in the axion masses of 10 meV, 15 meV, and 20 meV as a cooling source for spherically symmetric magnetised NSs. We have also shown the energy spectrum of axions and their conversion to photons. Our analysis shows that the cooling rate and the luminosity of observables (axions) for NSs change significantly due to the magnetic field. The results for the luminosity of axions is quite sensitive to its mass and EoS, as the less separation is observed for SLY EoS in comparison to the FPS and APR EoS. We report that the spectrum of axions from the Bremsstrahlung process dominates over the PBF process at lesser axion energies, within the possible axion mass range for PSR J1357-6429 NS. Our results reveal that the impact of the magnetic field is less at lower axion energies, indicating the necessity for including a magnetic field in axion-to-photon conversion mechanisms. The results for the axions mass 10 meV and 15 meV as compared to 20 meV confirms the existing report of the 16 meV.

title: On the stability and emittance growth of different particle phase-space distributions in a long magnetic quadrupole channel
abstract: The behavior of K-V, waterbag, parabolic, conical and Gaussian distributions in periodic quadrupole channels is studied by particle simulations. In the parameter range studied, the response associated with the K-V instabilities becomes progressively less pronounced toward the Gaussian distribution. For the third-order instability studied here, the emittance growth factor of an initially Gaussian beam after a large number of periods is considerably lower than that of an equivalent K-V distribution.\newline\indent In addition, the non-K-V distributions exhibit a rapid initial emittance growth within approximately one period of the channel, which becomes very significant at high beam intensities. This growth is attributed to the homogenization of the space-charge density, resulting in a conversion of electric-field energy into transverse kinetic and potential energy. Two simple analytical formulae based on different energy-partition assumptions are derived as estimates for this effect and are compared with the results obtained from particle simulations. They are not rigorous lower and upper bounds for arbitrary beam evolution. \\[6pt] Revised version of: Particle Accelerators {\bf 15}, 47--65 (1984)}

title: Improved envelope and emittance description of particle beams using the Fokker-Planck approach
abstract: Beam dynamics calculations based on the collisionless Vlasov equation omit collisional correlations such as intra-beam scattering. For a short-correlated process dominated by small momentum changes, a Fokker-Planck equation can describe their effect on the one-particle distribution. From this equation we derive equations of motion for the beam envelopes and for the rms-emittances. Prescribed friction against an external bath is distinguished from momentum- and energy-conserving self-collisions. For the latter, an affine mean-flow approximation and a scalar relaxation coefficient give simple equations for temperature balancing within the beam. The longitudinal diffusion and temperature are expressed in terms of the physical random momentum rather than the signed effective longitudinal mass. The resulting growth-rate formulas apply to this reduced relaxation model. The original numerical examples are retained for comparison, with the limitations of the storage-ring and numerical-noise applications made explicit. Revised version of: Particle Accelerators~{\bf 45}, 229 (1994)

title: High-Efficiency Wakefield Acceleration of Positrons via a Slit Plasma Channel
abstract: Although plasma-based wakefield acceleration has achieved remarkable success for electrons, efficient positron acceleration remains a long standing challenge, as positrons suffer severe defocusing in the accelerating phases of such structures. Here, we propose a slit plasma wakefield acceleration (SPWA) scheme, in which a relativistic electron beam propagating through a slit channel formed by two parallel plasma slabs excites crossing plasma-electron filamentary structures within the slit, generating intense wakefields tailored to simultaneously provide longitudinal acceleration and transverse focusing for a trailing positron bunch. A theoretical model is developed to characterize the wakefield structure responsible for positron acceleration and focusing. Three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations validate the model, and demonstrate that the SPWA scheme achieves a positron trapping efficiency of nearly 100%, while maintaining low emittance growth and narrow energy spread for an injected positron beam. These findings establish a new and robust approach to high-efficiency positron acceleration, with promising implications for future compact electron-positron colliders and high-energy positron applications.

title: Conceptual Design of Pumping Systems up to 1000 m3/s Based on Non-Evaporable Getters in a Gas-Dynamic Magnetic Trap
abstract: The Gas-Dynamic Magnetic Trap (GDMT), a new linear magnetic facility for confining high-temperature hydrogen plasma, is currently under development at the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics (BINP SB RAS). The total hydrogen flow that must be removed from the end expanders by the vacuum system is approximately 10^22 molecules/s, which corresponds to a required pumping speed on the order of 500 m3/s. Non-evaporable getters (NEG) are considered as a possible pumping method for this application. This article presents experimental studies of Ti-Zr-Al getters manufactured by Polema LLC. The pumping speed, sorption capacity, and sticking factors of the getter surface were measured. The sticking factors for hydrogen and deuterium are 2.23% and 1.54%, respectively. The getter pumping speed is maintained over 60 air-vent/reactivation cycles. Based on these results, a conceptual design of a NEG-based pumping system for the GDMT end expanders is proposed, providing a specific pumping speed of 74 m3/(m3s) for the getter panel. The proposed pumping system design and the required heating power are discussed.

title: Toponium hadroproduction at next-to-next-to-leading order in NRQCD
abstract: We present the first next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) predictions for inclusive color-singlet toponium hadroproduction within NRQCD in the zero-width limit for the top quark. The central new result is the NNLO QCD correction to the short-distance coefficient for pseudoscalar toponium production. The predictions include electroweak and relativistic corrections, additional production channels, and perturbatively evaluated bound-state matrix elements. At the Large Hadron Collider proton-proton center-of-mass energy of $13\,\mathrm{TeV}$, we obtain a cross section of $4.87^{+0.63}_{-0.65}\,\mathrm{pb}$, with scale and parametric uncertainties combined. The NNLO corrections reduce the renormalization- and factorization-scale uncertainties by approximately a factor of four relative to NLO, to the few-percent level. The dominant remaining uncertainty arises from the Coulomb-scale dependence of the bound-state matrix elements.

title: Shortcomings of the squark simplified model
abstract: We argue that the squark simplified model commonly used in collider analyses fails to represent realistic low-energy supersymmetric models and significantly underestimates squark production rates at hadron colliders. This has important implications for extracting squark mass limits at the LHC and assessing the potential reach of HL-LHC or the FCC-hh. In particular, we find that the current LHC squark mass limit is realistically in the range of 2.6-3.0 TeV, rather than the 1.7-1.8 TeV range that is typically quoted based on the simplified model.

title: Quark deconfinement as a natural trigger of Type-I critical collapse: black holes from neutron stars deemed stable
abstract: Spherically symmetric general-relativistic simulations show that a first-order hadron--quark phase transition can collapse radially stable neutron stars into black holes, even when a stable hybrid star of the same baryon mass exists. The dynamical threshold lies $0.12\,M_\odot$ in baryon mass below the static one, so black holes can be lighter than the heaviest stable star. The threshold is a Type-I critical point: near it, the star lingers at an unstable hybrid star of equal baryon mass for a time set by that star's unstable mode. The effect persists within a narrower window for finite conversion rates.

title: Probing the Sivers Asymmetry with Transverse Energy-Energy Correlators in the Small-$x$ Regime
