abstract: We investigate transverse energy-energy correlators (TEECs) for both polarized and unpolarized targets in the small-$x$ regime at the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). Focusing on the approximately back-to-back electroproduction of a hadron-electron pair, we apply transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization formulas that incorporate TMD evolution for both event-shape observables and expand them in terms of the small-$x$ dipole amplitude. This allows us to write the TEEC off the transversely polarized proton in terms of a C-odd interaction, corresponding to an odderon exchange. Due to the charge-conjugation-odd nature of the small-$x$ quark Sivers function, we restrict the sum over final hadronic states to positively and negatively charged hadrons separately. We present numerical predictions for the TEEC Sivers asymmetry at the EIC and find the magnitude of the asymmetry to be on the $0.01 \%$ level. This channel offers a promising avenue for benchmarking the still largely unconstrained odderon amplitude.

title: Multimuon Events from Cosmic Rays with the ALICE Detector
abstract: ALICE experiment at the CERN's Large Hadron Collider, carried out a cosmic data-taking campaign in the period 2015-2018 (LHC Run 2), for a total of 62.5 days of real observation time. In this contribution, the analysis of these data is limited to multimuon events, i.e. events with more than four detected muons. In particular, the muon multiplicity distribution (MMD) is studied in the low-intermediate multiplicity range ($4 100$, dominated by large statistical fluctuations of the data, the rate of the high muon multiplicity events (HMM) is measured. The results are compared with Monte Carlo simulations using three of the main hadronic interaction models describing the air shower development in the atmosphere: QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC, and SIBYLL 2.3d, and assuming two extreme compositions of primary cosmic rays, pure proton and pure iron, representing respectively the lightest and the heaviest composition. Although the models have difficulty precisely describing the trend of primary p and Fe as a function of cosmic ray primary energy, QGSJET-II-04 is the only model that reproduces reasonably well the MMD and the rate of HMM events assuming a heavy composition for the entire energy range studied.

title: Modeling a Framework for Comprehensive Analysis of $\boldsymbol{p^\uparrow\!{A}}$ Transverse Analyzing Power Measurements at the RHIC HJET
abstract: We present a model for calculating the forward elastic analyzing power $A_\text{N}^{pA}(t)$ in proton-nucleus scattering, based on the Glauber approximation and incorporating soft-photon exchange corrections. The model is tested against 100 GeV HJET measurements for several nuclei, including Au, Ru, Zr, Al, O, C, and the deuteron. The calculations use Woods-Saxon parameters to describe the nuclear density distributions, as well as the proton-proton and proton-neutron hadronic spin-flip amplitudes, with the latter constrained by a Regge fit to HJET $pp$ data. Using the nominal input parameters, the calculations provide a reasonable description of the measured analyzing powers, although further refinement is needed to achieve a satisfactory fit. Allowing the input parameters to vary in the fits substantially improves the agreement with the data, yielding effective parametrizations of $A_\text{N}^{pA}(t)$ in terms of three or four parameters, depending on the nucleus. Notably, the nominal values of the imaginary part of the effective proton-nucleus spin-flip parameter $r_5^{pA}$ agree well with the fitted values for all nuclei considered. Subject to the limitations of the present model, this observation concerning $\operatorname{Im} r_5^{pA}$ is consistent with the proton-proton spin-flip amplitudes measured at HJET and supports the interpretation of a non-zero Pomeron spin-flip coupling. The results presented in this paper also motivate further investigation of the energy dependence of the proton-nucleon spin-flip amplitude using HJET measurements over a broad range of beam energies, with potential applications to proton-carbon and \(^3\)He polarimetry at the Electron-Ion Collider.

title: Elliptic and triangular flow responses in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions from hydrodynamics and kinetic theory
abstract: Recent light-ion collisions at the Large Hadron Collider provide an opportunity to investigate the system-size dependence of hydrodynamization and whether the structure of light nuclei can be extracted from collective flow data. Both objectives require an accurate understanding of how the collision dynamics converts initial-state geometry into final-state momentum anisotropies. To this end, and to assess the impact of the experimental results, we compare simulations of O+O and Ne+Ne collisions in hydrodynamic and kinetic theory simulations across opacities. In both ultracentral and peripheral collisions, Ne+Ne-to-O+O elliptic flow ratios are robust against changes in dynamical description, supporting interpretations of data based on nuclear-geometry-driven effects. Triangular-flow ratios instead show substantially stronger sensitivity to nonequilibrium dynamics.

title: Production of vacuum particles from relativistic scalar particles in a deformed spacetime
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the quantum dynamics of relativistic scalar particles in a (1+1)-dimensional de Sitter spacetime deformed by rainbow gravity, in which the spacetime metric depends explicitly on the energy of the probing particles. We begin by deriving the covariant Klein–Gordon equation in this modified gravitational background and obtain its exact solutions by two independent methods, in terms of Whittaker and Hankel functions. Building upon this formulation, we analyze the corresponding energy spectrum and the semiclassical solutions, and subsequently examine vacuum particle production within the Bogoliubov approach. Both sets of solutions lead to the same particle number density, which takes the form of a thermal Bose–Einstein distribution depending only on the temporal rainbow function f 1 . In the large-mass limit, it reduces to a Boltzmann factor characterized by an effective Gibbons–Hawking temperature T = f 1 H / 2 π , showing that rainbow gravity rescales the de Sitter horizon temperature and can either enhance or suppress particle creation relative to general relativity.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Observable gravitational waves from unstable ALP catastrogenesis
abstract: We focus on gravitational waves (GWs) observable in pulsar timing array and interferometric searches that are produced by the annihilation of cosmic string-wall networks in axion-like particle (ALP) models. We called this process "catastrogenesis." It produces GWs with a characteristic peaked spectrum. These GWs would not be observable if the ALPs were stable. We thus assume that ALPs decay into two photons before Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). The large ALP-photon coupling required could induce field dissipation and friction on cosmic walls through interactions with the radiation background. We study the conditions under which these effects are negligible and map the parameter regions yielding observable GW signals onto the usual ALP mass-coupling parameter space. We find that, in these regions, ALPs dominate the energy density of the Universe before they decay, leading to a period of intermediate matter domination, which would leave a clear imprint on the GW spectrum.

title: Coordinate Independence of the Schwarzschild Black Hole Accretion Vlasov Gas Model
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a detailed study of the coordinate dependence of Vlasov gas accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole. Asymptotic results at infinity and nearhorizon are obtained via Taylor expansions for three different statistical distributions within the framework of the most general stationary spherically symmetric spacetime. Our findings demonstrate that the particle number density, energy density, radial and tangential pressures, and accretion rates are independent of the coordinate choice, even though individual components such as the particle current density and the stress-energy tensor explicitly depend on the coordinate system. Consequently, the accretion theory can be formulated without reference to any particular coordinate system. We also show that the mean energy of the accreted particles is $m_0+k_BT$, lower than the mean energy $m_0+\frac{3}{2}k_BT$ of the Maxwell-Boltzmann system in the classical limit. And the specific entropy of the accreted particles is lower than the global average by $\frac{3}{2}k_B$. This is because particles of lower energy are more easily accreted, while particles of higher energy are more readily scattered. We also present numerical results at finite radii for the relevant physical quantities.

title: 2:1 Harmonics in the Radio Light Curves of Supermassive Black Hole Binary Candidates
abstract: We present evidence of 2:1 harmonic periodicities in two supermassive black hole binary (SMBHB) candidates (PKS J0805-0111 and PKS 2131-021) in the Owens Valley Radio Observatory (OVRO) + University of Michigan Radio Astronomical Observatory (UMRAO) monitoring programs. This potential discovery follows the previous detection of a 2:1 harmonic periodicity in the SMBHB candidate J1309+1154 from these programs. If confirmed, these suggest a physical origin of blazars exhibiting strong periodicities favoring 2:1 commensurabilities in their light curves. There are significant differences between the 2:1 harmonics in these three blazars, which may be due to differences in their central engines. These three SMBHB candidates demonstrate the importance of careful dissection, i.e. cutting apart and close examination, of blazar light curves, to reveal underlying evidence of coherence between different aspects of the periodicities observed in blazars in the presence of correlated random noise variations. This is particularly important for blazar SMBHB searches, given that the observed periods thus far are all longer than 2 years, and can disappear for long timespans. Harmonics may therefore be crucial in confirming the reality of periodicities and identifying blazar SMBHB candidates. We discuss four models that can account for 2:1 commensurable periodicities in blazar light curves and explain how future detections of shorter period SMBHB candidates, or the lack thereof, may be used to discriminate among the models. Arguments for and against the reality of these periodicities are presented.

title: Topological Diagnostics of CP Degeneracies in Long-Baseline Neutrino Oscillations with Non-Standard Interactions via Pancharatnam Open-Path Phases
Probing damping effects in neutrino oscillations with 207 days of JUNO data
abstract: We consider different scenarios which lead to a damping of the neutrino oscillation probability and investigate their impact on the JUNO results. First, we study decoherence effects due to wave packet separation. In addition, we consider an open quantum system framework and adopt a phenomenological approach which allows us to parameterize the energy dependence of the decoherence effects more freely. Finally, we study the effect of invisible neutrino decay. In all cases with 207 days of data, JUNO can already place competitive bounds on the parameter space of the scenarios under consideration, while also maintaining a relatively robust measurement of the standard neutrino oscillation parameters.

title: Search for Vector-Like Singlet Top ($T$) Quark in a Future Muon-Proton ($\mu p$) Collider at $\sqrt{s} = 5.29, 6.48,$ and $9.16$ TeV using Advanced Machine Learning Architectures
abstract: We study the sensitivity of a future $\mu p$ collider to singly produced singlet vector-like $T$ quarks in the $T\to Wb$ decay mode across both fully hadronic ($bjj$) and leptonic ($b\ell\nu$) final states at $\sqrt{s}=5.29$, $6.48$, and $9.16~\mathrm{TeV}$. Utilizing resolved-object reconstruction and TMVA-based multivariate classifiers (BDT, BDTG, MLP, and Likelihood), we perform a fast-simulation scan over $m_T=2$--$5~\mathrm{TeV}$ and the $(g^{*},m_T)$ parameter space. To quantify improvements, we compare this multivariate selection against the closest cut-based baseline at a benchmark point of $m_T=3~\mathrm{TeV}$, $\sqrt{s}=9.16~\mathrm{TeV}$, and $\mathcal{L}=3000~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, incorporating a $20\%$ background-normalization uncertainty via the Asimov significance $Z_A$. At this benchmark, the hadronic channel exhibits a substantial enhancement in both $S/\sqrt{S+B}$ and $Z_A$, improving from $18.05$ and $1.44$ to $273.51$ and $42.24$, respectively. Similarly, the leptonic channel improves from $3.51$ and $0.330$ to $113.85$ and $21.51$. In the full parameter scan, the $\sqrt{s}=9.16~\mathrm{TeV}$ configuration provides the strongest sensitivity at $\mathcal{L}=3000~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The hadronic channel excludes (discovers) regions with $g^{*}\in[0.20,0.50]$ ($[0.30,0.50]$) up to $m_T\approx4.0~(3.5)~\mathrm{TeV}$, while the leptonic channel remains sensitive up to $m_T\approx5.0~\mathrm{TeV}$ for $g^{*}\in[0.10,0.50]$. These gains arise from the higher-purity multivariate signal regions evaluated under a common significance prescription, and not from a change of the collider configuration. The projections assume resolved-object reconstruction and fast detector simulation, and the absolute reach should be read with these assumptions in mind.

title: Non-Maxwellianity in Temperature Relaxation between Plasma Species
abstract: Temperature relaxation between plasma species is usually described by Landau--Spitzer (LS) theory, which assumes Maxwellian distributions throughout. We show analytically that, for two Maxwellian species in homogeneous isotropic plasmas, the interspecies collisions driving relaxation generate a universal three-lobe initial distortion and that these distortions initially reduce energy exchange over a broad parameter range. Full Fokker--Planck simulations reveal substantial relaxation delays when interspecies deformation competes with self-thermalization. For post-shock deuterium--tritium plasmas relevant to inertial confinement fusion, with $T_{\mathrm{T}}/T_{\mathrm{D}}=1.5$, the relaxation time exceeds the LS prediction by 47%. The accompanying distortions lower the apparent DD/DT temperature ratio and produce positive DD and negative DT Gamow-shift residuals relative to Maxwellian predictions. These results also motivate examining non-Maxwellianity in fuel heating by fusion $\alpha$ particles.

title: Modeling runaway electron mitigation via passively driven plasma instabilities in a high-current tokamak
abstract: A critical challenge for tokamak-based fusion power plants is the formation of high-current, relativistic runaway electron (RE) beams during abrupt confinement loss events called disruptions. RE beams may significantly damage machine components if left unmitigated, jeopardizing the operational and economic viability of fusion power plants. We present the first self-consistent extended magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computational study of RE mitigation with a passively driven RE mitigation coil (REMC) in a high-current tokamak. RE generation and transport are coupled with REMC-driven MHD activity in a 3D simulation that models the thermal and current quench phases of a mid-plane disruption, together with the vertical displacement and final termination of the plasma and RE beam on SPARC -- a high-field, high-current tokamak designed to achieve a fusion gain Q > 1. We demonstrate that REMC-driven magnetic stochasticity can reduce the RE current by over an order-of-magnitude when compared to unmitigated disruptions. The final termination is mediated via a post-thermal-quench "cold" vertical displacement of the plasma, which, together with magnetic stochasticity, increases RE losses via scrape-off once the plasma contacts the first wall. These results demonstrate a viable mechanism for RE mitigation using passively driven plasma instabilities on high-current tokamaks.

title: Hydrogen and Lithium Isotope Analysis via Optical Spectroscopy of Laser-Produced Plasmas
abstract: Accurate detection and quantification of light-element isotopes, particularly hydrogen (H) and lithium (Li), are essential across chemistry, materials science, geology, nuclear energy, forensics, and defense applications. Their isotopic compositions provide insight into fuel cycles, materials degradation, mass transport, and environmental processes. Hydrogen and Li isotopes are especially relevant in nuclear environments because neutron-induced reactions directly connect their isotopic inventories. Despite their importance, analysis of these light isotopes remains challenging due to their low atomic mass, high mobility, and, in some cases, radiological constraints. While some existing analytical techniques can detect and measure H and/or Li, they typically require extensive sample preparation, laboratory-based instrumentation, or extended analysis times that preclude real-time monitoring capabilities. To address these limitations, optical spectroscopy of laser-produced plasmas offers a promising solution, enabling field-deployable, standoff sensing of isotopic signatures with real-time analysis capability and no sample preparation requirement. This Topical Review summarizes fundamentals and recent advances in H and Li isotopic analysis using optical spectroscopy, with emphasis on laser-produced plasmas generated by laser ablation of solid targets. Key concepts relevant to isotope-resolved optical measurements are introduced, including isotope shifts, fine and hyperfine structure, and line-broadening mechanisms. Progress in optical emission, laser induced fluorescence, and absorption spectroscopy is reviewed for H and Li isotopes.

title: Signatures of Long-Lived Heavy Neutral Leptons from Neutrinophilic Charged Higgs Pair Production at the LHC
abstract: In the neutrinophilic Higgs doublet framework, the neutrino Dirac Yukawa couplings can be sizable because of the small vacuum expection value of the extra Higgs doublet, even for a low seesaw scale. Due to this structure, the neutrinophilic charged Higgs bosons, once created, decay dominantly into heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) and charged leptons. This is a new mechanism to produce a gauge singlet HNL without suppressed cross sections. In the standard seesaw, one HNL can be long-lived, when the lightest neutrino is sufficiently light. We investigate displaced vertex signatures of the long-lived HNLs produced from the decays of the charged Higgs pair at the high luminosity LHC. We consider one displaced vertex as well as two displaced vertices signatures and perform a dedicated simulation to identify the displaced leptons. We find that high statistical significance can be achieved for the observation of one displaced vertex for charged Higgs pair production cross section $>\mathcal{O}(1)$ fb. On the other hand, the observation of two displaced vertices is challenging, particularly for charged Higgs pair production cross section below $\mathcal{O}(10)$ fb.

title: Search for heavy neutral leptons in top quark decays with same-sign, same-flavor dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
abstract: A search for a Majorana-type heavy neutral lepton (HNL) produced in top quark decays is reported. The search is based on proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, collected during 2016$-$2018 with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC. In the type-I seesaw model, a Majorana HNL can mediate lepton-number-violating top quark decays. The search targets top quark pair production events in which one top quark decays into a bottom quark and a W boson, which subsequently decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and an HNL. The Majorana HNL then decays into a W boson and a charged lepton with the same sign and flavor as the one produced with the HNL. The experimental signature features a same-sign, same-flavor lepton pair and jets. The HNL masses between 20 and 100 GeV are probed. The data agree with the standard model background prediction. Observed (expected) upper limits at 95% confidence level are set on the branching fraction of the top quark decay into an HNL, a charged lepton, and a bottom quark, varying between [1.1 (0.71)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ and [4.8 (3.0)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dielectron channel, and between [3.7 (3.4)] $\times$10$^{-6}$ and [2.4 (1.3)] $\times$10$^{-5}$ in the dimuon channel.

title: Search for dark photons from Higgs boson decays in the gluon-gluon fusion channel in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV with the ATLAS detector
abstract: This paper presents a search for semi-visible Higgs boson decays in final states with a photon ($\gamma$) and missing transverse momentum $p_T^{miss}$. The analysis is optimised for the gluon-gluon fusion production channel and exploits a novel trigger deployed in 2023, with reduced thresholds down to 50 GeV on the photon transverse momentum ($p_T^{\gamma}$) and 70 GeV on the $p_T^{miss}$, in combination with a selection on the transverse mass of the $p_T^{miss}$-$\gamma$ system ($m_T$) above 80 GeV. The results are interpreted in terms of Higgs boson decays into a $\gamma$ and a dark photon $\gamma_d$ ($H \to \gamma \gamma_d$). The analysis is performed using 135 fb$^{-1}$ of Run 3 data collected by ATLAS in 2023 and 2024. A boosted decision tree is used to identify events with misreconstructed primary vertices, which can affect the $p_T^{miss}$ calculation. Data-driven methods are employed to estimate the backgrounds from jets and electrons misidentified as photons, while the backgrounds with genuine photons are taken from Monte Carlo simulations, normalised to data in control regions with muons. A binned maximum-likelihood fit to the $m_T$ distribution is performed to evaluate the compatibility of the observed data with the Standard Model expectation. No significant excess is observed over the Standard Model prediction, and an observed (expected) upper limit on the branching ratio of $H \to \gamma \gamma_d$ of 1.4% (1.2%) is obtained at 95% confidence level. Combining this result with previous Run 2 searches improves the observed (expected) upper limit to 0.9% (0.9%).

title: Electroweak Constraints on Nuclear Neutron Distributions and the Low-Energy Weak Mixing Angle
abstract:
Coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (CE$
u$NS) offers a low-energy probe of the weak mixing angle, $\sin^2	heta_W$, and possible new physics in the neutrino sector. Its reliable interpretation, however, requires independent constraints on the neutron distributions of the target nuclei. We exploit correlations across nuclei within an extended Skyrme energy-density-functional framework to propagate constraints from the CREX and PREX-II parity-violating electron-scattering (PVES) measurements to CE$
u$NS targets. This yields neutron form factors and radii, with relative radius uncertainties below $1\%$. Using these inferred neutron form factors, we jointly analyze the COHERENT CsI, Ge, and Ar data and obtain $\sin^2	heta_W=0.231^{+0.016}_{-0.015}$, consistent with the Standard Model prediction. These results provide the first electroweak-experimentally constrained benchmarks for nuclear-structure studies, neutrino-sector electroweak tests, and CE$
u$NS signal predictions in dark-matter detectors.

title: Constraining tau-sterile neutrino mixing with high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
abstract:
Whether a sterile neutrino mixes with the three active ones remains an open question. Its mixing with the tau neutrino, $|U_{	au 4}|^2$, is the least constrained, since terrestrial experiments probe it only indirectly and over limited ranges of sterile-neutrino mass. We show that TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos probe it differently. Their sources make almost no $
u_	au$, but oscillations over cosmological distances turn about one third of them into $
u_	au$ before they reach Earth. Mixing with a sterile neutrino would make these $
u_	au$ scarcer, lowering the $
u_	au$ fraction that neutrino telescopes measure, whatever the sterile-neutrino mass. In contrast, sterile mixing with $
u_e$ or $
u_\mu$ is nearly undetectable. Fitting the flavor composition measured by IceCube, with the composition at the sources left free, we find $|U_{	au 4}|^2 < 0.88$ at 90% C.L. Combining IceCube with present and planned neutrino telescopes, including IceCube-Gen2 and HUNT, could lower this limit to 0.24-0.29 by 2040 and to 0.12-0.14 by 2050. By 2050, these limits would match some present terrestrial limits, though not the strongest.

title: Carbon-Reaction Constraints on Stellar Evolution: White-Dwarf Heating, Carbon-Burning Products, and Black-Hole Masses
abstract: The effects of ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}+{}^{12}\mathrm{C}$ fusion and ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma){}^{16}\mathrm{O}$ capture on stellar heating, composition, and black-hole masses are examined. Rates from a published Bayesian analysis of carbon fusion are used in calculations with MESA. In an accreting carbon--oxygen white dwarf, the Bayesian rates move the point at which nuclear heating equals combined neutrino and surface photon losses to slightly larger stellar masses and higher central temperatures and densities. At an accretion rate of $10^{-7}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the Bayesian median gives a central temperature approximately $2.57\%$ higher and a central density $18.9\%$ higher than the calculation using the standard CF88 rate. A separate calculation follows carbon burning in an initially $20\,M_\odot$, $Z=0.0142$ star. Relative to the CF88 rate with MESA's standard division between proton and alpha channels, the Bayesian-median rate with the proton-to-alpha ratio of Yang et al. increases the neon-20 mass remaining at central carbon depletion by $10.8\%$ and decreases the sodium-23 mass by $28.7\%$. For helium capture on carbon, the nuclear constraint $S_{\rm tot}(300\,\mathrm{keV})=118\pm17\,\mathrm{keV\,b}$ is applied to the published $Z=10^{-5}$ stellar models of Farag et al. Linear interpolation gives a maximum black-hole mass below the pair-instability gap of approximately $61.5$--$77.4\,M_\odot$ within the assumptions of those models. New MESA calculations at $Z=0.00142$ give smaller bound masses before collapse. Differences in the stellar assumptions prevent attributing the difference between the two curves to metallicity alone.

title: Calibration of the jet energy scale and resolution of small-radius jets using semileptonic $t\bar{t}$ events with the ATLAS detector
abstract: A measurement of correction factors for the hadronic jet energy scale and resolution in the ATLAS detector is presented. These correction factors account for differences between simulated and observed data. They are obtained by analysing a selection of top quark events collected in proton-proton collisions by ATLAS between the years 2015 and 2018 at a centre-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV as well as in 2022 and 2023 at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6$ TeV. The impact of different jet energy scale or resolution corrections on the reconstructed mass of the hadronically decaying $W$ boson from top-quark decays in simulation is quantified. The correction factors are extracted from a fit to the parameterised reconstructed $W$-boson mass distribution to data. The energy scale and resolution corrections are measured as a function of the jet transverse momentum between 20 and 200 GeV and absolute pseudorapidity less than 0.8. The uncertainties in the energy scale range from about 0.93% to about 1.7% for jets between 35 and 200 GeV, while for the energy resolution the uncertainties range from about 14% to 28%. The method presented will be used in conjunction with other techniques to further improve ATLAS jet energy scale and resolution precision.

title: Axion Electrodynamics in Presence of a Stellar Non-homogeneous Background Magnetic Field
abstract: We re-assess effects of Axion Electrodynamics in the presence of non-homogeneous background magnetic fields. The Primakoff effect, which is an ALP-photon mixing induced by a background magnetic field, is generalized to the case of non-homogeneous backgrounds. The production of ALPs from a magnetized plasma thermal medium is also computed. The Eddington's solar standard model is adopted as the phenomenological scenario for our settings, and new bounds on the Axion Electrodynamics parameter space are imposed by considering helioseismological and neutrino observational measurements.

title: Anomalies in Hadronic $B \to VV$ Decays
abstract: Recently, a fit of charmless $B\to PP$ decays ($B \in \{B^0, B^+, B_s^0\}$, $P \in \{ \pi, K, \eta, \eta' \}$) to the latest data was performed under the assumption of flavour SU(3) symmetry [SU(3)$_F$]. It was found that there is a $4.1\sigma$ disagreement with the SU(3)$_F$ limit of the Standard Model [$\rm SM_{SU(3)_F}$]. In this paper, we extend this analysis to charmless $B \to VV$ decays ($V \in \{\rho, K^*, \phi, \omega\}$). The fit examining $B \to \rho K^*$ decays, assuming only isospin symmetry, is found to be acceptable. When we fit to $B \to VV$ decays with $V \in \{ \rho, K^* \}$ within SU(3)$_F$, we find a $5.2\sigma$ discrepancy with SM$_{SU(3)_F}$. Finally, when $B \to VV$ decays with $V \in \{ \rho, K^*, \phi, \omega \}$ are considered, the discrepancy grows to $>7\sigma$. The theoretical input in this analysis is modest, so our results are quite rigorous, group theoretically, and hold almost exactly in the SU(3)$_F$ limit. Although it seems unlikely that the introduction of $\sim 30$% SU(3)$_F$-breaking effects can account for this discrepancy, this must be verified.

title: Two-loop QCD amplitudes for $t\bar{t}W$ production at the LHC in the leading-colour approximation
abstract: We present a numerical computation of the two-loop QCD scattering amplitudes for the production of a top-antitop quark pair in association with a $W$ boson ($t\bar{t}W$) at the LHC in the generalised leading-colour approximation, retaining the exact dependence on the top-quark and $W$-boson masses. Rather than pursuing a fully analytic calculation, we employ a hybrid framework that combines numerical evaluation with strong algebraic and analytic control, allowing ultraviolet and infrared singularities as well as large intermediate cancellations to be treated exactly. This is achieved by expressing the finite remainder in terms of a set of special functions with rational coefficients. The special functions are evaluated numerically by solving differential equations through power-series expansions, while the values of the rational coefficients are reconstructed, point by point, from finite-field evaluations. The calculation is performed in the 't Hooft-Veltman scheme and validated against an independent implementation in conventional dimensional regularisation employing a substantially different computational strategy. We finally provide the colour- and polarisation-summed hard functions evaluated on the phase-space grid used in a previous computation of the next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to the $t\bar{t}W$ cross section.

title: Three-body forces in the quark model
abstract: We review the connection between constituent-quark Hamiltonians and QCD and investigate the long-standing difficulty of describing meson and baryon spectra with one common two-body interaction. A Hamiltonian calibrated to ground-state mesons leaves systematic baryon mass residuals, largest in the light-quark sector and decreasing toward heavier flavors. We show that a short-range, color-spin-dependent connected three-quark interaction substantially reduces this incompatibility. Mass-scaled finite-range profiles yield high-accuracy baryon spectra, whereas flavor-independent common-range profiles do not remove the residual flavor pattern. The result is tested on additional ground-state baryons outside the calibration set and through meson--baryon compatibility analyses across several alternative quark-model Hamiltonians. We also benchmark radial and orbital excitations to identify the regime in which a static compact valence Hamiltonian remains reliable, and provide explicit color-spin matrix elements for two- and three-body operators in baryons and multiquark configurations. Within the tested valence-space representations, the results indicate that a mass-dependent short-range connected three-quark interaction provides the missing contribution required for a consistent simultaneous description of meson and baryon ground-state spectra.

title: Spin alignment of vector mesons in a plasma at finite density
abstract: Holographic predictions for vector meson spin alignment at finite density have been limited by how the chemical potential is implemented. Existing models use a baryon chemical potential and report that the alignment is insensitive to it, while zero-density benchmarks do not address the geometric deformation. We address this limitation by using a charged AdS black-hole background with a quark chemical potential and solving the coupled bulk vector equations with infalling horizon conditions. The zero-density limit reproduces previous results of Sheng et al. [Phys. Rev. D 110, 056047 (2024)]. At \(T=0.15~\mathrm{GeV}\), the \(J/\psi\) spectral function has a resonance peak at \(\mu=0\) that lowers and broadens with increasing \(\mu\), whereas the \(\phi\) spectral function shows no pronounced peak. In the helicity frame, \(\rho_{00}\) deviates positively from \(1/3\) for the \(J/\psi\) and negatively for the \(\phi\). The density response is more visible in our setup than the weak baryon chemical potential sensitivity reported in a four-flavor soft-wall model. This difference illustrates the model dependence of the density response: it is controlled by the chemical potential normalization. We identify the presence of the resonance peak and the signs of the helicity deviations as robust qualitative features, and treat the numerical shifts of \(\rho_{00}\) as model-dependent estimates.

title: Quasi-normal Modes and Instabilities of Rotating Relativistic Stars
abstract: We derive the basic equations suitable for the coupled fluid--spacetime eigenvalue problem from the second-order action in full general relativity and accurately determine quasi-normal modes of a variety of rapidly rotating stars with outgoing-wave boundary conditions. For MIT-bag strange stars, the spectrum realizes Chandrasekhar's instability picture, with distinct Chandrasekhar--Friedman--Schutz and Jacobi-like neutral conditions and the transition to dynamical bar-mode growth. For neutron stars, we determine the $f$-, $r$-, and other inertial-mode spectra and their radiative damping or growth times. Interactions between $f$- and inertial modes reveal avoided crossings and exchanges for radiative damping or growth rates. We locate quasiradial collapse thresholds through a static stability analysis and independently verify them by tracking the fundamental $F$-mode frequency to zero, clarifying that the central density at the onset of the dynamical instability is always larger than that of the secular instability for uniform rotation. Our formalism and numerical implementation can also resolve highly damped $w$-modes.

title: On Photon Propagation in Strong Magnetic Fields: Time Delays from Pulsars
abstract: We study photon dispersion in the presence of a strong external magnetic field for propagation both perpendicular and parallel to the field, considering (i) the magnetized QED vacuum and (ii) a magnetized electron-positron medium at finite density (nonzero chemical potential). The analysis is performed in one-loop QED at finite temperature and density, and we extract polarization-dependent dispersion relations and phase velocities from the eigenmodes of the photon polarization operator. Using these phase velocities, we estimate propagation-induced time delays for photons emitted from neutron stars in the strong-field regime, adopting a simplified magnetosphere model with a toroidal magnetic field geometry and a radially varying chemical potential profile in the degenerate limit. We compare the predicted delays with observational timing constraints and discuss how strong-field QED and plasma corrections can generate measurable departures from the light cone, with potential signatures relevant for magnetars and modern polarimetric and timing observations. It should be noted that the time-delay estimates derived here are based on the phase velocity and serve as indicative order-of-magnitude predictions.

title: Investigating nucleon resonances in the $pp\to K^+K^+\Lambda\Lambda$ reaction
abstract: In this work, we investigate the \(pp \to K^+ K^+ \Lambda \Lambda\) reaction using an effective Lagrangian approach and the isobar model. The calculation includes the exchange of \(\pi\), \(\eta\), \(\sigma\), \(\rho\), \(\omega\), and \(K\) mesons, as well as contributions from eight nucleon resonances: \(N(1535)\), \(N(1650)\), \(N(1710)\), \(N(1720)\), \(N(1895)\), \(N(1900)\), \(N(2060)\) and \(N(2120)\). The double-resonance excitation mechanism (\(NN \to N^* N^*\)) is found to dominate this reaction over the entire energy range considered. Among the exchanged mesons, the \(\eta\) exchange provides the largest contribution at lower energies, whereas the \(K\) exchange dominates at higher energies. Near the threshold, \(N(1535)\) and \(N(1650)\) play the most important roles, while at higher energies \(N(1710)\) and \(N(1720)\) become dominant. Due to isospin conservation, this reaction is predominantly coupled to nucleon resonances, providing a relatively clean channel for \(N^*\) spectroscopy. Our results indicate the unique potential of this reaction for studying nucleon resonances and provide a theoretical reference for future experimental studies at HIAF.

title: Deconfinement Confined to the Heaviest Neutron Stars: Strange Quark Matter from a Flavor-Dressed Contact Interaction
abstract: We study cold, electrically neutral, beta-equilibrated quark matter with u, d, and s quarks described by a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose parameters are fixed in vacuum. The vector repulsion is varied as a fraction 0 < eta < 3/2 of the scalar coupling, and results are given with and without the flavor dressing of the effective coupling. Pure quark matter is not self-bound in this model, and no value of eta produces a star that reaches two solar masses while satisfying the tidal constraint from GW170817; the heaviest configurations owe their mass to an envelope of constituent quarks. We then construct hybrid stars with a relativistic mean-field hadronic phase fitted to GM1 saturation properties, using both Maxwell and Gibbs constructions and a deconfinement bag shift. Tying deconfinement to chiral restoration and requiring a continuous pressure yields an upper bound on this shift. Within that bound, quark matter appears inside stable stars only for eta < 1/2, never below about 4 n0, and only in stars between 2.2 and 2.35Msun, over a stable mass window of at most 0.02Msun. The vector strength that pure quark stars need to become massive prevents deconfinement in hybrid stars. Radii and tidal deformabilities of intermediate-mass stars are therefore set by the hadronic EoS alone; with the softer SLy4 EoS the transition moves to the maximum-mass configuration itself.

title: Measurement of the electron capture of 76 As into the first excited state of 76 Ge
abstract: The neutrinoless double beta decay of $^{76}$Ge is searched for in the large-scale experiment LEGEND. The measurement of the half-life of this process would give access to the neutrino mass using the nuclear matrix element. Experimentally the contribution of the $^{76}$As ground state to the nuclear matrix element can be investigated via the branching ratios of its $\beta^-$ and electron capture decay. While energetically, the electron capture of $^{76}$As into the first excited state of $^{76}$Ge is possible and was measured once before this work, the electron capture into the $^{76}$Ge ground state was not observed yet. The present study investigates the branching of $^{76}$As that is produced via $^{75}$As(n,$\gamma$) on a thin As$_2$O$_3$ sample. A silicon drift detector measures characteristic X-rays emitted by the germanium atoms caused by an inner vacancy after the electron capture. A high-purity germanium detector is used to measure the 562.9$\,$keV $\gamma$-rays emitted after electron capture into the excited state. Investigation of coincident signals in both detectors leads to the branching ratio of the $^{76}$As electron capture into the first excited state of $^{76}$Ge of $\nu_{\mathrm{EC}^\ast} = (0.0572 \pm 0.0029 (\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 0.0074(\mathrm{syst.}))\%$. This is the first measurement with the full uncertainty budget quantified.

title: Universal Z 2 / 3 / Q α scaling law in alpha decay from nuclei to neutron-star mergers
Galactic Cosmic-Ray Transport in the Giant Circumgalactic Medium Halo
abstract: Abstract Recent observations have revealed that the Milky Way is embedded in a massive circumgalactic medium (CGM) extending to several hundred kpc. Such an extended gaseous halo acts as both a reservoir of baryons and potentially as a confinement volume for Galactic cosmic rays (CRs). We investigate CR transport in this giant Galactic halo and compare its properties with those of conventional small-halo models. In the giant-halo scenario, the halo height is no longer a free parameter, but instead relates to the extent of the source region. We show that CR transport within the source region remains similar to that in small-halo models, while substantial differences emerge at larger distances. In the giant-halo scenario, CRs develop an extended approximately 1/ r spatial tail and exhibit a broader age distribution than the small-halo case. This model is shown to be consistent with current secondary-to-primary CR measurements. We further find that uncertainties associated with Galactic gas distributions are comparable to those arising from nuclear spallation cross sections. These results suggest that the giant-halo model provides a physically motivated alternative to conventional small-halo models and may have important implications for diffuse gamma-ray and neutrino emission from the Galactic environment.

title: First observation and interpretation of ion cyclotron emission from energetic ions accelerated by lower hybrid waves in a tokamak plasma
abstract: Abstract We report the first observation of ion cyclotron emission (ICE) during lower hybrid wave (LHW) and electron cyclotron resonance heating in a tokamak plasma, and subsequently interpret the resulting ICE spectrum using linear kinetic plasma theory to infer characteristics of the bulk plasma and of the fast-ion distribution. ICE spectra from deuterium plasmas in the EAST tokamak exhibit peaks at successive deuterium cyclotron harmonics, consistent with the collective relaxation of energetic deuterium ions through the magnetosonic cyclotron instability (MCI). By carrying out a multi-dimensional parameter scan of MCI growth rates in high-resolution two-dimensional (k//, k⊥) wavenumber space, we obtain best-fit values for the magnetic field, plasma density, background electron and ion temperature, concentration of fast deuterons, and the fast-ion pitch and bulk velocities parallel and perpendicular to the applied magnetic field, which are consistent with the observations within the assumptions of the model. The spectrum is consistent with emission from deuterons with an indicative energy of 770 keV, plausibly accelerated through LHW–ion interactions. Owing to the simplifying assumptions of the model — including an infinite, homogeneous plasma, a ring-beam fast-ion distribution, and the restriction to linear theory — the derived parameters should be regarded as indicative and qualitative rather than as definitive measurements. These results nevertheless suggest that ICE may serve as a passive diagnostic of energetic ion populations and warrant further investigation of the ICE–LHW connection, which may assist alpha-channeling scenarios for ash removal and boosting fusion gain.

title: Estimating cosmogenic backgrounds in nEXO at SNOLAB using Geant4 and FLUKA
abstract: The nEXO experiment was designed to search for neutrinoless double beta decay in the isotope $^{136}$Xe, using a five-tonne, isotopically-enriched liquid xenon time projection chamber (TPC). To meet nEXO's sensitivity goal, significant effort is placed on background mitigation strategies. Here, we evaluate the expected cosmogenic background rate for nEXO if placed at its preferred underground host site, SNOLAB. A comparison of results from Geant4 and FLUKA Monte Carlo simulations are presented. We perform detailed Monte Carlo simulations of muons reaching the underground SNOLAB environment using both Geant4 and FLUKA to study the production of radioactive isotopes from both direct spallation reactions or subsequent neutron-induced reactions. We find that, of the isotopes produced, the only one of concern for nEXO is $^{137}$Xe, produced by neutron capture on the xenon target. We develop a veto strategy that achieves an anticipated 92\% \xe{137} rejection efficiency while keeping dead time to less than 1 day over a 10 year exposure.

title: Observation of the Rare Decay η → μ + μ − e + e −
abstract: A first observation of the rare decay η → μ + μ − e + e − is reported by the CMS Collaboration at the CERN LHC. The result is based on a proton-proton collision data sample at s = 13.6 TeV corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 38.0 fb − 1 , acquired in 2022 using a high-rate dimuon trigger. Using the η → μ + μ − γ decay channel for normalization, the branching fraction is measured to be B ( η → μ + μ − e + e − ) = ( 2.4 ± 0.8 ) × 10 − 6 , with the uncertainty including statistical and systematic sources as well as the B ( η → μ + μ − γ ) uncertainty. This result is about a factor of 3 smaller than the existing limit and is consistent with recent theoretical predictions.

title: Probing core excitation in the breakup of 8 B with state-of-the-art nuclear structure inputs
Impact on Final-State Bulk Observables in Heavy-Ion Collisions from an Extended MC Glauber Model of Quantum Rotors
abstract: Nuclear structure is closely connected to anisotropic flow in central heavy-ion collisions (HICs), so flow observables provide important probes for constraining nuclear deformation. Conventional Monte Carlo (MC) models typically describe deformed nuclei as classical rotors with definite orientations, whereas the ground states of even--even nuclei with $J=0$ are rotationally invariant. Motivated by the importance of rotational symmetry restoration, we systematically investigate symmetric collisions involving the representative even--even nuclei $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, $^{28}\mathrm{Si}$, $^{96}\mathrm{Ru}$, and $^{238}\mathrm{U}$ using an extended MC Glauber model that incorporates quantum superposition of nuclear orientations. In the final state, the quantum treatment suppresses elliptic flow $v_2\{2\}$, with the strongest effect observed in ultra-central Ne+Ne collisions. Quantum superposition further induces system-dependent changes in normalized symmetric cumulants and shifts the Pearson correlation between $v_2^2$ and $[p_T]$ toward the corresponding near-spherical reference values. Moreover, the quantum treatment modifies cross-system flow ratios and the U+U/Au+Au covariance ratio used experimentally to constrain nuclear deformation parameters. Our results suggest that the quantum-rotor treatment may affect the interpretation of nuclear structure information inffered from heavy-ion collision final-state observables.

title: From wave-function to fireball geometry: the role of a restored broken symmetry in ultra-relativistic collisions of deformed nuclei
abstract: Monte Carlo (MC) Glauber models for high-energy nuclear collisions conventionally treat deformed nuclei as classical rotors, encoding deformation in the one-body distribution of a single intrinsic state. The physical nuclear ground state, however, is rotationally invariant and describes a quantum rotor: a coherent superposition of intrinsic states at different orientations, with shape information encoded in many-nucleon correlations. For axially deformed even-even nuclei, we develop a modified MC Glauber sampling procedure consistent with this rotational symmetry. The model retains information off-diagonal in the basis of orientations through an angular overlap function and a generalized thickness function. We provide a practical prescription for computing both quantities and show that the rotational symmetry of the nuclear ground state is important in central collisions involving light, strongly deformed nuclei: for ${}^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, the elliptic eccentricity is reduced by approximately $10\%$ level relative to the classical-rotor treatment. These results highlight the importance of incorporating quantum-mechanical constraints when relating intrinsic nuclear deformation to the QGP geometry in relativistic nuclear collisions.

title: Evidence for octupole correlations in $^{77}{\rm Br}$ from lifetime measurements
Evaluation of $2\nu\beta\beta$ decay nuclear matrix elements using Lanczos techniques preserving Gamow-Teller strengths from both parent and daughter nuclei
abstract:
We present two efficient shell-model approaches for calculating nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) for two-neutrino double-beta ($2
u eta eta$) decay and two-neutrino double-electron capture ($2
u$ECEC), based on the Lanczos strength-function and block-Lanczos techniques. The dual-sided Lanczos strength-function (DLSF) and block-Lanczos strength-function (BLSF) methods avoid the explicit calculation of a complete set of exact intermediate $1^+$ eigenstates and yield fully converged NMEs with a relatively small number of iterations starting from Gamow--Teller (GT) doorway states. Both methods simultaneously preserve the total GT strengths associated with the initial and final nuclei. We benchmark the methods for $^{48}$Ca in the $fp$ shell and apply them to candidates in different mass regions, including $^{58}$Ni, $^{76}$Ge, and $^{130}$Te. For $^{48}$Ca, a calculation allowing cross-shell excitations of up to $2\hbar\omega$ in the $sdpf$ model space yields a $2
u eta eta$ NME closer to the experimental estimate than the result obtained in the $fp$ shell. For $^{58}$Ni, we present, to our knowledge, the first shell-model calculation of the $2
u eta^+$EC/$2
u$ECEC NME. Comparison with the current experimental upper limit on the NME indicates the need for a more sensitive measurement of the $2
u eta^+$EC half-life. As an independent validation, the energy-denominator-free sums obtained with the proposed methods are compared with the corresponding double-GT matrix elements calculated directly between the initial and final ground states. Their agreement demonstrates that the methods correctly recover the complete energy-denominator-free intermediate-state sums.

title: A machine learning framework of ground-state properties of finite nuclei foraccelerated Bayesian exploration : NucleiML
abstract: Abstract The global behavior of the nuclear equation of state (EoS) is commonly studied using data from finite nuclei (FN), heavy-ion collisions, and astrophysical observations of neutron stars (NS). The constraints derived from FN such as binding energies and charge radii play the most crucial role in shaping the EoS up to saturation density. The computational cost associated with explicitly incorporating these constraints presents a significant challenge especially when the aim is to explore the model uncertainties rather than optimizing a single model. We address this by introducing NucleiML (NML), a machine learning framework trained on ground-state properties of a few finite nuclei generated by a relativistic mean-field model. NML allows us to integrate FN and NS properties within a Bayesian inference framework in an efficient manner. The results demonstrate reasonable accuracy and a speedup of $\sim 10^4$ times for calculation of FN properties for a single parameter set, yielding roughly $\sim 10^3 \times$ speed up in the Bayesian framework. The present study makes the case for extending the work to a larger set of nuclei, potentially enabling future studies of NS properties to incorporate the whole nuclear chart.

title: Exact factorization of finite-range three-body matrix elements between Gaussian wave packets and its application to the $0^+$ states of $^{12}C$
abstract: We introduce finite-range three-body interactions into the $\beta-\gamma$-constrained generator coordinate method of antisymmetrized molecular dynamics. These genuine operators give saturation without an additional prescription for the projection, but require $O(A^6)$ complex exponentials at every node of the projection grid. With the graph Laplacian of the ranges, as in spectral clustering widely used in machine learning, we factorize the exponential factor of a Gaussian three-body kernel exactly into pairwise tables of $O(A^2)$ exponentials. A cofactor expansion rewrites the remaining contraction as complex matrix-matrix products. For $^{12}C$, the factorization reduces the time of the kernels with the three-body term from $530$ to $24$ times that of the two-body kernels. We apply the method to the $0^+$ states of $^{12}C$ with the Volkov, Tohsaki F1, and Kanada-En'yo--Akaishi F3B interactions, restricting the intrinsic states to time-reversal-invariant ones. Without the three-body terms of F1 and F3B, $^{12}C$ collapses far below the three $\alpha$ threshold, whereas with them the ground state lies close to its experimental position below the threshold. When we adjust the Majorana parameter to this position, the Hoyle state lies within 0.6 MeV of experiment for all three interactions.

title: Partition of initial angular momentum in nuclear fission
Examining the accessibility of the compressibility of nuclear matter from nuclear experiments
abstract: The most accurate approach to determine the compressibility of nuclear matter remains the one based on microscopic Energy Density Functionals (EDFs). Recent analyses yield a value for nuclear incompressibility modulus $K_\sat=240\pm 20$~MeV, defined in nuclear matter as the second derivative of the energy per particle at saturation density. However, we demonstrate that the compressibility modulus can be reduced to values shifted by four times the suggested uncertainty, i.e., $K_\sat\approx 160$~MeV, by providing examples based on models where the second derivative ($K_\sat$) and third derivative ($Q_\sat$) of the energy per particle at saturation density can be independently varied, while the experimental binding energies, charge radii, and ISGMR data in $^{120}$Sn and $^{208}$Pb are enforced. The present work suggests a new methodology to access the compressibility of nuclear matter from nuclear experiments, still based on microscopic models, but using EDFs containing more flexibility than the ones employed up to now. Consequences of our results for nuclear matter at supra-saturation density are also discussed by exploring the quarkyonic cross-over. We predict that, for our models with low values for $K_\sat$, the quark onset density has to be low for neutron stars to exist.

title: Shape coexisting intruder states in even Sn isotopes and their influence on the $B_{4/2}<1$ anomaly
abstract: The normal and intruder configuration states of the even $^{114-122}$Sn nuclei are described in a geometric model using a double well collective potential. It is shown that subtle changes in the potential shapes can reproduce the mass dependence of the low-lying energy levels and the associated $E0$ and $E2$ transitions. The extracted shape dynamics reveals different instances of shape coexistence with and without mixing, in all considered nuclei. This information is used to track the origin of $B_{4/2}<1$ values reported for $^{114,122}$Sn isotopes, providing thus a phenomenological interpretation.

title: Current Results on Light Hypernuclei in the WASA-FRS HypHI Experiment
abstract: The current understanding of light hypernuclei, subatomic nuclei exhibiting strangeness, is being actively investigated by several collaborations. Recent studies employing high-energy heavy-ion beams have revealed unexpected results for the three-body bound state $^3_\Lambda$H, known as the hypertriton. Experimental measurements of its lifetime and binding energy across multiple experiments have produced a puzzling situation referred to as the ``hypertriton puzzle''. This puzzle is the central focus of the data analysis from the WASA-FRS HypHI experiment at GSI-FAIR within the SuperFRS Experiment collaboration. Light hypernuclei are being investigated using 1.96 GeV/u $^6$Li beams impinging on a fixed carbon target, in conjunction with the WASA detector system and the Fragment Separator (FRS) at GSI-FAIR. The WASA-FRS experimental campaign was carried out during the first quarter of 2022. The primary objective of the experiment is to measure the lifetimes of $^3_\Lambda$H and $^4_\Lambda$H. The possible observation of the nn$\Lambda$ state constitutes the second component of the WASA-FRS research program. This contribution provides an overview of our investigation of hypernuclei. Focusing on the WASA-FRS HypHI experiment, details of the current analysis status are presented.

title: Active-subspace learning reveals dominant parameter directions in nuclear observables
abstract: Nuclear observables computed using ab initio methods can depend on many low-energy constants (LECs) of the underlying chiral effective field theory interactions, while being sensitive to only a few LEC combinations. We use active-subspace learning to identify these dominant parameter directions directly from many-body calculations. For ground-state energies and charge radii of oxygen isotopes, we find that more than 99% of the gradient-based variation is concentrated along a single direction for each observable in the 17-dimensional LEC space. Comparing these directions across nuclei and observables quantifies similarities in their LEC dependence. The same analysis yields derivative-based global sensitivities without requiring a global emulator. Active-subspace directions can also serve as an efficient representation for emulation, greatly improving Gaussian-process emulators especially for broad LEC variations. We demonstrate this for Hartree-Fock calculations of $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$, where the emulator error is improved with active-subspace learning by more than two orders of magnitude.

title: Evolution of chiral geometry along the odd-odd 74 − − 84 Rb isotopic chain: A triaxial projected shell model analysis
Design of a 170 GHz waveguide-based notch filter for burning plasma diagnostics protection
abstract: Intense stray radiation from high-power 170 GHz gyrotrons used for electron cyclotron heating in magnetic confinement fusion devices poses a severe threat to sensitive microwave diagnostic receivers. To protect these critical front-end systems in next-generation burning plasma experiments, this paper presents ENOCH (Electromagnetic Notch Protection of Electron Cyclotron Heating), a novel 170 GHz waveguide-based notch filter. Engineered within a standard WR-06 waveguide geometry, the proposed eight-cavity resonant structure provides robust power protection without sacrificing diagnostic performance. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations demonstrate an exceptional rejection depth exceeding 60 dB at the 170 GHz interference frequency alongside a remarkably low insertion loss across the primary 134–166 GHz diagnostic passband. Furthermore, a coupled electromagnetic-thermal analysis confirms the filter’s structural resilience under 100 W of continuous-wave input power. Compact, manufacturable, and easily integrated, the ENOCH design fulfills the stringent operational criteria required for reliable diagnostic protection in high-power, harsh environments typical of ITER- and ARC-class tokamaks.

title: Global polarization of $\Lambda$, $\Xi$, and $\Omega$ hyperons in Au+Au collisions from the RHIC Beam Energy Scan-II
abstract: Global polarization of $\Lambda$, $\Xi$, and $\Omega$ hyperons is measured in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=7.7$, 9.2, 11.5, 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27~GeV using high-statistics data from the second phase of the RHIC Beam Energy Scan. No significant difference between the $\Lambda$ and $\bar{\Lambda}$ polarizations is observed over the measured collision-energy range, providing improved constraints on magnetic-field-induced contributions. The $\Lambda$ polarization increases with the magnitude of rapidity, with the slope of the linear fit differing from zero by 4.8 standard deviations, providing the first evidence for a nonzero rapidity dependence of global polarization in this energy range. Global polarization of $\Xi^{-}+\bar{\Xi}^{+}$ is observed for the first time at these energies at a significance exceeding 5 standard deviations, with a magnitude comparable to that of $\Lambda+\bar{\Lambda}$ and an increase toward lower collision energies. Measurements of $\Omega^{-}+\bar{\Omega}^{+}$ are compatible with a similar energy dependence and favor the decay parameter $\gamma_\Omega = +1$ with high probability under the assumption of the global polarization picture. These measurements provide new constraints on the energy evolution, rapidity dependence, and species dependence of global polarization in heavy-ion collisions.

title: Differential measurement of global polarization of $\Lambda$, $\Xi$, and $\Omega$ hyperons in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=7.7$--$27~\mathrm{GeV}$ from the RHIC Beam Energy Scan-II
abstract: We present high-precision differential measurements of the global polarization of $\Lambda$, $\Xi$, and $\Omega$ hyperons in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=7.7$, $9.2$, $11.5$, $14.6$, $17.3$, $19.6$, and $27~\mathrm{GeV}$ from the RHIC Beam Energy Scan Phase II (BES-II) using the STAR detector. The results show a clear centrality dependence, with polarization increasing toward more peripheral collisions. Within the present experimental precision, no significant dependence on transverse momentum is observed for $\Lambda$ and $\Xi$, and no significant rapidity dependence is observed for the $\Xi$. The polarization of $\Xi$ hyperons is comparable at the current precision to that of $\Lambda$ hyperons, consistent with a picture in which all hyperons acquire polarization from the same global angular momentum source, with differences arising from quark content and hadronization dynamics. These high-precision, differential measurements across centrality and $p_T$ over the measured energy ranges provide a unique test of spin--vorticity coupling and sensitivity to spin--spin correlations among hyperons with different quark content (uds, dss, and sss). The results are consistent, within current precision and under the stated spin-transfer assumptions, with a common vorticity-driven polarization mechanism across strange and multistrange hyperons. Consequently, they constrain the interplay of vorticity, magnetic fields, and quark-flavor dynamics in the produced medium.

title: Comparing the fusion of $^{19}$O and $^{20}$O ions with protons at near barrier energies
abstract: Proton capture on $^{19,20}$O nuclei was measured in inverse kinematics with the active-target detector MuSIC@Indiana using CH$_4$ as the target gas. Direct measurement of the (p,n) cross section was enabled by the intrinsically high efficiency and self-normalizing nature of the measurement. The excitation function of both (p,n) reactions exhibits an oscillatory behavior. For the neutron-rich nuclei studied, determining the (p,n) cross section provides access to the proton fusion cross section because the proton's de Broglie wavelength is much larger than that of the heavy ion. A significant suppression of the cross section in $^{19}$O compared to $^{20}$O is observed, suggesting level-density differences. While the coupled channel calculations reproduce the oscillatory behavior observed in the case of $^{20}$O, they fail to predict the oscillatory behavior observed in $^{19}$O or the overall suppression of the fusion cross section.

title: Charmonium production at energies available at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron and Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research
abstract: In this study we apply the Remler formalism to charmonium production at Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) and GSI/Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research (FAIR) energies in order to investigate the effects of baryon-rich matter on charmonium production and dissociation in heavy-ion collisions within the parton-hadron-string dynamics. As a first step the Remler formalism is tested in p + p collisions and then applied to p + A collisions in order to extract the nuclear absorption cross section of charmonium, which is then utilized in heavy-ion collisions. We find that the Remler formalism successfully describes charmonium production in heavy-ion collisions at SPS energies when an in-medium heavy quark potential is implemented, in which J / ψ dissociates near T c . Finally, the same formalism is applied to the low CERN/SPS energy and GSI/FAIR energies, where we estimate charmonium production.

title: Study of pion condensate in nuclear matter based on a Parity Doublet Model
abstract: In this work, we investigate the possibility of pion condensate in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter within a parity doublet model at zero temperature, treating the baryon and isospin chemical potentials as independent variables. We include the $\sigma$, $\pi$, $\omega$, and $\rho$ mesons and determine their mean fields from the gap equations. We introduce a novel subtraction scheme to calculate the thermodynamic potential in the no-sea approximation, in which the effective isospin chemical potential is retained in the subtraction term to remove the divergence. We find that the presence of baryons suppresses pion condensate, and that transition to the pion condensation phase is of second order. We further find that the phase boundary depends systematically on the chiral-invariant mass $m_0$: a smaller $m_0$ requires a larger critical isospin chemical potential for pion condensate. The presence of pion condensate also shifts the nuclear Liquid-Gas phase boundary toward larger baryon chemical potentials. Finally we study the existence of pion condensation phase in neutron star matter and find that pion condensate is unlikely to occur.

title: Jet quenching and its substructure dependence due to color decoherence
abstract: Motivated by color coherence and decoherence effects in the QCD medium, we propose a theoretical framework that combines vacuum-like emissions and medium-induced radiation to study jet quenching and its dependence on jet cone sizes and substructure. In our approach, a jet produced at a hard scale $Q$ first undergoes vacuum-like evolution, as described by the well-established generating-function method in the double logarithmic approximation. These vacuum-like emissions generate subjets at an infrared momentum scale $Q_0$. Each subjet then experiences medium-induced energy loss as described by the BDMPS-Z formalism. By modeling the QCD bulk medium using OSU (2+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics and treating $Q_0$ together with the jet-quenching parameters at the initial proper time of the hydrodynamic evolution as free parameters, our approach provides a very good description of the inclusive jet modification factor $R_{AA}$ for large-radius jets and its dependence on jet substructure in 0-10% PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\rm{TeV}$, as measured by the ATLAS experiment.

title: Higgs boson production classifier using weak supervision
abstract: A reliable determination of the Higgs production mechanism in hadron collider experiments is essential to the program of Higgs coupling measurements. We employ weak supervision, classification without labels (CWoLa) in particular, to train deep neural networks to distinguish vector boson fusion from gluon-gluon fusion events using simulated datasets as pseudoexperimental data, demonstrating the potential of reducing biases resulting from Monte Carlo simulations. Models based on the convolutional neural network and the transformer are tested and compared. In particular, the classification performance gets slightly better when the photon information is removed from training on the low-luminosity region of H → γ γ . We explicitly show that the performance can be improved when the training dataset is enlarged by data augmentation using physics-motivated methods. We further demonstrate that the trained model can be successfully applied to the H → Z Z and H → Z γ events, showing that such classifiers are agnostic to Higgs decay modes, provided these decay modes do not involve strong QCD corrections.

title: Design of the off-axis neutron camera for the Mega Ampere Spherical Tokamak (MAST) Upgrade
abstract: A dedicated four-channel, collimated neutron flux monitor has been designed for the Mega Ampere Spherical Tokamak (MAST) Upgrade to measure spatially resolved neutron emissivity in the off-axis Neutral Beam Injection (NBI) region, contributing to studies of fast-ion confinement and the effectiveness of plasma heating and current drive. This paper presents the design and motivation for the off-axis neutron camera (OANC) for MAST Upgrade. It describes the line-of-sight geometry, detection system, shielding configuration, and laboratory characterization of detectors using γ-ray sources. The OANC is optimized to complement the existing on-axis Neutron Camera Upgrade diagnostics and provide measurements in previously inaccessible regions. The design achieves 10% statistical accuracy with 10 ms time resolution in off-axis NBI scenarios. The diagnostic will be installed during the next engineering break and will become operational in the following campaign. The off-axis neutron camera is expected to provide valuable insights into fast-ion deposition, plasma heating, and confinement driven by off-axis NBI.

title: A multi-wavelength view of PSR J0437-4715 with NICER and other missions: Radius measurements from far-ultraviolet to hard X-ray pulse profile modeling
abstract: We report updated mass and radius measurements for the millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 obtained with pulse profile modeling of the emission from the far-ultraviolet to the hard X-rays. Using an extended 2.56 Ms Neutron Star Interior Composition ExploreR (NICER) dataset together with XMM-Newton, Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope ARray and Hubble Space Telescope observations, we perform Bayesian inference with models describing the thermal emission from hot spots of increasing complexities, together with the rest of the warm NS surface, as well as the non-thermal emission component represented by a phase-dependent (pulsed) power-law. With this comprehensive model and broadband data set, as well as radio timing priors on the mass, distance and inclination, our headline result for PSR J0437-4715 led to a mass M = 1.377(-0.034)(+0.038) Msun and an equatorial radius Req = 11.35(-0.39)(+0.40) km, one of the narrowest measurements of Req from NICER observations of millisecond pulsars. The geometric configuration favors a non-antipodal hot spot distribution, as noted in previous analyses of this pulsar. When combined with recent measurements of M and Req of other pulsars, the tight constraints from PSR J0437-4715 further reduce the allowed range of the dense matter equation of state, excluding those that predict radii above 12.0 km (at the 68% level) for all NS masses.

title: r -Process as Production of Lanthanides from Compact Object Mergers
abstract: Abstract The relative contributions of binary neutron star (BNS) and black hole–neutron star (BH-NS) mergers to the Galactic enrichment from the rapid neutron-capture process ( r -process) remain an open question in nuclear astrophysics. In this paper, we present end-to-end numerical simulations of binary population synthesis, nucleosynthesis, and Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) via Compact Object Mergers: Population Astrophysics and Statistics (COMPAS), the SkyNet network, and a stochastic multizone model, respectively. By considering five equations of state (EOSs) of NS and different spins of BH for BNS and BH-NS mergers, it is found that the averaged abundance seems not to be significantly dependent on the EOS of the neutron star (NS) and the spin of the BH for the BNS and BH-NS mergers. For the given EOSs of NS, the abundance of the BNS is higher than that of the BH-NS mergers before the second peak (for mass number A ∼ 130), but it is lower when the mass number is greater than 130. Moreover, the lighter r -process elements ( A < 130) are predominantly produced by the disk wind, while the heavier elements ( A > 130) originate mainly from the dynamical ejecta. The purely BNS mergers, on the other hand, are the dominant contributors to the production of lanthanides like europium (Eu) at the later stage of GCE, but BH-NS mergers make only a small contribution of heavy r -process elements for the Eu/Fe evolutionary tracks in the Milky Way.

title: Unveiling the Emission Mechanisms of Blazar PKS 1510−089. III. Relationship between the γ -Ray Variability and the Parsec-scale Jet
abstract: Abstract Over a 17 yr period, we analyze the multiwavelength relationship in the blazar PKS 1510-089, utilizing γ -ray, multifrequency radio (15, 43, and 230 GHz), optical spectra, and photometric data. Spearman rank correlations suggest that γ -ray production is cospatial with the 43 GHz quasi-stationary core (Q0), while the remaining decoupled from the 15 GHz core ( K 0) due to frequency-dependent opacity. A kinematic analysis identified nine superluminal components (Q2 − Q10) and a stationary feature (Q1) at ∼2.0 pc that we interpret as a downstream accelerator. To investigate the long-term evolution of jet opacity and flaring dynamics, we performed a time-resolved cross correlation analysis by dividing the dataset into four temporal epochs characterized by distinct quiescent γ -ray states. These results reveal that the kinematic transitivity of the jet is state dependent: while plasma disturbances propagate through successive τ ∼ 1 surfaces with clear, resolvable delays during quiescent and discrete flaring epochs, massive energy injections act as a low-pass filter, where extreme optical depth and spatial blending temporarily disrupt this kinematic coherence. Finally, the emergence of component Q10 in 2024 as a γ -ray dark event suggests a fundamental restructuring of the radiative environment of the jet following the 2021 high-energy quenching, likely driven by a depletion of external seed photons or enhanced internal γ -ray opacity.

title: The Skin Detector System of the LZ Dark Matter Experiment
abstract: This paper presents the design, calibration, and performance of the Skin Detector component of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) dark matter experiment. The Skin Detector consists of approximately 2 tonnes of liquid xenon instrumented with 131 photomultiplier tubes, surrounding the central time-projection chamber and functions as an active veto system for background rejection. Energy calibration with monoenergetic gamma sources established a position-dependent energy scale and determined prompt and delayed veto thresholds. Radon decays in the Skin can be identified with less than 15~mm spatial resolution, revealing stable convective flow patterns with measured velocities ranging from 2-4 mm/s that persisted throughout extended data-taking periods. The achieved Skin veto threshold meets or exceeds the design goal of 100~keV throughout the Skin volume. The prompt veto efficiency for gamma rays emitted following electron capture in $^{127}$Xe is found to be ($88 \pm 2$)\%, consistent with the simulated value of ($90.4 \pm 0.6$)\%. M-shell EC decays are used to validate the LZ detector sensitivity for low-mass dark matter during the first science run.

title: Photoneutron Yield for an Electron Beam on Tantalum and Erbium Deuteride
abstract: An electron beam may be used to generate bremsstrahlung photons that go on to create photoneutrons within metals. This serves as a low-energy neutron source for irradiation experiments [1-3]. In this article, we present simulation results for optimizing photoneutron yield for a 10-MeV electron beam on tantalum foil and erbium deuteride (ErD$_3$). The thickness of the metal layers was varied. A tantalum foil thickness of 1.5 mm resulted in the most photons reaching the second metal layer. When a second metal layer of ErD$_3$ was included, the photoneutron yield increased with the thickness of the secondary layer. When the electron beam was directly incident upon a layer of ErD$_3$, the photoneutron yield did not differ significantly from the yield when a layer of tantalum was included. The directional photoneutron yield reached a maximum level when the thickness of the ErD$_3$ layer was around 12 cm. About 1 neutron was generated per $10^4$ source electrons. When using a 2-mA beam current, it is possible to generate up to $10^{ 12}$ neutrons per second, making this combination a relatively-inexpensive neutron generator.

title: Eccentric and unbound compact binaries in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalog: Parameter estimation and waveform systematics with seobnrv6ehm
abstract: Orbital eccentricity encodes key information about compact binary formation channels and astrophysical environments, making it a critical target for gravitational-wave (GW) inference. We present parameter estimation (PE) analyses of GWs from eccentric compact binaries with the v6 waveform model. Using long, highly eccentric numerical relativity waveforms as synthetic signals, we compare parameter recovery across state-of-the-art eccentric models. We find that v5 and esum-alí can yield biased estimates of eccentricity, masses, and spins in the most challenging configurations, while v6 significantly reduces these biases. Applying v6 to 27 GW events from the O1–O4 LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing runs—including binary black hole, neutron star–black hole, and binary neutron star mergers—we identify five events with mild support for eccentricity over the quasicircular precessing-spin hypothesis, with Bayes factors log 10 B QCP EAS > 0.5 . Since v6 is applicable to generic planar binaries, we reanalyze five high-mass events allowing for unbound initial conditions. For three of them—including GW190521, previously claimed to originate from a dynamical capture—a direct-capture configuration is comparable to, or marginally favored over, both the eccentric aligned-spin and quasicircular precessing-spin hypotheses ( log 10 B QCP unbound ≈ 0.2 – 0.6 for GW190521). The recovered configurations are, however, astrophysically unrealistic and cannot be confidently discriminated from highly eccentric bound orbits, so these results do not, by themselves, support an unbound origin for these events. v6 is three to five times faster in PE analyses than v5, while improving waveform accuracy, enabling efficient, large-scale GW inference with eccentric waveforms.

title: Ton-scale Xenon Gas TPC for $0\nu\beta\beta$ Search at Atmospheric Pressure
abstract: We explore aspects of an unorthodox ton-scale xenon gas time projection chamber detector operated at normal temperature and pressure (NTP), designed for $0\nu\beta\beta$ discovery at $\sim10^{27}$ year sensitivity.
