The gravitational Olbers’ paradox and the entropic accelerating universe
abstract: The accelerating expansion of the Universe is reframed as the resolution to a gravitational analogue of Olbers’ Paradox. Because gravitational influence propagates at the speed of light—confirmed by the binary neutron star merger GW170817—each observer is surrounded by a cosmological event horizon beyond which matter exerts no gravitational pull. The horizon is a thermodynamic object: it possesses a temperature proportional to the Hubble parameter and an entropy proportional to its area. As the universe expands, the horizon grows and its entropy S H ∝ R H 2 increases geometrically—present in any expanding spacetime regardless of matter content. The second law of thermodynamics drives the universe toward states of larger horizon radius. The resulting entropic pressure, P = − 2 3 ρ crit c 2 , yields an effective equation of state ω eff = − 2 / 3 , providing accelerating expansion with no vacuum energy contribution and dissolving the cosmological constant problem without fine-tuning. The contribution of this work is to identify this result as the resolution of the gravitational Olbers’ paradox, supplying the physical justification for horizon thermodynamics that earlier entropic-force treatments acknowledged was lacking. The predicted dynamical dark energy, with ω ≠ − 1 evolving with redshift, is consistent with the 4.2 σ deviation from ΛCDM reported by the DESI Year 3 (DR2) survey.

title: Systematic investigation of density-independent and density-dependent nucleon–nucleon interactions in 16O-fusion induced reactions
abstract: A systematic investigation of fusion reactions induced by 16 O is carried out. Within the double-folding formalism, the nucleus–nucleus interaction potential is constructed using both density-independent nucleon–nucleon interactions (B3Y-Fetal, M3Y-Paris, and M3Y-Reid) and density-dependent interactions (BDM3Y1, CDM3Y6, and DDM3Y1). The reactions 16 O + 70 , 72 , 74 , 76 G e , 16 O + 112 , 116 , 118 , 120 S n , 16 O + 144 , 148 , 154 S m , 16 O + 186 W and 16 O + 208 P b are considered. Two groups of interactions exhibiting similar fusion cross sections are identified, with the similarities becoming more pronounced as the target mass increases. On one hand, potentials derived from the B3Y-Fetal and BDM3Y1 interactions yield comparable fusion cross sections; on the other hand, those obtained from the M3Y-Paris, M3Y-Reid, CDM3Y6, and DDM3Y1 interactions also produce similar results. The former group generally provides a better description of the experimental data, except for the 120 Sn for which the latter group offers the best fit. The analysis of the channel couplings strength reveals that BDM3Y1 interaction corresponds to the strongest channel couplings. It is also observed that the strength of channel couplings does not vary monotonically with the atomic mass, as might be expected. In light of these results, it follows that the B3Y-Fetal and BDM3Y1 nucleon-nucleon interactions systematically provide a better description of the experimental data. Furthermore, there are no specific features in the fusion cross sections that can be attributed solely to whether the nucleon-nucleon interaction is density-dependent or density-independent. This conclusion is supported by the identified two groups of nucleon-nucleon interactions, each containing density-dependent and density-independent interactions.

title: Subleading D-like three-nucleon interactions
abstract: We consider subleading contributions to the three-nucleon force from tree-level diagrams involving a single-pion exchange and a contact interaction between two nucleons, which appear at fifth order in the chiral expansion. We show that the corresponding D-like three-nucleon potential depends on 16 low-energy constants, which need to be determined from few-body data. Assuming that their numerical values are governed by the intermediate {\Delta}(1232) excitation mechanism, the considered three-nucleon force can be approximated using 4 low-energy constants that parametrize the short-range nucleon-nucleon to nucleon-{\Delta} transition amplitude.

title: Semiclassical analysis of fusion dynamics of ⁶Li with ⁹⁶Zr, ¹⁴⁴Sm, and ²⁰⁹Bi targets using phenomenological potentials at near barrier energies
abstract: We have analyzed the complete, incomplete, and total fusion excitation functions for reactions involving the weakly bound projectile ⁶Li on ⁹⁶Zr, ¹⁴⁴Sm, and ²⁰⁹Bi targets at around barrier energies by employing a semi-classical approach considering different nuclear interaction potentials. The study shows that the Aage-Winther (AW 95), Broglia-Winther (BW 91), and an independently fitted Woods-Saxon (WS) potentials provide overall good agreement with the experimental data across all systems, while the Christensen-Winther (CW 76) potential reproduces the behaviour reasonably well for the heavier targets (¹⁴⁴Sm and ²⁰⁹Bi) in the near and above barrier region. In contrast, the Bass 73 potential fails to reproduce the data consistently, as its lower predicted barrier height enhances tunnelling and leads to deviations in the sub-barrier and near-barrier regions. In addition, the calculated total fusion excitation functions are found to be in good agreement with the predictions of the empirical EBD2.2 model. Also, it is found through the comparison of the results of the fusion induced by the stable 12 C projectile on 92 Zr, 144 Sm, and 208 Pb targets with those of above mentioned systems that the breakup effects are pronounced only in case of weakly bound projectile.

title: Near-threshold OPE constraints and high-energy diffractive dynamics in J/ψ photoproduction
abstract: We study the forward J/ψN amplitude M ψ N ( λ ) using a leading-twist Coulombic operator-product expansion, exact physical-domain target-mass resummation, and modern gluon PDFs. Forward-intercept extrapolations reported by GlueX and CLAS12 constrain the amplitude modulus within a vector-meson-dominance normalization. After fitting an overall scale and a subtraction constant, the exact-TMC and no-TMC descriptions differ by only Δ χ 2 = 0.021 , while a two-parameter empirical exponential gives an equally good fit. The point C s u b = 0 changes the profiled minimum by only 0.033. Current near-threshold data therefore determine neither the target-mass correction nor the subtraction constant separately. An independent correlated fit to HERA data gives δ = 0.695 ± 0.023 . The absence of direct-proton measurements between W ≃ 4.73 and 20 GeV prevents a data-driven determination of the crossover to high-energy diffraction.

title: Holographic dark energy in Einstein-Cartan spin cosmology
abstract: We show that, in Einstein-Cartan theory, the torsion scalar modifies the dust-like equation of state of non-interacting holographic dark energy with the Hubble radius as the infrared cutoff, enabling late-time cosmic acceleration within the low-redshift domain of validity, which is not realized in the corresponding model in general relativity. Using the same holographic dark energy background, we further derive the torsion-induced modification of the cosmic distance duality relation, $d_L=d_A(1+z)^2(1+η)$. In the late-time universe, the magnitude of the deviation parameter, $|η|$, is small but non-vanishing, reflecting the cumulative effect of torsion along the light-propagation path.

title: Exploring the scenarios of non-singular bouncing cosmology in f(Q,Lm) gravity
abstract: In this work we explore the non-singular bouncing scenarios in the framework of 𝑓 ⁡ ( 𝑄 , ℒ 𝑚 ) gravity, where the gravitational action depends on the non-metricity scalar ( Q ) and matter Lagrangian density ( ℒ 𝑚 ) . Using the functional form 𝑓 ⁡ ( 𝑄 , ℒ 𝑚 ) = − 𝛼 ⁢ 𝑄 + 2 ⁢ ℒ 𝑚 + 𝛽 , two different bouncing scenario models are analyzed in a homogeneous, isotropic and flat FLRW universe. The cosmological evolution is analyzed through the behavior of the Hubble parameter, deceleration parameter, energy density, pressure, and equation of state parameter. Both models exhibit a successful bounce characterized by a smooth transition from a contracting universe ( H 0) without encountering any initial singularity ( 𝐻 = 0 ) . The EOS parameter exhibits phantom crossing behavior, while the energy conditions reveal NEC and SEC violation around the bounce, consistent with bouncing cosmology requirements. Stability analysis through metric perturbations and adiabatic index confirms stable late-time cosmic evolution. The study suggests that 𝑓 ⁡ ( 𝑄 , ℒ 𝑚 ) theory offers a promising geometrical background for understanding non-singular early universe dynamics and bouncing scenarios.

title: Elastic deuteron-deuteron scattering in the 5S2 channel within nuclear lattice effective field theory
abstract: We calculate low-energy deuteron-deuteron scattering in the spin-quintet $^{5}S_2$ channel using nuclear lattice effective field theory. The calculation combines chiral interactions at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order, implemented through wavefunction matching, with the adiabatic projection method. Because the radial cluster basis develops small norm-matrix eigenvalues at large Euclidean projection time, we investigate two stabilization procedures: Tikhonov regularization and projection onto well-resolved norm eigenmodes. The two procedures yield consistent Coulomb-subtracted phase shifts within their statistical and numerical uncertainties. A Coulomb-modified effective-range analysis gives ${}^5a_{dd} = (11.99 \pm 0.22)$ fm and ${}^5r_{dd} = (3.44 \pm 0.79)$ fm. The phase shifts are more negative, and the scattering length is substantially larger than in previous calculations, corresponding to a stronger effective repulsion in the $^{5}S_2$ channel. These results provide a first nuclear-lattice benchmark for deuteron-deuteron scattering and establish a starting point for future coupled-channel calculations of the deuteron-induced reactions relevant to big-bang nucleosynthesis.

title: Co-production of Fission-Activation methods for Mo-99
Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints on f(Q,C) gravity
abstract: In this work, we examine Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) within the framework of f ( Q, C ) gravity by considering three representative functional forms of the gravitational Lagrangian. The first model is constructed from quadratic contributions involving the nonmetricity scalar Q and the boundary term C . The second employs a separable form containing the standard linear dependence on Q together with a logarithmic correction associated with C , whereas the third model introduces a multiplicative coupling between Q and C . For each scenario, we investigate the background dynamics during the radiation-dominated phase and assess whether the resulting expansion history is compatible with the requirements of successful BBN. We subsequently derive constraints on the corresponding model parameters by confronting the predicted primordial abundances of the principal light elements, with particular emphasis on helium-4 and deuterium. Among the three cases considered, the second model yields the most favorable agreement with the observationally inferred primordial abundances of helium-4 and deuterium, thereby identifying a viable region of its parameter space.

title: Study of radiative proton capture by the 7 Be nucleus with the use of ab initio approaches*
abstract: Abstract A theoretical study of the 7 Be( p , γ ) 8 B reaction in the "astrophysical" energy range with the use of ab initio methods is presented. The used approaches are No-Core Shell Model and Cluster Channels Orthogonal Functions Method. The scheme also contains elements of R-matrix theory and procedures for extrapolating various data obtained in ab initio computations. The developed approach as a whole allows one not only to calculate the astrophysical S -factor and all nuclear characteristics that determine its value, but also to evaluate the reliability of the obtained results and to identify the dominant reaction mechanisms against a background of insignificant ones. The high accuracy of the obtained results and has been demonstrated.

title: Investigation for antimagnetic rotational structure in 107,109,111 Pd*
abstract: Abstract Partial level schemes of have been reported in the literature, and antimagnetic rotational bands were recently predicted within the cranked shell model for the negative-parity bands of and , although lifetime data and semiclassical particle-rotor model studies are still unavailable. Electric quadrupole ( ) transitions have also been observed in the negative-parity band of , for which the rotational structure has not yet been theoretically investigated within the semiclassical particle-rotor framework. Over the past decade, the semiclassical particle-rotor model has been extensively applied to antimagnetic rotational bands in various nuclei, successfully explaining the generation of angular momentum through the shears mechanism and reproducing the observed systematics of excitation energies and transition rates. In the present work, the negative-parity bands of are investigated within the semiclassical particle-rotor model, where angular momentum is generated through the closing of proton-hole shears toward the neutron-particle angular momentum vector involving high- j orbitals. The calculated values decrease with increasing spin, while the ratio increases for the negative-parity bands of , consistent with the characteristic signatures of antimagnetic rotation.

title: Exploring the origin of D0 meson elliptic flow in PbPb collisions at sNN=5.02TeV using event shape engineering
Dual gamma-ray and thermal neutron counter based on BGO and GAGG scintillators coupled to silicon photomultipliers
Cs2LiYCl6:Pr,Ca single crystal: An efficient neutron-gamma resolving scintillator
Correlation between nuclear bubble structure and EMC effect
abstract: Abstract The correlation between the nuclear bubble structure and the EMC effect is investigated within the framework of T. D. Lee's soliton bag model and the double Q 2 -rescaling model. For 27 Al, we artificially reduce its central density via a three-parameter Fermi distribution of nucleon density while conserving the mass number. It is found that as the central density decreases, nucleons are redistributed from the interior to the surface, leading to a systematic reduction in the average nucleon swelling factor, rescaling parameters and the EMC slope. However, this single-parameter modification fails to simultaneously reproduce both the magnitude and the slope of the experimental EMC ratio within the same parameter set, suggesting that additional nuclear medium effects must be considered. For the density distributions of the candidate bubble nucleus 48 Si, we calculate them by the Skyrme-Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov (SHFB) theory with the SLy4, SKM * and LNS interactions, while the density profiles given by the PKA1 interaction are taken from the relativistic Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov (RHFB) calculation (Phys. Lett. B 788 , 192 (2019)). Among the PKA1, SLy4 and SKM * interactions, a stronger bubble structure correlates with a larger nucleon swelling factor and a stronger EMC effect. The LNS interaction, however, presents an exception: despite having a weaker bubble, it yields the largest EMC effect, owing to its systematically higher overall nuclear density. This demonstrates that the EMC effect in bubble nuclei depends on both the bubble strength and the global density scale set by the effective interaction.

title: Application of energy-compensated G-M counter in the measurement of gamma ambient dose equivalent in reference neutron fields
Preface
Microscopic structure of the quasi-γ bands in 128,130Xe
Evaluating the efficacy of polymer gel dosimeter, N-vinylcaprolactam (PNVCl), with sodium chloride (NaCl) salts in pulse-echo ultrasound gel dosimetry
abstract: Poly(N-vinylcaprolactam) (PNVCl) is a polymer that has a lower critical solution temperature (LCST) when it is mixed with water. We present the inaugural ultrasonic assessment to determine the efficacy of this novel polymer gel dosimeter. The study investigated the correlation between the absorbed radiation dosage, the velocity of travel, and the attenuation of ultrasonic waves in PNVCl polymer gel dosimeters. The gel dosimeter was prepared by combining gelatin type A, distilled water, the BIS, PNVCl, sodium chloride (NaCl), and tetrakis (hydroxymethyl) phosphonium chloride (THPC). We conducted the first experiment without adding the salts. However, the salts were introduced into the BIS-acrylamide gel to improve the dose-response characteristics of the gel dosimeter. The gel samples underwent irradiation in a water phantom at several doses utilizing 6 MV Linac X-ray beams with a dosage rate of 200 cGy/min. We calibrated the ultrasonic systems with a frequency range of 1-4 MHz and measured the ultrasound velocity and attenuation coefficient of the gel samples. The efficacy of ultrasonic parameters was examined in measuring dosage rates using the dose-response curve. The examination of the velocity of sound and the attenuation coefficient showed a strong linear connection between the applied radiation and the resulting dose response values. It can attribute the linear correlation to the uniform dispersion of the salts and the consistent characteristics of the gel substance, thereby validating the gels' capacity to accurately monitor radiation dosage. The results demonstrate the versatility of polymer gel dosimeters as a common material for measuring radiation dosage, making them suitable for a wide range of applications.

title: Editorial Board
A BP neural network-based model for the neutron ambient dose equivalent estimation along flight routes in China
abstract: This study developed a BP neural network model to approximate calculations of route-integrated neutron ambient dose equivalent, along commercial flight routes in China. The CARI-7A was used to calculate the neutron ambient dose equivalent (H∗(10)), for 696 domestic flight routes at cruising altitudes ranging from 8000 to 12 000 m. Based on these CARI-7A-derived results, a Back Propagation (BP) neural network was trained using input variables including cruising altitude, cruising time, and geographical information. Trained, validated, and tested using 14 616 data points to ensure predictive accuracy, the BP neural network demonstrated excellent performance with an adjusted R2 of 0.9998 and a minimal mean square error (MSE) of 0.0002; when compared with measured neutron H∗(10) data from 30 domestic flight routes, the model predictions showed an average relative deviation of 14.00%, with 80.0% of the routes falling within ±20% of the measured values. The developed BP neural network model provides a rapid approximation of neutron H∗(10) for Chinese air routes. Rather than replacing direct radiation measurements, the model may serve as a supplementary tool for preliminary route-level assessment of neutron H∗(10), particularly for routes not conveniently covered by direct measurements or CARI-7A airport settings. Further validation with a larger number of measured flights is still needed before broader operational application.

title: Particle geodesics, shadows and accretion disk luminosity of a Dehnen (1,4,5/2)-Schwarzschild black hole
abstract: One of the central questions in strong-gravity astrophysics is whether a surrounding dark matter distribution can create measurable imprints on black hole observables in the strong-field region. To explore this, we study a Schwarzschild black hole located in a Dehnen (1,4,5/2) dark matter halo using the self-consistent framework introduced by Bolokhov. We investigate how the halo parameters ( ρ s , r s ) modify the spacetime geometry and affect the motion of null and timelike particles near the black hole. Specifically, we focus on light paths related to the photon sphere, black hole shadow, lensing, transfer functions, and the grouping of direct, lensed, and photon-ring paths gathered through backward ray tracing. We further study thin accretion-disk observables within the Novikov–Thorne formalism, including the ISCO radius, radiative flux, temperature distribution, and differential luminosity. Finally, by confronting the predicted shadow size with the Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*, we place model dependent observational constraints on the allowed parameter space of the dark matter halo.

title: Measurement of the Z →μ+μ− angular coefficients in pp collisions at s= 13 TeV as functions of transverse momentum and rapidity
abstract: A measurement of the eight angular polarization coefficients, $ A_0 $ to $ A_7 $, in the cross section for the Drell--Yan production of two muons is presented. The analysis is based on proton-proton (pp) collision data recorded with the CMS detector at the LHC at a center-of-mass energy of $ \sqrt{s}= $ 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb$ ^{-1} $. The coefficients are determined double differentially in eight intervals of transverse momentum and two intervals of rapidity of the muon pair $ \mu^{+}\mu^{-} $. The results are presented for the $ \mu^{+}\mu^{-} $ invariant mass range 81--101 GeV and are compared with theoretical predictions calculated at next-to-next-to-leading order in perturbative quantum chromodynamics. The measurement provides relevant information about the underlying partonic dynamics and the Z boson production mechanisms.

title: Measurement of dijet angular distributions and search for beyond the standard model physics in proton-proton collisions at s=13TeV
abstract: A measurement is presented of dijet angular distributions in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 TeV , using data collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 f b − 1 . For the first time, the dijet angular distributions, corrected for detector effects, are compared with the predictions of perturbative quantum chromodynamics at next-to-next-to-leading order, including next-to-leading-order electroweak corrections. While data are generally found to be in agreement with predictions, a small difference in shape of the normalized distributions is seen for dijet masses ranging from 2.4 to 4.8 TeV and above 6TeV. The distributions are used to search for proposed signatures of quark compositeness, extra spatial dimensions, quantum black holes, dark-matter mediators, axion-like particles, and anomalous gluon couplings. The most stringent limits to date are set for most of these scenarios. Quark contact interactions are excluded at 95% confidence level (CL) up to a scale of 17 (37)TeV for destructive (constructive) interference in a benchmark scenario, valid to next-to-leading order in quantum chromodynamics, and in which only left-handed quarks participate. The coupling of axion-like particles to the gluon, c g / f a , is constrained to be lower than 0.42 T e V − 1 at 95% CL. The anomalous triple-gluon coupling, C G /Λ 2 , in a standard model effective field theory is constrained to be lower than 0.0076 T e V − 2 at 95% CL.

title: Enhanced dark matter quantum sensing via phase-space geometric interferometry
abstract: We propose a quantum sensing protocol for coupled qubit-oscillator systems that enhances the sensitivity by exploiting a geometric phase for dark matter searches. Instead of letting the cavity evolve freely under a weak dark matter background, we combine large coherent displacements and squeezing operations within the evolution protocol, thereby mapping the signal onto an enhanced quantum phase determined by the geometric area enclosed in phase space. Relative to the conventional free-evolution scheme, the protocol enhances the quantum Fisher information and improves the projected sensitivities to cavity-based detection of dark-photon and axion dark matter.
