Vortex stability in pseudo-Hermitian theories
abstract: Pseudo-Hermitian (including 𝒫 𝒯 -symmetric) field theories support phenomenology that cannot be replicated in standard Hermitian theories. We describe a concrete example in which the vortex solutions that are realised in a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian field theory exhibit a novel metastability, despite the model parameters residing within the naively stable regime of exact antilinear symmetry of the vacuum theory. This instability is identified analytically and confirmed through numerical simulations, and it arises from the small breaking of the underlying antilinear symmetry of the pseudo-Hermitian theory due to the presence of the topological defect. This leads to spacetime-dependent parameters in the equations of motion governing fluctuations around the vortex, inducing non-trivial exceptional-point structures and complex frequencies within their spectrum. Aside from offering intriguing possibilities for cosmology, this result serves to illustrate the ability to produce long-lived metastable configurations in pseudo-Hermitian field theories of relevance beyond cosmology and high energy physics.

title: Topological inversion of the Schwarzschild event horizon: Causal decoupling in the conformally flat ghost star
abstract: Utilizing the conformally flat ghost star characterized by a specific exotic energy density profile (Herrera et al., 2024) as a theoretical laboratory, we investigate the geometric implications of its interior spacetime. Specifically, we analyze the components of its metric, calculate the proper radial distance, the null affine parameter, and the coordinate time interval within the stellar interior. Our analysis reveals a coordinate singularity at r = r m = 2 r Σ / 3 that represents a topological inversion of the Schwarzschild event horizon: while the coordinate time required to reach r m is finite, the proper distance and null affine parameter diverge. This coordinate singularity acts as a geometric horizon, ensuring that the central curvature singularity remains geodesically distant and causally decoupled from the exterior spacetime. Consequently, we discuss how this enforces the cosmic censorship hypotheses (CCH) through geometric depth rather than temporal freezing.

title: Topological graviton mass generation and Chern-Simons graviton scattering amplitudes
abstract: We study the mechanism of topological mass generation in 3d topologically massive gravity (TMG). We establish a Topological Graviton Equivalence Theorem (TGRET) to uncover this mechanism. We formulate TMG in Weyl-transformed variables by introducing a compensating (unphysical) dilaton field that decouples in unitary gauge. In the Weyl-transformed TMG (WTMG), the massive graviton has one physical degree of freedom, which will be transferred to the dilaton field in the massless limit. We present the BRST quantization of the WTMG and prove the TGRET to all loop orders for the first time. The TGRET connects each N -point graviton scattering amplitude to the dilaton amplitude in the high-energy limit. Using the TGRET, we prove in general that the N -point Chern-Simons graviton amplitudes ( N ≥ 4) have striking high-energy cancellations that ensure good ultraviolet behavior. In particular, the four-point and five-point graviton amplitudes respectively exhibit substantial high-energy cancellations at tree level, E 12 → E 1 and E 15 → E 0 , in TMG.

title: Thermodynamic volumes of extended black hole thermodynamics with auxiliary gauge fields
abstract: By applying the Iyer-Wald formalism to the modified Lagrangian form for the gravitational system, where the coupling constants appearing in the original Lagrangian form, such as the cosmological constant, are promoted to the dynamical scalar fields by introducing the corresponding auxiliary gauge fields, we derive the first law of the extended black hole thermodynamics, where the resulting thermodynamic volumes as the conjugate thermodynamic variables to the coupling constants are nevertheless independent of the auxiliary gauge fields and exactly the same as those obtained before via varying the coupling constants by brute force. In addition, it is further shown that such volumes can also be expressed in terms of the auxiliary gauge fields and evaluated on the black hole horizon, validating the proposal made in the previous literature.

title: The generalized i-boson model and the BUC hierarchy
abstract: In this paper, we develop the generalized i -boson algebra and its Fock-space representation. By means of the quantum inverse scattering method, the ( N, N )-particle states and scalar products of the generalized i -boson model are expressed in terms of the generalized Q -functions, which are (restricted) τ functions of the BUC hierarchy. Furthermore, the shifted topological vertex without boundary conditions is shown to admit a vacuum expectation value representation using vertex operators associated with generalized Q -functions.

title: Testing a quantum motivated effective black hole geometry with photon ring and orbital diagnostics
abstract: We analyze a one parameter static spherical deformation of Schwarzschild containing an r − 3 term. This term is treated as a quantum motivated effective template rather than a unique microscopic prediction, while the factor 256 π in the alternative parameter η is identified as a normalization convention. From the same geometry we derive the horizon, photon sphere, critical impact parameter, timelike circular orbit, ISCO, radiative efficiency, and epicyclic frequency diagnostics. Mapping the fiducial 68 percent EHT Sgr A* shadow size intervals yields − 1 ≤ χ ≤ 0.863 for the Keck calibration and − 1 ≤ χ ≤ 0.156 for the VLTI calibration. The screen polarimetric construction is used only as a fiducial tangential reference on the critical curve. At small deformation, comparison with the leading conservative Schwarzschild self force gives equal ISCO frequency shifts at | χ | ≃ 3.70 q ; under genuinely Planck suppressed matching, however, the geometric shift is negligible relative to self force for astrophysical extreme mass ratio systems. The correlated null and timelike observables define a falsifiable metric level diagnostic.

title: Spontaneous wandering of the magnetic axis in pulsars: 3D magneto-thermal simulations and the imprint on braking indices
abstract: The braking index measurements of hundreds of pulsars, despite the observational caveats, show a clear trend: n<3 at early ages, n>3 at middle ages, and increasingly large, fluctuating values at larger characteristic ages. Crustal magnetic fields in isolated neutron stars evolve through Ohmic dissipation and non-linear Hall redistribution across scales, with additional early-time contributions from the chiral instability and from post-burial re-emergence. Initial conditions are usually assumed dipole-dominated, whereas more complex and realistic fields, with energy spread more evenly over a broad range of scales, have not been explored in the context of the braking index. We assess how the internal dynamics of initially non-trivial crustal fields change the dipolar field strength and obliquity, and compare their combined contribution to the braking index n, together with that of the expected alignment, with the observed values. We performed long-term 3D magneto-thermal simulations, for initial configurations ranging from the standard dipole-dominated case to tangled, small-scale-dominated fields. Small-scale-dominated configurations with relatively weak dipolar components tend to show rich dynamics: the dipolar mode is continuously fed by the small scales and may grow or decay depending on the initial spectrum, driving n<3 or n>3, while the obliquity varies on timescales as short as $ ̧al O $(kyr). These spontaneous changes often dominate the alignment torque, and can account for the large, sign-alternating braking indices observed at characteristic ages τ_c yr, unlike the dipole-dominated cases. Small-scale initial conditions can reproduce the large values of n-3, of either sign, observed at late ages. However, short-term magnetospheric fluctuations or superfluid-driven variations of the torque may still be needed to explain the available measurements and the structured timing residuals quantitatively. Future work comparing the observed timing properties in detail could fine-tune the most promising initial configurations.

title: Signature splitting and inversion in neutron-deficient 117–127 Ba isotopes: a systematic total-Routhian-surface study*
abstract: Abstract Signature splitting in the rotational bands of the odd- N neutron-deficient isotopes 117–127 Ba is investigated systematically. Band crossings and shape evolution are studied using pairing- and deformation-self-consistent Woods-Saxon-Strutinsky calculations within the total-Routhian-surface (TRS) method in the deformation space. Calculated alignments and deformation-dependent Routhians indicate that proton-pair alignment is favored in 117–123 Ba, whereas proton and neutron alignments compete in 125,127 Ba. The signature splitting of the lowest quasineutron Routhians is examined as a function of and γ , both below and above the first band crossing. The observed reduction and occasional inversion of the splitting are interpreted qualitatively in terms of competing γ -driving tendencies of the strongly coupled odd neutron and the aligned proton pair. For the heavier isotopes, the calculations associate large splitting with an aligned, oblate configuration; this association may help explain why only one member of a partner pair has been identified experimentally at high spin.

title: Shadow signatures and near-horizon energy accumulation in coherent quantum sine-integral black holes
abstract: Quantum modifications of black hole spacetimes can lead to observable departures from the predictions of classical general relativity, particularly in the strong-gravity regime near the event horizon. In this context, the coherent quantum black hole model introduces a sine-integral correction to the gravitational potential, characterized by a coherence scale R s , which softens the central singularity and alters the near-horizon geometry. Motivated by the growing precision of black hole imaging and strong-field observations, we explore how these quantum-induced effects influence photon motion and the resulting shadow structure. Considering representative values within the interval R s ∈ [0.5 M , 1.2 M ], we show that the photon sphere shifts inward while the critical impact parameter decreases, reaching values such as b crit ≈ 4.764 M for R s = 0.5 M . Consequently, the shadow radius becomes systematically smaller and develops a more intricate structure than in the Schwarzschild case ( b c r i t = 3 3 M ≈ 5.196 M ). The analysis of the corresponding intensity distributions also reveals a pronounced enhancement of radiation near the shadow boundary, especially for intermediate coherence scales. This feature can be attributed to photons remaining longer within the modified near-horizon region before escaping toward distant observers. Such an increase in brightness may therefore provide a possible observational signature of quantum corrections at horizon scales. Furthermore, although the geometry allows radiation and energy to accumulate around an effective horizon surface, its response to perturbations differs from that expected for compact objects with stable light rings. Instead of contracting under backreaction effects, the accumulation surface shifts outward. These findings suggest that coherent quantum black holes preserve the asymptotic behavior of classical solutions at large distances while introducing potentially detectable imprints in strong-field gravitational lensing and black hole shadow observations.

title: Self-consistent phonon inputs for vibrationally corrected combinatorial nuclear level densities*
abstract: Abstract Phenomenological vibrational prescriptions are widely used in microscopic combinatorial nuclear level-density (NLD) calculations, but they introduce empirical phonon-energy systematics that are not generated by the underlying nuclear-structure model. This empirical input limits the predictive consistency of the model, especially for nuclei for which low-lying collective spectra are unavailable. To reduce this empirical component, we construct self-consistent phonon inputs for vibrationally corrected combinatorial NLDs by calculating the first 2 + , 3 - , and 4 + phonon states with the relativistic quasiparticle random-phase approximation (RQRPA) built on the relativistic Hartree–Bogoliubov ground state. The corresponding RQRPA excitation energies are used in place of the phenomenological phonon energies, while the intrinsic combinatorial density and the established combinatorial vibrational prescription are kept unchanged. The method is benchmarked in selected even-even Sn isotopes against the phenomenological prescription and Oslo-normalized level densities. The RQRPA-based calculation approximately preserves the average vibrational enhancement of the phenomenological prescription and achieves agreement with the Oslo-normalized data comparable to that of the phenomenological calculation. These results demonstrate, for the selected semi-magic Sn isotopes, that self-consistent microscopic phonon energies can serve as collective inputs for vibrationally corrected combinatorial NLDs without using experimental low-lying spectra as model inputs.

title: Schwinger instability for near-extremal charged BTZ black hole
abstract: We study the near-horizon region of a near-extremal charged BTZ black hole, where a controlled AdS 2 × S 1 throat emerges. In this background we solve the Klein–Gordon equation for a charged scalar exactly, identify the BF-bound threshold, and compute the mean Schwinger pair-production rate, which reduces to the standard semiclassical formula in the appropriate limit. The hypergeometric solution is exact within the decoupled near-horizon AdS 2 black-hole patch; with ingoing conditions imposed at the true outer horizon, it yields a closed-form mean number of produced pairs throughout the controlled near-extremal throat regime. Its finite-temperature dependence enters only through the ratio of the mode frequency to the Hawking temperature, while the extremal limit reproduces the known AdS 2 Schwinger result and admits an exact thermal-like form in terms of curvature-corrected effective temperatures. We also compute charged Hawking emission via a WKB tunneling analysis done directly in throat coordinates, allowing a clean comparison between thermal and electric contributions and fixing the instability threshold in terms of an effective Unruh temperature. Finally, we discuss how the stress-energy flux generated by Schwinger production may enter the generalized-entropy extremality condition, while leaving a complete backreaction and quantum-extremal-surface analysis for future work.

title: Probabilistic safety assessment in medical cyclotron facilities
Open quantum battery in the background of a three-dimensional rotating black hole
abstract: We investigate the charging process of an open quantum battery coupled to a scalar field in a three-dimensional rotating black hole spacetime. We evaluate the stored energy, ergotropy, and charging power to quantify the effect of rotation on the charging performance of the quantum battery. Our results demonstrate that when the energy level spacing is smaller than the charging amplitude, rotation enhances the finite-time stored energy and charging power exclusively under the Dirichlet boundary condition; whereas, when the energy level spacing exceeds the charging amplitude, rotation suppresses the energy extracted from the vacuum fluctuations via dissipation, thereby decreasing the charging power. Furthermore, ergotropy analysis reveals that, irrespective of the ratio of the energy level spacing to the charging amplitude, rotation consistently enhances the ergotropy under the Dirichlet condition; under the transparent condition, however, this enhancement occurs only after an initial charging phase. These behaviors originate from the distinct effects of the dephasing and incoherent relaxation rates under different boundary conditions. Our findings advance the understanding of relativistic quantum thermodynamics and provide insights into selecting optimal charging environments within a rotating BTZ black hole background.

title: On modified Hawking radiation under quantum gravity effects in the fermion sector
abstract: In this letter, after briefly discussing Hawking radiation (HR) as quantum tunneling, we emphasize that special care must be taken when computing temperature corrections in the presence of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV), particularly by ensuring consistency between the modified dispersion relation and the gamma matrix structure used to describe fermions that are tunneling. We present a consistent implementation of such corrections in static, spherically symmetric black hole (BH) spacetimes. As the conserved Killing energy ω = p μ ξ μ in a stationary, asymptotically flat spacetime corresponds to the particle’s energy measured by an observer at infinity, one might expect LIV terms that increase (decrease) the energy of a free particle, as defined in the local spacetime frame, to lead to a corresponding increase (decrease) in the Hawking temperature. We discuss the conditions under which this expectation holds. We also determined the changes in Bekenstein-Hawking entropy for Schwarzschild-like BHs, including corrections from LIV scenarios.

title: On entropic cosmology, late-time acceleration and the quantum bounce
abstract: In this work, we present a unified entropic description of the quantum bounce that is present in Loop Quantum Cosmology (LQG) and dark energy that drives the late time acceleration of the Universe. By considering a minimal area $A_0$ for the Universe and a modified entropy area constructed as the sum of $S_Q$, $S_{BH}$ and $S_{DE}$, we derive the Friedmann equations. We show that in the limit $A\sim A_0$, there is a critical density that generates the quantum bounce and depends on the minimal area. Moreover, in the limit $A\gg A_0$ (large Universe) the late time dynamics gives an accelerating scale factor. Therefore, we can argue an entropic origin for the quantum bounce and dark energy.

title: Noncommutative wormholes with generalized uncertainty principle in f(R, T) gravity: Energy conditions and gravitational wave echo time delay
abstract: A central difficulty in the physics of traversable wormholes is the requirement of exotic matter, which arises from the violation of the null energy condition within classical general relativity. This motivates the study of modified gravitational frameworks and quantum-gravitational corrections that collectively reshape the effective stress-energy sector. In this work, we develop a unified construction combining three physically well-motivated ingredients: noncommutative geometry (NCG), the generalized uncertainty principle (GUP), and f ( R, T ) modified gravity with f ( R , T ) = R + 2 λ T . We adopt the matter Lagrangian L m = − ρ and derive the corresponding modified field equations carefully, specifying the explicit form of the effective stress-energy tensor. The NCG Gaussian matter distribution regularises the source profile over a minimal length scale θ and may reduce the amount of exotic matter required near the throat, while the GUP introduces quantum-gravitational corrections to the energy density and pressure at sub-Planckian scales. We perform a complete derivation of the wormhole shape function, writing it as b ( r ) = b N C G ( r ) + b G U P ( r ) , where each contribution is obtained through an explicit integration of the corresponding source term. The throat conditions, flare-out criterion, and asymptotic flatness are verified analytically, and the key limiting cases β → 0, λ → 0, and θ → 0 are checked for consistency. An analysis of the null energy condition shows that the NEC violation is spatially localised near the throat owing to the Gaussian suppression provided by the NCG matter distribution, and the volume integral quantifier is evaluated with the f ( R, T ) coupling included explicitly. The effective potential for axial perturbations is derived and used to compute the gravitational wave echo time delay, which provides potential phenomenological signatures relevant for future gravitational-wave echo searches.

title: Non-perturbative transitions in the island formula: A finite-N resolution of the page curve kink
abstract: The island formula, derived from replica wormhole saddles in the gravitational path integral, successfully reproduces the unitary Page curve for black hole radiation entropy in the large- N (large central charge) limit. However, the resulting entropy profile contains an unphysical sharp kink at the Page time t Page —a mathematical artefact of the min operation that dominates in that limit. Any finite quantum system must exhibit a smooth, analytic transition. In this paper we work within Jackiw–Teitelboim (JT) gravity coupled to a holographic CFT bath and derive systematically the leading finite- N correction to the radiation entropy, S rad ( t , N ) = S Hawk ( t ) + δ S ( N , t ) , δ S ∼ O ( e − S BH ) , originating from non-perturbative interference between the Hawking and replica wormhole saddles. Using a soft-mode resummation of the gravitational path integral we show that these corrections replace the sharp kink with a log-sum-exp interpolation controlled by 1/ N . We further study an interference term arising when both saddles contribute at comparable weight, providing the first analytic description of a smooth cross-over in the island formula. Our predictions are confirmed by a random-unitary-circuit simulation of an n -qubit Page transition and by direct numerical evaluation of the partition function in a matrix-model truncation of JT gravity. The results imply that information begins to leak gradually from the black hole interior long before t Page , consistent with unitarity but without invoking a firewall.

title: Muon pair production in electron-positron collisions close to threshold in the presence of a strong laser field
abstract: Within the framework of strong-field quantum electrodynamics, we study the creation of muon-antimuon pairs in laser-assisted collisions of electrons with positrons, whose center-of-mass energy is close to the threshold of the process. Our focus lies on incident collision energies slightly below the threshold, where the associated energy gap has to be overcome by multiphoton absorption from the applied high-intensity laser field while the collision occurs. We calculate the cross section of the process and discuss its nonperturbative dependencies on the energy gap and the laser parameters. Three qualitatively different interaction regimes are identified, where the influence of the laser field either has a classical or fully quantum nature. In the latter case, an exponential dependence of the cross section on the collision parameters is found, which can be related to Schwinger-like effects.

title: Magnetic dipole moments as probes of doubly-bottom molecular pentaquarks
abstract: Abstract We investigate the magnetic dipole moments of doubly-bottom pentaquark states with spin-parities and , interpreted as hadronic molecules in the , , and configurations. The analysis is conducted within the framework of QCD light-cone sum rules employing photon distribution amplitudes. Our results demonstrate a strong sensitivity of the magnetic dipole moments to the internal spin structure and quark composition of the states. Specifically, the light-quark sector provides the dominant contribution in the configuration, whereas the magnetic moment of is largely governed by the heavy bottom quark. For the molecular state, both light and heavy sectors contribute constructively, leading to a significantly enhanced magnetic dipole moment. These findings indicate that magnetic dipole moments serve as a sensitive probe of the internal structure of molecular-type doubly-bottom pentaquarks and provide testable predictions for future experimental studies.

title: Joule Thomson expansion of κ-deformed Schwarzschild-AdS black hole
abstract: We investigate the Joule-Thomson expansion of a non-commutative Schwarzschild-AdS black hole, whose space-time geometry is described by the Lie-algebraic κ -deformed space-time, and show that the κ -deformation parameter induces Joule-Thomson expansion in an uncharged-AdS black hole. We find the ratio of minimum inversion temperature to critical temperature T i ( m i n ) / T c ≃ 0.493 , is independent of the deformation parameter, and is in close agreement with the value for Reissner-Nordstrom black hole. Furthermore, we show the existence of a minimum black hole mass (depending on the κ -deformation parameter) below which the Joule-Thomson expansion vanishes.

title: Isospin diffusion coefficient for nuclear matter*
abstract: Abstract A systematic evaluation of the isospin diffusion coefficients of symmetric and β -stable nuclear matter in the low-temperature limit is presented within the Abrikosov–Khalatnikov framework. Key microscopic inputs, including the susceptibility, effective mass, and in-medium differential cross sections, are obtained self-consistently within the Brueckner–Hartree–Fock approach using the realistic Av18 potential, with and without a microscopic three-body force. The inclusion of three-body forces suppresses the effective in-medium cross sections and consequently enhances the diffusion coefficient. Compared with the exact Abrikosov–Khalatnikov results, the neutron–proton total cross-section approximation, which retains only the neutron–proton contribution, provides a comparatively robust description, highlighting the dominant role of the neutron–proton channel. Furthermore, the dependence of the diffusion coefficient on the isospin asymmetry β deviates significantly from the quadratic form and exhibits a symmetric double-peaked structure. This behavior arises primarily from the β dependence of mixing effects associated with the effective mass, in-medium scattering, and Fermi-momentum splitting, in addition to the contribution from the susceptibility. These results provide useful microscopic input for transport simulations and constraints on the nuclear symmetry energy.

title: Higher form symmetries of axion electrodynamics in 6-dimension with mass
abstract: We explore the higher form symmetries of 6-dimensional axion electrodynamics with mass in the low energy scale. The Chern-Weil(CW) symmetries derived from the Bianchi identities enrich the topological structure of this theory. Furthermore, the background gauging needs to up to 7-dimension and the gauging procedure leads to the modifications of the gauge transformations, thereby revealing the underlying higher group structure. In the end, we give the ’t Hooft anomalies of these higher form symmetries which obstructed the simultaneous gauging of these symmetries and the physical meanings of these anomalies.

title: Gauge conditions in the perturbative quantization of quadratic gravity and its quantum Lagrangian
abstract: In the perturbative formulation of the Hamiltonian of quadratic gravity, a specific gauge condition is required to hold the equivalence of the Hamiltonian equations of motion with the covariant field equations. Here we give robust evidence that this is an effect of perturbations, the exact nonperturbative equations of both formulations are equivalent, with no need of specific gauge conditions. Despite this, the required gauge condition must be imposed in the perturbative approach. We use it, together with other conditions obtained on very broad grounds, to obtain the quantum Lagrangian resulting from the integration on the canonical variables of the BFV quantization of the theory. This allow us to characterize the quantum modes from the Lagrangian perspective.

title: Entropy quantization and quasi-normal modes of dyonic Kerr-Sen black holes
abstract: We explore the properties of inner and outer horizon thermodynamics of dyonic Kerr-Sen black hole (DKSBH). It is observed that the entropy (or area) product is universal, depending only on the angular momentum of the BH. We then proceed to study the dual conformal field theory (CFT) in the Kerr/CFT correspondence using thermodynamic relations and compute the central charges from 2D CFT. The central charges are found to be universal with only angular momentum dependence. By comparing to Kerr-Newman BH, it is found that the essential difference is in the right-moving sector of the CFT. Interestingly, we can then explicitly produce the non-vanishing central charges related to its static solution, the dyonic dilaton BH, using the thermodynamic method. Moreover, from the CFT relations to multi-horizon thermodynamics, we find the analytical expression of the quasi-normal modes (QNM) spectra in terms of BH parameters. This QNM computation supports the Bekenstein-Hod conjecture on the BH’s entropy quantization.

title: Entanglement inequalities, black holes and the architecture of typical states
abstract: Using the holographic realization of the Araki–Lieb (AL) inequality, we argue that the leading entanglement plateau constrains the organization of typical pure states in a fixed-( E, J ) sector of a large- c two-dimensional holographic CFT. On the field-theory side, its equality structure motivates an effective factorization of the regulated micro-canonical code subspace into ultraviolet (UV), intermediate and infrared factors, with part of the intermediate sector providing a purifier of the ultraviolet one. In the bulk, entanglement-wedge reconstruction realizes the ultraviolet sector as an asymptotic corona, universal to simple probes with length scale smaller than L UV . Crucially, L UV is determined only by the conserved charges. At finite c , universal perturbative dressing correlates these leading factors and lifts the AL plateau at order c 0 . We formulate a generalized ETH ansatz under which O ( e − S < ) fluctuations, with S < = min ( S L , S R ) , account for the O ( c 0 ) deficit of the AL plateau, while the state dependence of matrix elements of individual simple operators smeared over lengths shorter than L UV remains exponentially small. This provides a holographic realization and rotating generalization of the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis: for zero rotation it reduces to the standard O ( e − S / 2 ) . Independently, the separation between L UV and the scale of quantum correlations is of order e − 6 S < / c at large S < .

title: Coherent quantum state corrections in RN–black holes: Photon dynamics, shadow casts, and energy backreaction
abstract: We revisit the Reissner-Nordström (RN) geometry within the coherent quantum black hole framework, introducing a version that remains well-behaved at short distances while preserving the expected classical behavior at large scales. The key ingredient is a smooth Gaussian regularization, which replaces the usual sharp cutoff and suppresses the unphysical oscillations. This construction introduces a characteristic core radius R s , constrained relative to the mass M and charge Q to ensure either a Ricci-regular center or a softened integrable singularity. Near the origin, the spacetime exhibits distinct behaviors depending on the choice of parameters. When R s satisfies the critical relation 𝑅 * s = √ 𝜋 𝑅 2 Q / 𝑅 M , the geometry is Ricci-regulFar, while deviations from this value produce a milder, integrable singularity. We clarify that for generic parameters, the Kretschmann scalar retains a 1/ r divergence even at 𝑅 * s , so the center is not fully regular in the sense of finite curvature invariants. The effective stress-energy tensor can be interpreted as an anisotropic fluid, whose density and pressure smoothly interpolate between the quantum-dominated core and the classical RN region at large radii. The Misner-Sharp mass accumulates gradually from the center, recovering the ADM mass asymptotically. The quantum scale also modifies the horizon structure, giving rise to standard, extremal, or horizonless configurations depending on the ratios 𝛼 = 𝑅 Q / 𝑅 M and 𝛽 = 𝑅 s / 𝑅 M . Photon motion is correspondingly affected: the photon sphere moves inward, light deflection and Shapiro delay are slightly reduced, and the resulting shadow appears more compact and smoother, reflecting the quantum-corrected geometry. These features illustrate how parameter choices control both regularity and observable signatures. Altogether, this work revisits charged black holes with quantum modifications, free from spurious oscillations and offering measurable consequences.

title: Casimir effect for a massive scalar field confined between parallel plates with a spatially varying effective mass
abstract: We investigate the Casimir effect for a massive real scalar field confined between two perfectly reflecting parallel plates in the presence of a position-dependent effective mass, a mechanism for coupling a scalar background to a scalar field. Exact normal modes are obtained by solving the corresponding Klein-Gordon equation, leading to a transverse energy spectrum that exhibits a characteristic Landau-like structure despite the absence of an external magnetic field. Upon quantization of the field, the vacuum energy is evaluated by means of generalized zeta-function regularization together with an appropriate renormalization procedure. The renormalized vacuum energy naturally separates into a Landau-like contribution and an additional term induced by the spatial dependence of the effective mass. We show analytically and numerically that both contributions are exponentially suppressed in the strong-coupling regime. In the opposite limit, the Landau-like contribution smoothly reproduces the standard vacuum energy for a massive scalar field confined between parallel plates, whereas the additional contribution becomes singular owing to the restricted domain of validity of the exact spectrum. Except in the vicinity of this singular limit, the vacuum energy is shown to be dominated by the Landau-like sector. Our results establish a direct connection between position-dependent effective masses and boundary-induced quantum vacuum phenomena, providing a new exactly solvable framework for the investigation of Casimir effects in spatially inhomogeneous relativistic systems.

title: Astrophysical origins of TeV features in the cosmic-ray lepton spectrum*
abstract: Abstract Precise measurements of high-energy cosmic-ray electrons and positrons have revealed spectral features that are difficult to reproduce with a single smooth power-law background. The rising positron fraction measured by PAMELA and AMS-02, together with the all-electron excess reported by ATIC and the high-precision all-electron spectrum measured by DAMPE, has motivated interpretations ranging from nearby astrophysical accelerators to dark-matter annihilation or decay. In this work, we revisit the conventional diffuse electron background and the possible contribution from nearby pulsars within a common propagation framework. The diffuse component is modeled using GALPROP configurations calibrated against cosmic-ray nuclei and diffuse gamma-ray observations. We then use the Green-function solution for nearby discrete sources with radiative losses to study pulsar contributions with both burst-like and continuous injection histories, including the effect of stochastic inverse-Compton cooling on the propagated spectra. We also use the highest-energy DAMPE data points as an illustrative case to compare possible local-source contributions from pulsars and supernova-remnant-like burst sources. The spectral shape of such features provides a useful diagnostic for distinguishing physically plausible nearby-source features from more exotic interpretations.

title: A comprehensive cosmographic and thermodynamic analysis of non-metric-matter coupled gravity
abstract: Abstract The main objective of this manuscript is to explore the viable cosmological bounce solutions in the background of gravity, where Q denotes the non-metricity scalar describing the curvature of spacetime, represents the matter-Lagrangian density, and T is the trace of the energy-momentum tensor. For this purpose, we consider an isotropic and homogeneous universe with bulk viscous fluid to examine the implications of this framework on the dynamics of the early universe. The central focus of this work is to uncover the role of bulk viscosity on the cosmic evolution, especially in non-singular bounces. Furthermore, we investigate the behavior of various cosmological parameters to identify the viable bounce solutions. We find that the positive energy density, negative pressure profile and violation of energy conditions (ECs) support the realization of a cosmological bounce. These results emphasize the importance of bulk viscosity in shaping the cosmic dynamics. We demonstrate that system's entropy evolution satisfies the second law of thermodynamics, confirming its thermodynamic consistency over time. Moreover, the examination of cosmographic parameters and adiabatic sound speed demonstrates the model's kinematic feasibility and stability. Our findings imply that gravity stands as a consistent and alternative theory for standard cosmology, providing a significant theoretical framework to study the gravitational interactions. This modified gravitational theory (MGT) successfully accommodates important aspect of cosmic evolutions and offers a new perspective on geometric and coupling effects that may govern the dynamics of the universe beyond the predictions of general relativity.

title: Probing quantum anomaly corrections on black hole physics through chaos
Primordial black hole interpretation of the subsolar merger event S251112cm
Landauer’s principle as a criterion for thermodynamic consistency in generalized black hole entropies
A collider as a quantum computer
Tuning a rotating black hole spectrum with dark matter halo: quasibound states, scalar cloud, black hole bomb and superradiant scattering
abstract: Abstract We investigate the spectral dynamics of a rotating black hole embedded in a Dehnen dark matter halo, in which quasibound states and superradiant scattering jointly characterize the physical response of the system. Starting from an exact Schwarzschild–Dehnen solution, we construct its rotating counterpart via the Newman–Janis algorithm, thereby obtaining a consistent axisymmetric geometry that incorporates the influence of a structured halo. Through its inner slope parameter γ , the Dehnen profile introduces a controlled deformation of both the near-horizon and asymptotic regions of the spacetime. Using the analytical asymptotic matching method, we derive the quasibound-state spectrum and show that the real part of the frequency retains a hydrogen-like structure but is systematically shifted by the leading-order halo correction proportional to . In particular, denser, more extended, and cuspier halos strengthen the binding of the quasibound states, lower the critical mass required for the onset of instability, and typically suppress the growth rate of the black hole bomb. In the scattering sector, we obtain an analytic expression for the superradiant amplification factor and find that the same halo properties that strengthen the binding effects also tend to narrow the superradiant window. These results demonstrate that quasibound states and superradiant scattering are complementary manifestations of a unified spectral structure, with the Dehnen halo acting as an environmental tuner that directly imprints its properties onto both the resonance spectrum and the energy-extraction channels of the rotating black hole.

title: Tuning of generalized k-omega turbulence model for prediction of heat transfer and pressure drop for helium cooled demo FW
abstract: The HCPB blanket concept for EU-DEMO fusion reactors employs high-pressure (8 MPa) helium gas as coolant for the plasma facing first wall. Up-to-date estimations for the total maximum of heat flux go up to 0.73 MW/m². Higher short-term transient loads are possible. 60°-V-shaped rectangular ribs show high heat transfer and are thus the subject of the presented studies. Long term objectives of the qualification work for numerical simulations for the helium cooled First Wall channels of DEMO are to provide a consistent, fully validated and practically feasible (in terms of computing resources) numerical approach to provide simulations of complete rib enhanced FW channels/ full-size blanket components. The generalized k-omega (GEKO) turbulence model offers higher accuracy predicting heat transfer and pressure drop compared to other types of RANS (Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes) models, even the Reynolds Stress Models (RSM). In this study, the GEKO model is used for simulating predictions for heat transfer and pressure drop. Three short channel segments with 60° V-shape rib configurations with rib heights of 0.4, 0.6 and 0.9 mm are studied at Re = 150,000. High-fidelity LES predictions serve as target data. The effects of the primary GEKO calibration parameters ( C sep , C mix , C nw , C corner ) are investigated. The predicting of Nu number and pressure gradient of the GEKO model is analysed and discussed.

title: Transient behavior analysis of the intermediate-circuit-balanced HCPB fusion power plant
abstract: The HCPB concept of the EU-DEMO fusion power plant uses helium cooling of the reactor, operated in pulsed mode due to inductive current drive. Since conventional Rankine steam cycle power generation does not allow for pulsed operation, the thermal power must be balanced. For this reason, an intermediate circuit with molten salt thermal storage tanks is used. This circuit acts as a thermal buffer and is designed to stabilize the heat input to the steam generators and steam superheaters. In this paper, the transient behavior of the assembly of the primary heat transfer system, the intermediate heat transfer system, and the steam production for the power conversion system (PCS) is analyzed. A specialized system code has been developed to study the transient behavior of such a thermodynamic system.

title: Thermal-hydraulic analysis of the HTS part of the hybrid Central Solenoid designed for the next generation experimental fusion device
abstract: Recently a new design of the CS for the next-generation experimental fusion device has been proposed. The CS system comprises six stacked subcoils, each split into two modules. The inner modules located in the high-field region use a YBCO high-temperature superconductor (HTS), while the outer low-field submodules utilize Nb₃Sn. Each HTS module is composed of 5 hex‑pancakes wound with the identical conductor based on the HTS Conductor-on-Round Core (CORC) strand concept. We performed simulations of normal operation of four selected HTS conductors during the whole CS current scenario, using the THEA code by CryoSoft. We took into account heat loads due to magnetization, coupling and eddy current AC losses. These were estimated based on the evolution of the magnetic field distribution within the CS modules which was obtained from an electromagnetic analysis using the 2D axisymmetric ANSYS Parametric Design Language (APDL) model. The coupling losses and eddy current losses were evaluated using the n τ values dependent on the magnetic flux density, which were computed for the considered conductor geometry with a dedicated electrostatic FEM model. The goal of the study was the estimation of the minimum temperature margin (Δ T marg ) in the considered conductors to verify the potential possibility of safe operation of the HTS modules. For all considered conductors the global minimum of Δ T marg occurred in the first second of the current scenario (when the current and magnetic field were close to the maximum) and it was sufficiently large (above the 1.5 K criterion).

title: Thermal-hydraulic analysis of energy storage and intermediate heat transfer systems for tokamak fusion reactors
abstract: The pursuit of sustainable and clean energy has intensified global interest in nuclear fusion, particularly through tokamak reactors, which are seen as promising candidates for safe and efficient energy generation. A crucial aspect of their development is the study of the Balance of Plant (BoP). It includes all the systems belonging to the main heat transfer chain, devoted to the plasma power removal and to its conversion into electricity. This research involves BoP thermal-hydraulic analyses, focusing on the cooling system behavior, carried out by using RELAP5 system thermal-hydraulic code. Specifically, a study of the Intermediate Heat Transfer System (IHTS) design is proposed, which couples the primary circuit with the Power Conversion System (PCS). This study includes the sizing of the primary and secondary heat exchangers, verified under steady-state conditions within a comprehensive numerical model of the IHTS. Given the pulsed nature of tokamak operation, alternating between plasma pulses and dwell phases, particular attention is given to transient analysis. These transient conditions pose challenges to reactor operations, influencing its efficiency, thermal stability, and safety. For this, the study includes an investigation of thermal storage systems designed to accommodate plasma power variations. The primary goal is to develop a pre-conceptual design for main cooling system components and the evaluation of the BoP response under normal operating conditions. This research allows the understanding of energy transfer and heat management in fusion reactors, contributing to the optimization of tokamak design and operation. These insights and data aim to support the development of tokamak fusion reactors.

title: The Helios cryostat, maintenance schemes, and cryogenic production system
abstract: “Helios”, the Thea Energy, Inc. stellarator fusion power plant described by Swanson (2025), operates cryogenically, in vacuum, and requires repeatable access for scheduled maintenance. This paper outlines the preconceptual design of the Helios cryostat, the cryogenic cooling system, and the considerations made in mechanical design and remote handling to reduce plant downtime during planned maintenance cycles. The represented design state is a major piece of the stellarator system that is presented in whole by this, and its partner papers. A majority of the concepts introduced are not novel to fusion. However, the compilation of these concepts, in a single stellarator, provides novel insight into the design for maintenance and high availability that the planar coil stellarator architecture permits. The presented modular cryostat provides access to inner stellarator components through easily removable and replaceable panel port covers. The plasma vessel is segmented into 24 sections that are sealed and joined with bolted joints to promote ease of maintenance. This method of assembly allows repeatable access to internal components without the need for destructive ingress methods. Remote handling equipment is used to gain access to these components after operation as the surrounding area remains off limits to personnel due to material activation. An 84 day, 88% capacity factor, biennial maintenance cycle is outlined with supporting analysis for decay heat and equivalent dose after Helios shut down. Helios’ cryogenic cooling requirements are broken into three distinct stages; cool down, operational ramp, and power generation. The cool down phase is supplemented with a supply of liquid nitrogen for the higher power requirements. Total designed cooling power is 1 MW at 80 K and 50 kW at 20 K.

title: Performance evaluation of CAD-to-MCNP conversion tools in complex fusion systems: A case study of VUV diagnostics in JT-60SA
abstract: The accurate conversion of CAD models into MCNP geometry is fundamental to the design and development of nuclear fusion facilities such as ITER, DEMO, JT-60SA, and IFMIF-DONES, where radiation transport simulations play a critical role. As system geometries grow increasingly complex, advanced computational tools are essential for generating reliable MCNP models. This study evaluates the performance of the GEOUNED code and RadModeling tools for CAD-to-MCNP conversion. The CAD model of the Vacuum Ultra Violet (VUV) spectrometer, developed to monitor the divertor region of JT-60SA, diagnostic system for JT-60SA has been simplified and processed using these tools. The validity of the resulting MCNP model has been confirmed through stochastic volume calculations and benchmarked against results obtained using the SuperMC code. Preliminary nuclear response simulations, including neutron and proton fluxes, total dose, total heating, and neutron flux difference (%), have been performed for the integrated JT-60SA model with VUV diagnostic, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed conversion workflow.

title: Overview of the helios design: A practical planar coil stellarator fusion power plant
abstract: Thea Energy, Inc. has developed the preconceptual design for “Helios,” a fusion power plant based on the planar coil stellarator architecture. In this overview paper, the design is summarized and the reader is referred to the papers in this special issue for more detail. The Helios design is based around a two-field-period quasi-axisymmetric (“QA”) stellarator equilibrium with aspect ratio 4.5 and a novel tokamak-like X-point divertor. The natural stability, low recirculating power, and steady-state capability of the stellarator are leveraged. Stability and transport are calculated using state-of-the-art, high-fidelity codes and grounded in measured performance of existing experiments. The electromagnetic coil set is high-temperature superconducting (“HTS”) and consists of 12 large, plasma-encircling coils like the toroidal field coils of a tokamak, and 324 smaller, field-shaping coils. All coils are planar and convex. A maximum of 20 T on-coil is enforced, a value which has been achieved in existing large-bore HTS coils. There is a minimum of 1.2 m between plasma and coils, leaving space for tritium breeding blanket and neutron shielding. Because of this thick shielding, all coils have a minimum 40-year operational lifetime, the same minimum lifetime of the overall power plant system. 1.1 GW of thermal power and 390 MW of net electric power are produced. The shaping coils are individually controllable, enabling a uniquely configurable magnetic field for relaxed manufacturing and assembly tolerances as well as plasma control in the presence of bootstrap current. A practical maintenance architecture is a primary driver of the design; maintenance is performed on entire toroidal sectors that are removed from between the encircling coils. A biennial maintenance cycle is estimated to take approximately 84 days, resulting in an 88% capacity factor. In all systems, rigorous engineering constraints such as temperature and stress limits are enforced.

title: Optical diagnostic design for measuring the radiation front with a mid-leg pumped divertor on DIII-D
abstract: The design of an optical diagnostic system to localize the radiation front in a mid-leg pumped divertor configuration on DIII-D is presented. Divertor detachment is a key mechanism for handling power exhaust in tokamaks, and mid-leg pumping offers a promising approach to radiatively dissipate power while maintaining acceptable core performance. To predict the location of the radiation front and design a spectroscopic diagnostic to measure its position, a database of SOLPS-ITER simulations across a range of input powers and gas puffing rates representative of DIII-D operation was employed. These simulations provide self-consistent plasma backgrounds for a Cherab-Raysect synthetic diagnostic framework, which incorporates detailed tokamak geometry and physically accurate ray-tracing. Synthetic simulations of optical sightlines and viewing cone geometry were used to calculate line-integrated emission from the plasma, particularly of the C III 465 nm line, to serve as a proxy for the Te ≈ 7-10$ eV temperature region associated with the onset and evolution of divertor detachment. Neutral deuterium emission is also evaluated for comparison. The synthetic diagnostic is used to assess the performance of existing DIII-D optical systems, including filterscopes and the Multichord Divertor Spectrometer, and to optimize line-of-sight placement within mechanical and installation constraints. The results provide quantitative guidance for diagnostic implementation on DIII-D and demonstrate the advantage of integrated synthetic diagnostics for divertor design studies and future advanced divertor concepts.

title: Integrated workflow for DEMO divertor design using Reduced Order Models
abstract: EU-DEMO (European Demonstration Fusion Power Plant) is considered the successor to the experimental fusion reactor ITER (”The Way”). EU-DEMO will have to operate under significantly more demanding conditions, reaching the energy production of an industrial-scale plant, producing energy continuously. This case study examines the EU-DEMO divertor, a critical component of nuclear fusion reactors and one of the most significant engineering challenges to be addressed. The divertor has to handle extremely high heat fluxes, due to the discharge of exhausted ion particles, and it is subjected to intense neutron fluxes, while providing shielding to the vacuum vessel and the vacuum pumping system in order to reduce plasma contamination. The development of such a complex component requires the integration of multi-physics analysis, such as plasma or computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, which are more computationally expensive, with EM/FEM analysis, which are generally less time-consuming. A BPMN-based (Business Process Model and Notation) model was developed to comprehensively map the multi-disciplinary phases of the divertor design process. This work highlights the differences in terms of time consumption among various simulation approaches, suggesting the exploration of alternative methodologies. This paper investigates the feasibility of integrating a pre-existing high-fidelity database of plasma physics simulations into the modeFRONTIER software, as a case study, to evaluate the capability of predicting the heat flux on divertor targets through mathematical models, thereby accelerating the assessment of different scenarios and reducing computational time and resources.

title: Influence of tritium aging and helium-3 content on fracture resistance in austenitic stainless steel GTA welds and heat-affected zones
abstract: The mechanical performance of primary containment material is critical for tritium handling, processing, and storage, which are enabling capabilities for fusion energy. Austenitic stainless steels display significant resistance to hydrogen embrittlement, although they are not completely immune. Tritium further exacerbates degradation with the additional effect of its helium-3 decay product. Helium-3 is not soluble in the lattice so generates a distribution of high-pressure nanoscale helium bubbles, further reducing mechanical performance and fracture resistance. Welds and heat affected zones (HAZ) are an area of concern due to their potential for defects, residual stress, and altered microstructures. In this work, 304 L and 21Cr-6Ni-9Mn (referred to as 21-6-9) austenitic stainless-steel forgings were gas tungsten arc welded with 308 L filler metal. Notched bend specimens were machined and precracked in a manner to extend the crack into the weld fusion or heat affected zones. Bend specimens were exposed to tritium at elevated temperature and pressure followed by aging to allow significant helium-3 to develop. Specimens were aged different times and then fracture tested. Crack growth resistance curves were developed and compared to understand the effect of built-in helium. Notably, the HAZ of 21-6-9 material displays a larger decrease in fracture resistance compared to their weld fusion zones and to the HAZ or fusion zones of 304 L steel specimens tested at the same conditions. The 304 L fusion zone exhibited lower fracture resistance than the 21-6-9 fusion zone upon tritium charging and aging. In addition, fracture surfaces were examined of the welds and HAZ to elucidate the trends in the fracture behavior.

title: Fluid dynamics simulations of gas retention systems for shattered pellet injectors
abstract: The HUN-REN Centre for Energy Research’s Fusion Plasma Physics Laboratory team is developing a shattered-pellet injector (SPI) system for plasma disruption mitigation of the ITER experiment. A high-pressure valve accelerates the cryogenic protium and neon pellets to speeds of a few hundred metres per second before they hit the shattering head. For effective disruption mitigation, it is necessary that the propellant gas does not reach the plasma before the solid particles. The propellant retention system, or gas suppressor, requires numerical analysis to determine its efficiency. This paper discusses the modelling constraints and difficulties of Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations of such systems. It addresses the difficulty of continuum modelling, shock capturing, and the selection of numerical methods using commercially available ANSYS Fluent software. The simulations take advantage of overset mesh approaches, as well as adaptive meshing, to accurately model the expansion of high-pressure gas into vacuum and high-vacuum environments. The study presents different modelling approaches and analyses the effect of different simulation parameters. It also offers a brief comparison of measurement data with the simulation results for different configurations of the SPI suppressor system. The results serve as a basis for the development of an effective gas retention system to be used at the ITER experiment and potentially in other more exotic uses.

title: FEM-based plasma equilibrium reconstruction for transient and off-normal phases in KSTAR
abstract: In this study, we developed a finite element method (FEM)-based equilibrium reconstruction code for the KSTAR tokamak to analyze plasma behavior during highly transient phases, including early startup, pre-disruption, and vertical displacement events (VDEs), where conventional equilibrium fitting (EFIT) reconstructions often fail to converge. The code minimizes a weighted least-squares cost function fitting magnetic diagnostic signals, with the currents induced in the vacuum vessel and passive structures fitted simultaneously with the plasma current rather than prescribed through a separate eddy current circuit model. Validation against EFIT for stable limited and diverted discharges yielded plasma position agreement to within 20–40 mm, a level consistent with the intrinsic uncertainty of EFIT-based reconstruction during the current ramp-up and plasma shaping phase. Applied to the early startup phase, cross-validation with fast-frame camera imaging confirmed the code's ability to capture initial plasma breakdown well before EFIT becomes available. The reconstruction was further extended through the VDE and current quench phases, with the results cross-validated against halo current monitors, deuterium-alpha emission, and diamagnetic flux measurements, confirming the physical consistency of the reconstructed plasma evolution throughout the event. These results demonstrate the capability of the FEM-based reconstruction code to reliably track plasma behavior across a wide range of transient operational phases, and the framework can serve as a valuable tool for analyzing transient plasma phases in future tokamak devices.

title: Evaluated nuclear data for the optimum cyclotron production of 169Yb
Development of a flow distributor for the actively pumped open-surface lithium loop
abstract: A distributor, producing uniform flow, has been designed, manufactured, and installed onto the Actively Pumped Open-surface Lithium LOop (APOLLO) at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign (UIUC). The anisotropic features of the distributor were determined using a two-step approach utilizing topology optimization routines in COMSOL Multiphysics and the Turing reaction-diffusion system equations. The distributor was then additively manufactured from 316 stainless steel and installed onto the APOLLO Plasma Facing Component (PFC). Good distribution was achieved during experimentation with a variation of 6% – 9% in velocity measured across the distributor outlets. With a flat PFC plate, full wetting was not achieved as flow rivulets were observed on the plate. The inclusion of a 3D mesh structure on the flow plate was shown to promote spreading due to capillary action and complete lithium wetting and coverage of the PFC was achieved.

title: Design trends and challenges in fusion reactor Remote Handling Systems
abstract: Fusion energy is a compact, clean, and safe power source that is advancing through demonstration-plant development and industry-scale investment. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the historical development and current State-of-the-Art (SOTA) of robotic systems for maintenance, inspection, and handling of in-vessel components. Robotics are critical to fusion plant productivity because they directly influence maintenance duration and overall plant availability. Key technical challenges in the design, deployment, and operation of these systems, including high radiation, extreme temperatures, limited access, and contamination, are identified and analyzed. Engineering solutions to these challenges are systematically categorized, and enabling technologies and practices from adjacent industries are examined for relevance to fusion-specific constraints. By surveying historical development, task-based SOTA systems, and emerging approaches, this review consolidates current knowledge and provides a foundation for future research and development in fusion robotics.

title: Application of the RCC-MRx entrance key to the structural design of HCCP TBM-set components
abstract: The Test Blanket Module (TBM) installed in the ITER device must satisfy fusion-specific thermo-mechanical requirements as well as European and French nuclear regulatory constraints, since it operates within a French nuclear installation under high-temperature and high-radiation conditions. A clear and consistent application of design codes and regulations at an early design stage is therefore essential to ensure regulatory compliance and design consistency. This study applies the RCC-MRx Entrance Key methodology to the structural design of the Helium-Cooled Ceramic Pebble (HCCP) TBM-set, focusing on the TBM-box and the TBM-shield as functionally distinct components. Their functional roles, structural characteristics, and system boundary definitions are examined, and component-specific Entrance Keys are defined by integrating RCC-MRx criteria with regulatory applicability under the Pressure Equipment Directive (PED) and the French regulation for nuclear pressure equipment (ESPN). Based on the defined Entrance Keys, the applicable RCC-MRx design subsections are identified, and the implications for structural design, fabrication, inspection, and qualification are discussed. The results demonstrate that the Entrance Key provides a practical framework for aligning design code application with regulatory requirements for fusion blanket components.

title: A statistical study on as-built deviation of ITER blanket shield block interfaces
abstract: The blanket shield block (SB) is a key component of ITER blanket system, providing critical interfaces for the attachment of the first wall (FW) and assembly within the vacuum vessel (VV). To ensure assembly feasibility which is first assembled on VV in ITER site, the SBs are manufactured with a dimensional (size) tolerance of ±1 mm on the external surfaces, while critical features directly interfacing with mating components require position of 0.2 mm, and flatness of 0.02 mm specified using Geometrical Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T). In addition, key components of ITER are manufactured by multiple domestic agencies (DAs) and procured independently, accurate as-built dimensional information is essential for assembly preparation. In this study, dimensional (size) tolerance and geometrical tolerances of 54 inboard SBs manufactured in KODA were statistically analyzed against the applied size and GD&T requirements using descriptive statistics, considering measurement uncertainties associated with three-dimensional coordinate measuring machines (3D-CMMs). Based on the statistical analysis using normalization of manufacturing deviation and process capability index with centering, key interfaces area of SBs requiring process improvement were identified. These results provide quantitative insight into SB manufacturing accuracy and support the prevention and diagnosis of potential integration issues during ITER tokamak assembly. In addition, the resulting as-built dimensional database could support on-site assembly by providing accurate geometric information to facilitate local fit-up or minor machining of the SB and mating components.

title: Study of the reaction*
abstract: Abstract We study the isospin-violating reaction, recently measured by the BESIII collaboration, by considering the dominant terms involving and pairs of pseudoscalar-baryon particles that together form an SU (3) singlet and can therefore couple to the . We then allow these pairs to undergo final-state interaction to produce the final . We find that the relevant original channels are and , and that the incomplete cancellation of terms involving charged and neutral particles, owing to their different masses, is responsible for the reaction. With this mechanism, we find good agreement with the three experimental mass distributions.

title: Searching for ultralight dark matter with Mössbauer resonance*
abstract: Abstract We investigate the feasibility of probing interactions between ultralight scalar dark matter and atomic nuclei using stationary Mössbauer spectroscopy. The exceptional energy resolution of the Mössbauer resonance enables searches for minute nuclear energy shifts induced by the local dark matter field. The dark matter mass range considered in this work is – . We present projected constraints for two candidate Mössbauer isotopes, and , with providing the strongest sensitivity. For , projected sensitivities of approximately , , and can be achieved for the scalar DM–photon, DM–gluon, and DM–quark couplings , , and , respectively. In the low-mass region, the projected sensitivity to the scalar DM–photon coupling approaches current constraints from equivalence-principle (EP) tests. These results demonstrate that Mössbauer-based techniques provide a promising and competitive approach to probing ultralight dark matter interactions with Standard Model particles.

Topological signatures in Kerr-Sen AdS black hole thermodynamics
abstract: Abstract Black hole thermodynamics and topology have emerged as a robust foundation for a coordinate-independent understanding of phase transitions. Using both Duan’s topological current theory and a novel complex residue method, we conduct a topological study of the Kerr-Sen AdS black hole arising in heterotic string theory. Specifically, we identify the zero points corresponding to on-shell black hole states and calculate their winding numbers to determine the global topological charge by constructing the generalized off-shell free energy and examining the corresponding vector field in a parametric space. Our analysis reveals that the Kerr-Sen AdS black hole exhibits three distinct thermodynamic phases—small, intermediate, and large black hole branches—characterized by critical points with winding numbers , , and , respectively, culminating in a total topological charge . Significantly, this topological number remains invariant under variations of the dilaton charge parameter, indicating that the dilaton field does not alter the fundamental topological class established for Kerr-AdS and RN-AdS black holes. However, the rotation parameter proves crucial in determining the phase structure and the emergence of multiple critical points. We systematically examine three limiting configurations: the full Kerr-Sen AdS spacetime, the GMGHS AdS limit ( ), and the asymptotically flat Kerr-Sen case ( ). The GMGHS AdS black hole yields a vanishing total topological charge, with winding numbers and canceling each other, while the Kerr-Sen black hole ( ) similarly exhibits despite possessing two distinct phase branches. Furthermore, we propose a novel approach by analytically continuing the thermodynamic characterization to the complex plane. The resulting complex function, derived from the off-shell Gibbs free energy, possesses isolated singular points whose residues directly encode the winding numbers. Our results indicate that topology offers profound insights into black hole phase transitions, with potential implications for understanding holographic dualities.

title: Rational orbits and gravitational waves in static spherical spacetimes: an open-source numerical framework*
abstract: Abstract Timelike orbits constitute a crucial probe for exploring the intrinsic properties of curved spacetimes, and the accompanying gravitational radiation signals provide a direct window into strong field gravity. In this paper, we develop a versatile computational framework based on Mathematica and the OpenMP parallel architecture to simulate the rational orbits of timelike particles and their gravitational radiation in static spherically symmetric spacetimes. Specifically, with only the user defined covariant metric as input, this numerical tool can efficiently calculate rational orbits for various configurations, as well as the corresponding gravitational wave polarization states and characteristic strains. The package presented here provides an efficient and comprehensive tool for investigating the properties of curved spacetimes and their potential observational signatures. To demonstrate the reliability and capability of our code, we apply it to the Schwarzschild spacetime as a test case, illustrating its functionality in several key aspects, including the effective potential, stable orbital regions, rational and irrational orbits, and gravitational wave signals. Furthermore, we show that the gravitational waves emitted by an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral system composed of an intermediate mass black hole and the Galactic Center supermassive black hole could be detected by future space detectors.

title: Polarization modes of gravitational waves in general symmetric teleparallel gravity*
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the polarization modes of gravitational waves within the most general symmetric teleparallel gravity theory that allows for second-order field equations. We consider scenarios where test particles either carry or do not carry a hypermomentum charge. Our findings reveal the existence of tensor, vector, and scalar modes of gravitational waves. First, the theory supports the + and × tensor modes propagating at the speed of light. Second, in the case where particles do not carry hypermomentum, vector modes propagating at the speed of light exist only within a very specific parameter space. However, when particles do carry hypermomentum, there are two shear modes that propagate at the speed of light, while the vector- x and vector- y modes emerge only under very specific conditions. Third, in the presence of hypermomentum, there is always a longitudinal mode propagating at the speed of light. The universal existence of the shear modes and the longitudinal mode in the presence of hypermomentum is a key feature of symmetric teleparallel gravity, distinguishing it from the Riemannian framework through gravitational wave polarization detection. We also analyze the polarization modes in two widely studied special theories: f ( Q ) theory and quadratic non-metricity theory.

title: Photon spheres and shadows of black holes with modified entropy-inspired metrics*
abstract: Abstract Starting from the first law of black hole thermodynamics, we establish an explicit correspondence between the corrected entropy and the metric function under the condition of fixed black hole energy and horizon location. Using the corrected metric, we then compute the photon sphere radius and shadow size, demonstrating that different entropy corrections produce characteristic optical shifts. By comparing these results with Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*, we constrain the parameter range associated with the corrected entropy. This analysis provides a feasible approach for testing generalized entropy frameworks and probing deviations from the Bekenstein--Hawking area law.

title: Photon regions, shadow observables and constraints from M87* of a Kerr-Newman-like black hole in Bumblebee gravity surrounded by plasma*
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the photon regions, shadow, and observational constraints of a Kerr-Newman-like black hole in Bumblebee gravity within a plasma medium. Using a specific non-homogeneous power-law plasma model to ensure the separability of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, we derive the null geodesic equations, analyze the photon regions, and construct the black hole shadow. Furthermore, we introduce two sets of shadow observables to systematically analyze the distinct effects of each physical parameter (spin a , charge , Lorentz-violating parameter ℓ , and plasma parameter k ) on the shadow geometry. Specifically, we find that a and ℓ mainly enhance the distortion of the shadow, whereas and k primarily lead to radial shrinkage. In addition, a brief evaluation of the energy emission rate shows that increasing these parameters generally suppresses the emission peak. Finally, by modeling M87* as a charged, rotating black hole in Bumblebee gravity surrounded by plasma, we constrain the physical parameters using observations from the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT). For a fixed viewing angle of , the angular diameter narrows the viable parameter space, while the circularity deviation and axis ratio satisfy the EHT limits. This suggests that the charged, rotating black hole in Bumblebee gravity surrounded by plasma may be a candidate for real astrophysical black holes.

title: Observational constraints on fractional holographic dark energy in the light of DESI DR2*
abstract: Abstract Based on the fractional entropy from fractional quantum mechanics, fractional holographic dark energy (FHDE) has been proposed with the Hubble horizon as the IR cutoff (FHDEH). We extend this framework by adopting the future event horizon and the particle horizon as the IR cutoff and proposing the FHDEF and FHDEP models. Using the SN+OHD+DESI DR2 dataset to constrain these models, we find that all three models provide a marginally lower compared to ΛCDM but without significant preference according to AIC and BIC. When CMB distance priors are included, the FHDEH and FHDEP models are strongly ruled out. We further analyze the cosmological evolution for these models, and find that only the FHDEF model predicts nearly identical evolutions of and to those of the ΛCDM model across cosmic history, but its deceleration parameter q deviates from the ΛCDM model in the future, indicating richer late time dynamics beyond the standard ΛCDM cosmology.

title: Observable thin accretion disk around a self-dual black hole in loop quantum gravity*
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we study a self-dual black hole (BH) in loop quantum gravity (LQG) by analyzing both timelike and null geodesics. Using observational data from Mercury’s perihelion shift and the orbit of the S2 star around Sagittarius A * (Sgr A * ), we derive constraints on the polymeric function P . We also investigate photon trajectories near the self-dual BH under various scenarios to assess their observational relevance. Finally, we examine the properties of accretion disks around the self-dual BH in LQG, including their direct and secondary images. We further study the redshift and observed energy-flux distribution across the accretion disk, as measured by distant observers at different inclination angles. Our findings provide new insights into the physical nature and accretion properties of self-dual BHs in LQG and their possible observational consequences.

title: Frequencies spectra and gravitational ringing around Hayward-AdS black holes immersed in a string fluid*
abstract: Abstract We investigate the dynamics of test particles in a Hayward–AdS black hole with string fluid, with particular emphasis on how the relevant parameters influence particle motion. The stability of circular orbits is studied using the effective potential method, which yields analytic expressions for the particle energy and angular momentum in terms of the black hole parameters. The effects of these parameters on the innermost stable circular orbit and the effective force are also examined. In addition, we calculate the pericenter precession frequency and investigate the small oscillatory motion of a particle around a stable orbit, examining how the corresponding frequency is modified by the black hole parameters. We further compare particle dynamics in the Hayward–AdS spacetime with string fluid to those in the Hayward–AdS, the Hayward Reissner Nordstrom, and the conventional Hayward black holes. Lastly, we examine the influence of the string fluid and the Hayward parameter on the quasinormal spectrum and the time-domain dynamics of electromagnetic perturbations, and find that these two terms have reciprocal effects on the quasinormal scale.
